hackathons.how: OWASP London ran a hackathon and CTF in the City; current hackathon calendars were not confirmed.

airsoft.how: Indoor airsoft runs at Ultimate Airsoft in Whitechapel and Bunker 51 in Charlton; outdoor sites exist in Surrey.

paintball.how: Paintball parks near the M25 such as AA Paintzone (Whyteleafe) and Campaign Paintball (Cobham) take walk-in groups.

arcade-games.how: Arcade bars such as Four Quarters and London Games Room (Shoreditch, London Bridge) offer retro arcade cabinets.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Bowling lanes are available at Lane7 Victoria and Gravity Wandsworth.

vr-gaming.how: VR arenas and booths include Sandbox VR in Holborn and DNA VR in Camden, Battersea and Hammersmith.

escape-rooms.how: Escape Hunt runs escape rooms at its Oxford Street venue, and other operators exist across London.

esports-gaming.how: Esports venues such as Meltdown (Caledonian Road) and Platform (Shoreditch) host competitive gaming.

parkour.how: Parkour Generations runs parkour classes across London including a beginner course.

birdwatching.how: London Wetland Centre in Barnes has wildlife sightings and runs birding events such as an Urban Birder course.

science-museum.how: The Science Museum in South Kensington has free admission (pre-booked ticket) and galleries such as Wonderlab, Space and Flight.

museums.how: Free national museums such as the Science Museum in South Kensington are open to visitors daily.

art-gallery.how: Tate Modern offers free entry to its collection displays on Bankside.

stamp-collecting.how: The Royal Philatelic Society London, based at 15 Abchurch Lane, welcomes stamp collectors and postal historians as members.

coin-collecting.how: The British Numismatic Society holds regular talks and gatherings; its London meeting place was not confirmed on its page.

ancient-ruins-excavation.how: The Thames Discovery Programme, run by MOLA, involves volunteers in recording archaeology on the Thames foreshore; this is survey and monitoring rather than a full dig.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Battersea offers kennel and cattery support roles and fostering volunteers at its London centre.

community-gardening.how: Spitalfields City Farm runs a volunteer programme with a dedicated growing section.

meetups.how: Meetup lists a large Games and Hobbies directory of groups in London.

chess.how: Meetup's London listing includes chess clubs and groups.

board-games.how: Meetup's London listing includes board game groups.

contract-bridge.how: Meetup's London listing includes bridge clubs and groups.

hot-spring-bathing.how: No natural hot springs exist in the London basin; the nearest, Thermae Bath Spa in Bath, is roughly 2 hours away by train.

safari.how: No free-roaming African safari exists near London; the nearest drive-through safari is Woburn Safari Park in Bedfordshire, about 1 hour by car.

yoga.how: Free Bryant Park Yoga classes run on Tuesday mornings and Wednesday evenings through summer (registration on Eventbrite; bring your own mat), alongside thousands of paid studio classes citywide.

stamp-collecting.how: The Collectors Club of New York (philatelic society and library) hosts philatelic talks, a single-frame exhibit competition, Philatelic Foundation workshops open to anyone, and swap days at its Midtown clubhouse.

toastmasters.how: Numerous Toastmasters clubs meet around the city, e.g. Bryant Park Toastmasters, Astoria Toastmasters and Columbia University Toastmasters, listed on Meetup.

language-exchange.how: Many Meetup language-exchange groups hold regular in-person sessions, e.g. Langroops NYC Language Exchange, the NYC Spanish/English Intercambio and the Polyglot Language Meetup.

knitting-crochet.how: Regular knit and crochet meetups include NYC Knitters, the New York City Crochet Guild, Knitting Around New York and NYC Pints 'n' Purls.

urban-sketching.how: Meetup groups such as Weekend Urban Sketch and the Central Park Sketching & Art Meetup Group run outdoor sketching outings around the city (e.g. sketching the streets of Chinatown).

go-weiqi.how: Gotham Go Group holds weekly Tuesday evening Go sessions at pinkFROG cafe in Williamsburg.

tai-chi.how: Meetup groups including The New York Chen Tai Chi Chuan Meetup Group and Taiji Form & Qigong Manhattan hold regular tai chi sessions.

qigong.how: Qigong NYC and Taiji Form & Qigong Manhattan run regular qigong sessions through Meetup.

trail-running.how: Groups such as Palisades Running Club (Joseph Clarke Trail runs) and Staten Island Hiking Meetup organise trail outings on nearby trail networks.

poker.how: Many weekly Meetup poker clubs run live low-stakes Hold'em games, e.g. New York Poker Club, Williamsburg Poker Club and Poker Night Out NYC.

game-development-jams.how: GameMaker Meetup Group and IGDA-linked events plus NJ Game Developers host game dev meetups and playtests; dedicated jam events are occasional.

stargazing.how: The Amateur Astronomers Association hosts free public telescope sessions one Friday night a month from May to October on the esplanade at Carl Schurz Park, with other pop-up sessions around the city.

rc-aircraft.how: The Pennsylvania Avenue Radio Control Society has flown model aircraft for decades from the north end of Floyd Bennett Field and runs an annual Big Apple Jet Rally.
rc-aircraft.venue: Pennsylvania Avenue Radio Control Society (Floyd Bennett Field)

keelboat-yachting.how: North Cove Sailing teaches keelboat courses (Sailing 101 leading to US Sailing Basic Keelboat certification) on Colgate 26 keelboats from Brookfield Place; Hudson River Community Sailing and SailTime New York also offer lessons.

kitesurfing.how: New York Kiteboarding School gives IKO-certified lessons at Breezy Point, Seagate, Rockaway Beach and Oak Beach, wind and weather permitting.

high-ropes-course.how: Alley Pond Adventure Course in Queens has a high ropes course with zip line and climbing elements, with free family programs on Sundays by lottery; Adventures at Governors Island and Area 53 in Brooklyn have further ropes and climbing courses.

zip-lining.how: Short zip lines operate at Adventures at Governors Island (Flywire Zipline, sometimes closed for maintenance), Sky Chaser at Luna Park in Coney Island and indoors at Area 53 in Brooklyn; longer canopy tours are 1 hour or more outside the city.

paintball.how: An indoor paintball venue was reported in Long Island City (2010 article) and Area 53 in Brooklyn is listed in directories; large outdoor fields such as Liberty Paintball in Patterson are about an hour from the city.

indoor-skydiving.how: iFLY Yonkers operates a vertical wind tunnel with first-time flyer sessions, about 30 minutes north of Manhattan.

watchmaking-horology.how: The Horological Society of New York has taught horology to the public since the 1940s through its NYC education programme and lists watchmaking schools and programs.

watch-collecting.how: The Horological Society of New York has met monthly since 1866 for lectures and social events open to watch enthusiasts, ticketed via Eventbrite.

ikebana.how: Ikebana Flowers New York (1133 Broadway) runs beginner and advanced ikebana classes (Nageire, Moribana, Jun Fusion), also bookable on CourseHorse and Classbento.

kintsugi.how: Yuko Gunji teaches 90-minute kintsugi ceramic repair workshops in Manhattan (epoxy method, materials provided), listed by Flatiron NoMad.

bagpipes.how: An 8-session Introduction to the Highland Bagpipes course is listed on CourseHorse in Manhattan, and Manhattan University's Pipes and Drums recruits beginners with weekly practices.

blacksmithing.how: Brandr Forge in East Flatbush teaches basic and advanced blacksmithing classes and bladesmithing, and Craftsman Ave runs knifesmithing workshops, both listed on CourseHorse.

chinese-calligraphy.how: Celestial Calligraphy offers drop-in calligraphy workshops in Midtown, Flushing Library has hosted weekly Chinese calligraphy series, and New York Zendo has run eight-week courses.

kathak.how: Kathak Legacy Project holds an annual summer immersion at New York Live Arts, and Leela NY offers kathak workshops and classes.

candle-making.how: Candle-making classes run at studios such as Nose Best, Classpop! in Brooklyn and Back Porch Soap Company on the Upper West Side, listed on CourseHorse.

mixology.how: J. Bespoke is the NYC-addressed provider of cocktail-making classes listed on CourseHorse (mostly virtual, with kits delivered); in-person bartending and cocktail classes also run at bars and schools but were not confirmed.

whisky-tasting.how: Kings County Distillery in Brooklyn runs whiskey tasting classes and Astor Center, Whisky Gourmet and Craftsman Ave offer whisky classes and barrel-aging workshops.

wine-tasting-wset.how: Wine tasting classes run at Astor Center, the Institute of Culinary Education and NYC Wine Company; WSET-accredited certification itself was not confirmed on the listing.

cheese-making.how: Murray's Cheese on Bleecker Street runs 90-minute mozzarella and burrata making classes with wine, and CocuSocial offers a fresh mozzarella class.

butchery.how: Dickson's Farmstand Meats (Chelsea Market) runs whole-hog and beef butchery classes, with further courses at Fleishers Craft Butchery and The Brooklyn Kitchen.

stone-carving.how: New York School of the Arts offers a beginner stone carving course (Tuesday afternoons; students bring their own stone) and other stone carving classes are listed on CourseHorse.
stone-carving.venue: New York School of the Arts

animation-2d.how: Noble Desktop and Manhattan Edit Workshop run After Effects and motion-graphics animation courses; dedicated hand-drawn 2D animation classes were not listed.

korean-language.how: ABC Languages gives private and group Korean lessons and COEI (West 32nd Street, Koreatown) runs conversational Korean courses.

french-language.how: French Institute Alliance Francaise (East 60th Street) runs French courses from beginner to B2 advanced, with further group courses at ABC Languages.

german-language.how: ABC Languages (26 Broadway) runs an 8-session in-person German course for total beginners plus private lessons.

sign-language.how: American Sign Language levels 1-6 are taught at Sign Language Center in Manhattan, ASL NYC in Brooklyn, Brooklyn Brainery and community colleges (ASL rather than a local sign language).

pilates.how: Power Pilates (Third Avenue) teaches mat Pilates teacher-training courses and many studios run drop-in Pilates classes; New York Fencing Academy in Brooklyn lists a Pilates conditioning class.

breakdancing.how: Peridance Capezio Center runs beginner Street Styles hip hop classes covering popping, locking and breaking.

coffee-roasting.how: Joe Coffee (Long Island City) has run an Explorations in Roasting class and Stumptown a Coffee Roasting class, alongside barista and cupping classes.

pedal-boating.how: Pedal boats rent by the hour on Meadow Lake in Flushing Meadows Corona Park and at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside on Prospect Park Lake.

lacrosse.how: Volo Sports runs adult recreational lacrosse leagues (men's, women's and coed) and drop-in pickup games across the New York metro area.

netball.how: Manhattan International Netball Club trains weekly (Monday and Thursday) on the Upper East Side and fields teams in Netball America's national league.

australian-rules-football.how: The New York Magpies, a men's and women's club in the Eastern Australian Football League, play home games at Tibbetts Brook Park in Yonkers.

lawn-bowls.how: Central Park has two lawn bowling and croquet greens north of Sheep Meadow, home to the New York Lawn Bowling Club since 1926; visitors need a Parks Department permit and bring their own bowls.

horse-polo.how: MeadowBrook Polo Club on Long Island offers a four-week introductory polo course with group lessons, about 20 miles from Manhattan; NYC Polo Club in Patterson runs adult leagues.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: Rat Rock and other schist boulders in Central Park offer free legal outdoor bouldering, while the Shawangunks (the Gunks) are a roughly 90-mile drive for roped climbing.

parkour.how: 92NY on the Upper East Side runs adult parkour classes (90-minute beginner sessions) as well as youth classes, and Brooklyn Zoo NY and NY Parkour Academy (East River Park) offer further training.

harp.how: Irish Arts Center and City Music Schools list Celtic harp classes, and teachers such as Anna Lien and Kirsten Agresta Copely give private pedal and lever harp lessons in Brooklyn and Manhattan.

wargaming-warhammer.how: The Games Workshop Warhammer store at 55 East 8th Street has free-use gaming tables, and The Compleat Strategist in Midtown East hosts weekly wargaming and roleplaying nights.

temple-activities.how: The Hindu Temple Society's Sri Maha Vallabha Ganapati Devasthanam in Flushing is open daily with pujas, festivals such as Navaratri, in-person yoga and meditation, a patasala and volunteering.
temple-activities.venue: Sri Maha Vallabha Ganapati Devasthanam (Ganesh Temple)

moocs.how: Coursera and similar platforms offer online courses from universities with free audit access, usable from anywhere in the city.

onsen.how: Spa Castle in College Point, Queens is a large Korean bathhouse (jimjilbang) with hot pools, saunas, and shiatsu and other massage services.

massage.how: Spa Castle in College Point offers shiatsu and other massage by the hour, among many massage studios across the city.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Animal Care Centers of NYC runs a volunteer programme at its Manhattan, Queens and Staten Island shelters (dog walking, cat socialising, enrichment), with orientations and a six-hour-per-month commitment.

coastal-cleanup.how: NYC Parks, the Jamaica Bay-Rockaway Parks Conservancy and Surfrider NYC host volunteer shoreline cleanups at Rockaway Beach, with gloves and bags supplied.

community-gardening.how: NYC Parks GreenThumb supports more than 550 community gardens that welcome volunteers, with free public workdays and no experience needed.

urban-exploration.how: Meetup groups such as 5 BORO Exploration and New York Adventure Club run urban walks and explorations of city sites; access to abandoned sites is not formally organised.

silat.how: A silat-focused community martial arts session ran at the Brooklyn Pride Center, and a Chinatown school lists a Silat and Southeast Asian martial arts curriculum.

intertidal-walking.how: NYC Urban Park Rangers lead free guided tide-pool and shore-exploration walks at Orchard Beach and other city shorelines.

drone-flying.how: Drone and model-aircraft flying is possible at club-run fields such as Calvert Vaux Park in Brooklyn (AMA membership needed), while flying in most city parks needs a permit.

control-line-aeromodelling.how: Control-line fliers in the NYC area use club fields; Garden State Circle Burners in Lincoln Park NJ ran a learn-to-fly program (dated source).

ski-simulator.how: NRTHRN Strong in Flatiron offers machine-based indoor cross-country ski training, and the Big SNOW indoor slope at American Dream (NJ) is about 30 minutes from Midtown.

snow-sculpture.how: Snow sculpture is seasonal at best; Governors Island Arts has run an ice sculpture show open to artists with no carving experience, pairing them with Okamoto Studio carvers.
snow-sculpture.venue: Governors Island Arts ice sculpture show

meteorite-hunting.how: Hunting needs arid strewn fields where dark stones stand out; the best areas are Arizona's Franconia and Gold Basin fields and other US Southwest deserts, about 5 hours by air.

big-wall-climbing.how: No big walls in the metro area; the Shawangunks (Gunks) cliffs, about 2 hours north, offer multi-pitch trad climbing, and true big walls need Yosemite or similar.

bobsled.how: No bobsled track in the metro area; the Olympic track at Lake Placid is about 5 hours north and sells tourist rides.

buzkashi.how: Central Asian horseback game needing a steppe horse culture; not played in the metro area.

camel-racing.how: Needs a camel-racing culture and tracks (Gulf states, Australia); none in the metro area.

cheese-rolling.how: Tied to a single hill in Gloucestershire, England; no equivalent event in the metro area.

elephant-polo.how: Needs working elephants (Nepal, Thailand, India); none in the metro area.

ski-jumping.how: No jumping hill in the metro area; the Olympic jumping complex at Lake Placid is about 5 hours north.

capoeira.how: ABADA-Capoeira runs adult and kids classes in a Midtown studio; Capoeira Angola classes also run in Manhattan.

drone-racing.how: The Drone Racing League is headquartered in NYC but is a pro circuit; a pay-per-race indoor venue (DroneRush) was listed, with current status unconfirmed.

ultimate-frisbee.how: DiscNY lists pickup games in Prospect, McCarren, Central and Riverside parks; Manhattan Ultimate Disc runs leagues with a recreational tier for beginners.

dragon-boat.how: Club crews train for the annual Hong Kong Dragon Boat Festival, raced on Meadow Lake in Flushing Meadows Corona Park with festival-supplied boats and paddles.
dragon-boat.venue: Hong Kong Dragon Boat Festival, Meadow Lake

urban-foraging.how: Naturalist Steve Brill leads paid foraging walks in Prospect Park and Central Park covering edible and medicinal wild plants.

mushroom-foraging.how: A 3-hour guided Prospect Park foraging walk covers edible and medicinal plants and mushrooms; a dedicated fungi walk listing exists but may be unavailable.

outrigger-canoe.how: New York Outrigger runs free novice sessions for outrigger canoeing from the Pier 96 boathouse on the Hudson (age 14+).

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: New York Outrigger offers free novice stand-up paddleboarding sessions from Pier 96, and Perfect Paddles runs paid SUP lessons in Brooklyn Bridge Park.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Circus Warehouse in Long Island City teaches flying and static trapeze and aerial classes; Trapeze School New York and Circus Academy New York also offer silks.

improv-comedy.how: The Peoples Improv Theater runs improv classes including weekend drop-in sessions.

ballet.how: Peridance Capezio Center teaches ballet and other dance at all levels in open classes.

irish-dance.how: The Irish Arts Center offers Irish dance classes alongside fiddle, harp and bodhran instruction.

orchestra.how: The Chelsea Symphony is a Manhattan community orchestra with a play-with-us page for musicians.

guitar.how: Greenwich House Music School gives guitar lessons for all levels, from first-timers up.

piano.how: Greenwich House Music School gives piano lessons for all levels, from first-timers up.

pole-dance.how: Body & Pole teaches pole classes from first-timers to professionals, with first-class offers for new students.

salsa-bachata.how: Drop-in salsa and bachata classes with socials run at Latin dance studios across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

sitar.how: Chhandayan Center for Indian Music in Midtown Manhattan lists group sitar and tabla classes.

stand-up-comedy.how: Beginner stand-up courses of about six weeks end in a graduation show at a Manhattan comedy club.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Lindy hop series for beginners run at the 92nd Street Y and Chelsea studios, with no partner needed.

tabla.how: Chhandayan runs small-group tabla classes (10 students or fewer) for all ages and levels with an annual recital.

taiko.how: Soh Daiko, founded 1979 at the New York Buddhist Church, runs public taiko workshops and recruits members; Taikoza offers paid classes.

tap-dance.how: Beginner and adult tap classes are widely offered at Manhattan dance studios.

chinese-opera.how: Chinese (Peking) opera is performed by local societies such as the New York Chinese Opera Society and Yeh Yu; regular public classes are not clearly listed.

batik-painting.how: Textile Arts Center in Brooklyn lists a batik one-day intensive on its workshop calendar.

embroidery.how: Textile Arts Center in Brooklyn lists embroidery and bead embroidery workshops.

etching.how: Manhattan Graphics Center has practitioners in intaglio (including etching), relief, lithography and screenprint and runs classes.

lithography.how: Manhattan Graphics Center teaches lithography alongside intaglio, relief and screenprinting.

printmaking-screenprint.how: Manhattan Graphics Center offers screenprinting among its printmaking classes.

film-photography-darkroom.how: International Center of Photography runs courses through Open Education and has darkrooms and media labs; film and alternative processes are taught.

filmmaking.how: New York Film Academy offers filmmaking programmes and short-term workshops of 1 to 15 weeks.

glassblowing.how: UrbanGlass in Brooklyn runs Intro to Glassblowing and Glassblowing 101 classes for beginners.

lampworking.how: UrbanGlass lists Flameworking and Beadmaking classes such as Hot Torch Basics Bootcamp for beginners.

laser-cutting.how: NYC Resistor's shared space in downtown Brooklyn lists a laser cutter for members.

robotics-arduino.how: NYC Resistor hosts electronics classes (e.g. KiCad circuit board design) and members' maker projects.

origami.how: OrigamiUSA runs monthly Folding Sundays meetings and special sessions at the American Museum of Natural History.

3d-printing.how: Fat Cat Fab Lab, a volunteer-run makerspace in the West Village, offers 3D printing and a 3D Printing 101 class.

cnc-machining.how: Fat Cat Fab Lab has CNC routing with a members-only CNC safety class.

oil-painting.how: The Art Students League of New York offers painting classes at all levels on West 57th Street.
oil-painting.venue: Art Students League of New York

charcoal-life-drawing.how: The Art Students League of New York runs drawing classes, and life drawing is its long-standing core offering.
charcoal-life-drawing.venue: Art Students League of New York

clay-sculpture.how: The Art Students League of New York offers sculpture classes.
clay-sculpture.venue: Art Students League of New York

watercolour-painting.how: Brooklyn Brainery runs watercolor classes such as Watercolor Fundamentals and Watercolor Landscapes.

chocolate-making.how: Raaka Chocolate makes bean-to-bar chocolate in Red Hook and runs a 3.5 to 4 hour bean-to-bar class on weekends.

beekeeping-honey.how: NYC Beekeeping, a volunteer group, runs a Saturday Series hands-on course, mentoring, newcomer events and community honey harvests.

cosplay.how: New York Comic Con at the Javits Center holds cosplay competitions such as the Crown Championships of Cosplay.

vr-gaming.how: Sandbox VR lists a New York City location for group VR gaming.

pub-trivia.how: Sporcle Live runs pub trivia events with a Find a Game location finder; NYC bars host weekly quiz nights.

dim-sum-making.how: Hands-on dim sum and dumpling classes run at Chelsea Market (Buddakan) and ICE, with CocuSocial offering cheaper dumpling sessions.
dim-sum-making.venue: Buddakan dim sum class, Chelsea Market

sushi-making.how: Beginner sushi-rolling classes run by Taste Buds Kitchen, CocuSocial and others; ingredients and tools are supplied.

sake-tasting.how: Brooklyn Kura's Sake Studies Center runs guided sake tasting classes with a brewery tour, plus a taproom.

sake-making.how: Brooklyn Kura brews sake in Industry City and its classes include a brewery tour; hands-on brewing is limited to the tour and courses.

tea-ceremony.how: Beginner chanoyu (Japanese tea ceremony) classes are taught at Resobox in the East Village.

latte-art.how: Partners Coffee and other roasters teach barista and free-pour latte art classes for beginners.

sourdough-baking.how: NY Cake Academy teaches a two-hour sourdough class covering starter, kneading and baking.

whisky-society.how: The Scotch Malt Whisky Society hosts recurring guided tastings in Midtown Manhattan, and Drammers Whisky Club began as a NYC group.
whisky-society.venue: Scotch Malt Whisky Society NYC tastings

hawker-crawling.how: Guided and self-guided street-food crawls cover the food courts and stalls of Flushing's Chinatown, reached by the 7 train.

butterfly-watching.how: The AMNH Butterfly Conservatory houses hundreds of live butterflies, and Central Park's North Meadow butterfly gardens attract wild species in summer.

comic-collecting.how: Midtown Comics, Forbidden Planet and JHU Comic Books sell new and back-issue comics across Manhattan.

trading-cards.how: Chameleon Comics & Cards in the Financial District sells trading cards, and many comic and game shops host card-game play.

rock-fossil-collecting.how: NYC Parks rangers lead fossil walks at Wolfe's Pond Park on Staten Island, and hobbyists report fossil finds on Staten Island beaches.
rock-fossil-collecting.venue: Wolfe's Pond Park fossil exploration (NYC Parks)

sneaker-collecting.how: Flight Club on Broadway buys, consigns and sells rare and vintage sneakers.

train-spotting.how: The New York Transit Museum shows vintage subway cars in a retired station, runs Nostalgia Rides on vintage trains and a Grand Central gallery.

whale-watching.how: Gotham Whale runs whale and dolphin watching trips from Riis Landing in Rockaway, mostly humpbacks, May to November.

archival-research.how: The NYC Municipal Archives has public research rooms open by appointment.

genealogy.how: The Municipal Archives' 'Research Your Family History' programme points to its vital records collection, with research-room access.

creative-writing.how: Gotham Writers Workshop (now writingclasses.com) runs creative-writing classes in New York; the site refused automated access.

poetry-slam.how: The Nuyorican Poets Cafe runs the Bowery Slam, Final Friday Slam and weekly open mics at off-site venues during renovation.

history-walks.how: Big Onion Walking Tours has run guided two-hour history walks of about 20 neighbourhoods since 1991.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The Museum of Chinese in America in Chinatown shows exhibitions and runs calligraphy workshops, screenings and performances.

wartime-history.how: The Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum is a WWII-era aircraft carrier museum on the Hudson.

public-lectures.how: 92NY on the Upper East Side hosts public lectures and talks; the site returned no text to the fetcher.

philosophy-cafe.how: The NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community meetup runs reading and discussion sessions such as Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit.
philosophy-cafe.venue: NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community

meetups.how: Meetup lists hundreds of NYC hobby groups, such as sketching, piano, songwriting and board games.

book-club.how: The Meetup NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community reads set texts weekly, and many other reading groups are listed.
book-club.venue: NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community

running-club.how: New York Road Runners organises races and group runs in Central Park; the page sat behind a queue at fetch time.

volunteering.how: New York Cares lists over 1,000 volunteer opportunities in tutoring, food, gardening and more.

support-groups.how: NAMI-NYC Metro runs peer support groups led by trained volunteers with lived experience.

meditation.how: New York Insight Meditation Center runs sittings and classes in Manhattan.

pet-adoption.how: Animal Care Centers of NYC run adoption centres in all five boroughs.

indoor-snow-play.how: Big SNOW at American Dream offers real-snow tubing and snow play year-round, just over the river in New Jersey.

snow-skiing.how: Big SNOW at American Dream offers year-round indoor skiing and snowboarding with lessons, and real mountains need a 2-3 hour drive.

rodeo.how: PBR bull riding comes to Madison Square Garden each January as a one-off event, with no regular local rodeo.
rodeo.venue: Madison Square Garden (PBR Buck Off at the Garden)

outdoor-skydiving.how: No drop zone operates in the dense metro area; Skydive Long Island at Shirley is about 55 miles east, roughly 1.5 hours by car.

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is not practised in the US; the nearest legal bullrings are in Mexico or Spain, a flight away.

canyoning.how: No suitable gorges exist in the metro area; the nearest canyoning is in the Adirondacks or Appalachians, several hours away.

cave-diving.how: The area has no flooded caves; the nearest cave diving is in Florida, a flight away.

dog-sledding.how: No snow-reliable terrain exists locally; the nearest dog sledding is in the Adirondacks, several hours away.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers exist nearby; the nearest are in Alaska, Canada or Iceland.

luge.how: There is no luge track nearby; the nearest is the Olympic track at Lake Placid, about 5 hours north.

volcano-boarding.how: No volcanoes exist in the region; the activity is offered at Cerro Negro in Nicaragua.

sandboarding-desert.how: No desert exists locally; real sandboarding and desert trekking means the US Southwest or beyond, a flight away.

white-water-rafting.how: No whitewater exists in the metro area; the nearest rafting is on the Delaware or Lehigh rivers, roughly 2 hours away.

mountaineering.how: No alpine terrain exists locally; the nearest mountaineering is in the Adirondacks, about 4-5 hours north.

cave-exploring.how: No natural caves exist in the metro area; the nearest show caves such as Howe Caverns are about 2.5 hours north.

ancient-ruins-excavation.how: No ancient ruins exist in the region; excavation field schools are abroad in the Mediterranean or Latin America.

base-jumping.how: BASE jumping from city structures is illegal; the legal organised event is Bridge Day in West Virginia, about 7 hours away.

hiking.how: NYC Parks lists marked hiking trails (Staten Island Greenbelt, Van Cortlandt, Pelham Bay) and runs guided hikes with Urban Park Rangers.

rowing.how: Row New York offers free beginner rowing lessons at Paerdegat Basin, and Sebago Canoe Club hosts community open houses with rowing outings on Jamaica Bay.
rowing.venue: Row New York / Paerdegat Basin Community Dock

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Ring-making and silversmithing classes run at Ayaka Nishi Jewelry Design School and other studios listed on CourseHorse; tools and materials are supplied.

birdwatching.how: Central Park's Ramble and Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge are major birding sites, with NYC Bird Alliance guiding birders to sites across the five boroughs.
birdwatching.venue: Central Park Ramble / Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge

dinghy-sailing.how: Riverdale Yacht Club (Bronx) has taught sailing on Optimist, Laser and 420 dinghies; Hudson River Community Sailing and Atlantic Yachting teach small-boat and keelboat sailing on the Hudson.

sailing.how: Offshore Sailing School runs lessons from North Cove Marina in Battery Park, and Hudson River Community Sailing offers beginner classes from its boathouse.

geocaching.how: Geocaching.com lists active caches in NYC parks such as Cunningham Park.

mountain-biking.how: Cunningham Park in Queens has about 6.5 miles of graded mountain-bike trails built and maintained by the CLIMB volunteer group.

scuba-diving.how: PADI Open Water courses with a Manhattan pool run at Scuba Network and Scuba.com New York, and Captain Mike's Diving Services on City Island is a 5-star PADI facility.

bharatanatyam.how: Aalokam NY teaches Bharatanatyam to adults and children in Manhattan and Brooklyn with a free trial class; Dakshina Palli also teaches in Midtown.

dj-turntablism.how: Scratch DJ Academy (Cooper Square), Dubspot and Garnish Music Production School teach DJing and turntablism in small classes.

music-production.how: Garnish Music Production School and Dubspot run Ableton Live, Logic Pro and mixing courses with 4-student classes.

bookbinding.how: Brooklyn Craft Company runs a beginner Bookbinding 101 class (long-stitch journal) and Manifesto in Gowanus offers bookbinding workshops.

leatherwork.how: Leatherworking workshops to make wallets and cases run at Brooklyn studios listed on CourseHorse, including Manifesto in Gowanus.

tango.how: NY Tango School holds weekly beginner group classes and a milonga practice; no partner or experience required.

chinese-orchestra.how: The Chinese Music Ensemble of New York (founded 1961) is a Chinese orchestra with concerts and lessons; Columbia Chinese Orchestra is a student group.
chinese-orchestra.venue: Chinese Music Ensemble of New York

erhu.how: The Chinese Music Ensemble of New York lists private lessons including erhu.
erhu.venue: Chinese Music Ensemble of New York

guzheng.how: China Institute in Lower Manhattan launched guqin, erhu and guzheng classes; private teachers also advertise in NYC.

gamelan.how: Gamelan Kusuma Laras (Javanese) and Gamelan Dharma Swara (Balinese) are community ensembles based at the Indonesian Consulate in Manhattan.

lion-dance.how: Troupes such as New York United Lion and Dragon Dance Troupe practise in Sara D. Roosevelt Park, and W.O.W. Project and NY Choy Lay Fut run lion dance teams in Chinatown.

fishing.how: Catch-and-release fishing is allowed at Central Park's Harlem Meer (NY State licence needed for ages 16+), with Central Park Conservancy fishing programs and bamboo-pole loans when running.

freshwater-fishing.how: Harlem Meer in Central Park holds largemouth bass, sunfish, carp and chain pickerel and is open to catch-and-release angling.

board-games.how: Board game cafes such as Hex & Co. (500+ games, walk-in cover charge), The Uncommons and The Brooklyn Strategist let visitors play from large libraries.

esports-gaming.how: Waypoint on the Lower East Side is a gaming cafe with 30 PCs for titles such as League of Legends and Fortnite.

curling.how: CurlNYC and Brooklyn Lakeside Curling Club run learn-to-curl sessions and leagues on Prospect Park's ice; Long Island Curling Club curls at Syosset.

vinyl-records.how: Dozens of independent record stores including Academy Records, Rough Trade NYC, Generation Records and Brooklyn Record Exchange sell new and used vinyl.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: CocuSocial, Red Inside Culinary and Murray's Cheese run hands-on fresh pasta classes in Manhattan.

artisan-bread-baking.how: NY Cake Academy offers a Bread Making Certificate Series and focaccia classes.

dog-parks.how: NYC has fenced dog runs (Tompkins Square, Chelsea Waterside, Carl Schurz Park) and park areas that allow off-leash dogs before 9am and after 9pm.

flamenco.how: Ballet Hispanico School of Dance offers adult flamenco classes open to all levels, and Flamenco Vivo Carlota Santana runs classes at its Center for Flamenco Arts.

safari.how: No free-roaming wildlife safari exists in the metro area; the nearest drive-through safari is Six Flags Great Adventure in Jackson, New Jersey, about 1.5 hours away, and the Bronx Zoo only has enclosed exhibits.

hot-spring-bathing.how: There are no natural geothermal springs in the New York metro area; the nearest are in Berkeley Springs, West Virginia, roughly 5 hours away (Korean spas such as Spa Castle in Queens use heated pools instead).

hunting.how: Firearm discharge and hunting are banned in the five boroughs; the nearest deer hunting is on Long Island's east end and in the Hudson Valley, roughly 1.5-2 hours away.

hang-gliding.how: The metro area has no launch ridges; the nearest hang gliding is at Ellenville in the Shawangunks, about 2 hours away, or Kitty Hawk Kites' tow operation in New Jersey.

sup-yoga.how: Manhattan Kayak Company runs SUP yoga classes and A-Team Paddleboarding in Rockaway Park offers yoga on paddleboards.

disc-golf.how: Highland Park Disc Golf Course, a 10-hole permanent course opened in 2024 on the Brooklyn/Queens border, was built by the NYC Disc Golf Association with NYC Parks.

choir.how: Everybody Sing New York is a free no-audition weekly community choir on the Upper West Side, and Washington Heights Community Choir is a no-audition adult chorus.

museums.how: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, MoMA, the Guggenheim and many others are open daily to visitors.

art-gallery.how: MoMA and the Guggenheim show modern and contemporary art, and Chelsea has a dense cluster of free commercial galleries.

hackathons.how: Tech Week's NYC calendar lists hackathons across Manhattan and Brooklyn each June, alongside university-hosted events at NYU and Columbia.

amateur-radio.how: The ARRL club directory lists Queens clubs offering entry-level licence classes and test sessions, including Hall of Science Amateur Radio Club and ARC Emergency Communications Service.
amateur-radio.venue: Hall of Science Amateur Radio Club

ctf-security.how: Anarcho-Tech NYC runs a beginner-friendly CTF team and NYU's Cybersecurity Club holds weekly HackNights and CTF101 sessions.

coding-meetups.how: OWASP New York City holds open application-security meetups, and many developer meetups and NYU/Columbia tech clubs run regular events.

acting.how: HB Studio in Greenwich Village teaches acting classes, one of many conservatories and studios offering adult courses.

nature-guided-walks.how: NYC Parks Urban Park Rangers and partner groups lead free guided hikes and nature walks through the city's parks.

escape-rooms.how: The Escape Game NYC in Midtown and many other operators run one-hour themed escape rooms.

archery.how: Indoor archery ranges with intro classes, lane rentals and leagues operate in Gowanus and the Lower East Side; NYC Parks rangers also run free archery on Staten Island.

bmx.how: The city's Harold Ickes Playground skate and BMX park in Red Hook opened in 2024; BMX-specific programming is limited.

bouldering.how: VITAL and Brooklyn Boulders run indoor bouldering gyms with day passes and shoe rental.

cricket.how: Cricket is widely played on park pitches such as Van Cortlandt Park by the NYC Cricket League and community clubs; cricket became a varsity sport in city schools in 2008.

fencing.how: Tim Morehouse Fencing Club, Manhattan Fencing Center and New Amsterdam Fencing Academy run adult beginner classes with loaner gear.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: New York GAA, founded 1914, fields hurling and Gaelic football teams that play at Gaelic Park in the Bronx.

horse-riding.how: Riding lessons and trail rides are available at Brooklyn and Bronx stables such as Kensington Stables beside Prospect Park.

ice-hockey.how: Chelsea Piers Sky Rink runs year-round adult leagues and learn-to-play classes, and Central Park's Davis Center has an adult league.

ice-skating.how: Public skating is offered at Central Park's Wollman Rink, Bryant Park, Rockefeller Center and Chelsea Piers, with skate rental.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Central Rock Gym on the Upper West Side and Brooklyn gyms offer top rope, auto-belay and lead climbing with rentals.
rock-climbing-top-rope.venue: Central Rock Gym Upper West Side

judo.how: Judo is taught in dojos such as Hoteikan Dojo in Bay Ridge and Staten Island Judo Jujitsu Dojo.

padel.how: Padel Haus runs indoor padel courts in Brooklyn and Replay offers padel and pickleball.

pickleball.how: CityPickle runs pay-to-play pickleball courts at Wollman Rink in Central Park, and indoor venues such as Replay exist.

rugby.how: Several amateur rugby union clubs play around the city, listed at nycrugby.com.

skateboarding.how: Free public skateparks include Pier 62, LES Skatepark under the Manhattan Bridge, Astoria Skate Plaza and Red Hook.

snowboarding.how: Big SNOW American Dream in East Rutherford, NJ, is an indoor real-snow slope with lesson programs; outdoor resorts are 1.5-2.5 hours away.

taekwondo.how: Taekwondo schools such as Ahns' Taekwondo NYC and West Side Taekwondo offer adult and kids classes.

allotment-gardening.how: GreenThumb supports hundreds of community gardens across the five boroughs where residents can join and garden plots.

camping.how: Camping is possible at Floyd Bennett Field in Brooklyn (permit based) and at nearby state and county campgrounds.

hydroponics-urban-farming.how: Brooklyn Grange operates soil-based rooftop farms in Queens and the Brooklyn Navy Yard with farm visits and events.

kayaking.how: Downtown Boathouse offers free walk-up kayaking on the Hudson at Pier 26 from May to October.

surfing-ocean.how: Ocean surfing with lessons and board rental is available at Rockaway Beach in Queens, reached by subway or ferry.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Mangroves do not grow in the New York climate; the nearest guided mangrove kayaking is in Florida, about a 2.5 hour flight.

macrame.how: The New York Sewing Center teaches macrame alongside knitting and needlepoint classes.

perfumery.how: Bios Apothecary runs a natural perfume workshop where participants take home a 15ml bottle; Back Porch Soap Company also lists custom perfume classes.

photography.how: The School at ICP runs open-enrolment photography courses and workshops for all skill levels.
photography.venue: International Center of Photography (The School at ICP)

pottery-handbuilding.how: Greenwich House Pottery teaches handbuilding to all levels at its Jones Street and Chelsea studios.

pottery-wheel.how: Greenwich House Pottery offers wheel-throwing classes for first-timers upward; Pottery NYC also runs wheel courses.

rug-tufting.how: Craftsman Ave in Industry City runs tufting wall-art and rug classes using a tufting gun; other studios list punch-needle and tufting workshops.

stained-glass.how: UrbanGlass in Fort Greene offers stained glass suncatcher, projects and sampler classes.

weaving.how: CourseHorse lists multiple weaving classes in NYC, including Saori weaving, though the operating studio was not confirmed.

woodworking.how: Craftsman Ave teaches beginner woodworking, including a two-day side-table build, in a professional shop.

hackerspace-electronics.how: NYC Resistor in downtown Brooklyn is a long-running member hackerspace with workshops such as KiCad PCB design; Hack Manhattan holds open houses on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

chess.how: Marshall Chess Club in Greenwich Village offers adult classes, instruction and tournaments; casual chess also runs in Washington Square Park.

contract-bridge.how: Honors Bridge Club in Manhattan is a long-established duplicate bridge club (founded 1993).

arcade-games.how: Barcade operates classic-arcade bars in Chelsea, FiDi, St. Marks Place and Brooklyn.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Twenty Sided Store hosts weekly beginner-friendly D&D sessions with materials provided.

trading-card-games.how: Twenty Sided Store runs Magic: The Gathering events and prereleases.

mahjong.how: New mahjong social clubs and pop-up game nights have multiplied across the city.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Brooklyn Bowl is a bowling alley and music venue with lane rentals and a restaurant.

homebrewing-beer.how: Brooklyn Brew Shop sells beer-making kits and mixes and hard-cider kits for apartment homebrewing.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Brooklyn Brew Shop sells kombucha kits, fermented hot sauce kits and fermentation supplies for home use.

science-museum.how: The New York Hall of Science in Queens is a hands-on science museum.

japanese-language.how: Japan Society's Language Center teaches Japanese across 13 levels in 10- and 5-week sessions.

spanish-language.how: Instituto Cervantes New York runs Spanish courses in person and online.

heritage-trails.how: Municipal Art Society runs guided historic and architectural walking tours of neighbourhoods such as SoHo, Grand Central and Bed-Stuy.

sauna.how: The Russian & Turkish Baths in the East Village have a redwood sauna, Russian and Turkish rooms.

cold-plunge.how: The Russian & Turkish Baths list an ice-cold pool alongside the sauna.

lacrosse.how: Atlanta Lacrosse League runs adult leagues alongside youth programs at Sandy Springs fields such as Hammond Park.

tap-dance.how: Atlanta Ballet offers drop-in adult tap classes for all ability levels at its Buckhead and other studios.
tap-dance.venue: Atlanta Ballet Centre for Dance Education

bookbinding.how: Occasional bookbinding workshops are held at venues such as Scraplanta in Tucker and Piedmont Park Community Center, but no permanent course was confirmed.

ikebana.how: Ichiyo Ikebana of Atlanta teaches classes in Old Fourth Ward and Ikebana International Atlanta Chapter 265 and Atlanta Botanical Garden also run workshops.

urban-sketching.how: A local architect-artist led an urban sketching outing in Little Five Points listed by Midtown Atlanta; no standing chapter page was found.
urban-sketching.venue: Urban sketching outing at Variety Playhouse

paintball.how: Wildfire Paintball in Snellville runs an indoor speedball and hyperball arena with rentals; outdoor fields operate in Roswell/Alpharetta, Conyers and Acworth.

go-weiqi.how: The Atlanta Go Club held tournaments with Chinese and Korean community groups at Oriental Chess in Duluth in 2012; current activity was not confirmed.

game-development-jams.how: Georgia State University's Creative Media Industries Institute hosts an annual Global Game Jam site in downtown Atlanta open to anyone 18 or older, with PCs and Unity/Unreal provided.

dj-turntablism.how: ScratchOutLoud is an Atlanta all-vinyl DJ school offering lessons and workshops for a range of skill levels.

orchestra.how: The Atlanta Community Symphony Orchestra and the volunteer Atlanta Philharmonic Orchestra rehearse weekly for non-professional players.

kathak.how: Aparna's Dance Academy has taught Kathak, Bollywood and Indian folk dance in metro Atlanta since 2000 and stages an annual Kathak showcase at Georgia Tech's Ferst Center.

magic.how: IBM Ring 9 (Georgia Magic Club) is an 85-year-old chapter of the International Brotherhood of Magicians with about 90 members, alongside a local Society of American Magicians chapter.

poker.how: Meetup groups such as Posh Poker Group (Texas Hold'em at Mazzy's in Milton and Roswell) and The Four Suit Poker League run freeroll social poker in the Atlanta area.

korean-language.how: The Atlanta Korean Language Meetup Group runs weekly Saturday Korean-English language exchange sessions for all levels.

book-club.how: Dozens of Meetup book clubs meet across the metro, including Books by the Beltline, Atlanta Nonfiction Book Club and Decatur Women's Book Club.
book-club.venue: Books by the Beltline Book Club

debate.how: District 213 Toastmasters clubs (Village Speakers, Clarkston Community, Northwords) hold public-speaking meetings listed on Meetup; competitive debate leagues were not confirmed.

community-gardening.how: Volunteer mornings at the Food4Lives Community Garden recur on Sundays, listed through the Atlanta Vegetarian & Vegan Meetup group.

support-groups.how: Many peer support groups meet in the metro, such as Decatur Grief Walks, Alpharetta Prostate Cancer Support Group and ASCA-Atlanta.

mentoring.how: Ladies That UX Atlanta hosts speed-mentoring sessions and Toastmasters clubs provide peer mentoring; no dedicated youth-mentoring programme was confirmed.

parkour.how: Atlanta Parkour runs coach-led fundamentals to advanced classes, open gym and a family class for ages 7 to 60, and LEAP Parkour teaches mobile classes around the metro.

hot-air-ballooning.how: Balloon Atlanta in Woodstock flies passenger rides year-round across the metro, and tethered balloon rides run at Piedmont Park's Balloon Glow.

airsoft.how: Atlanta Airsoft Inc operates a 15,000 sq ft indoor field with a retail store, and Georgia Paintball & Airsoft offers open play and scenario games.

cheese-making.how: Occasional hands-on cheesemaking classes have been run in Atlanta, for example by Oli+Ve and Cultured South (vegan cashew cheese); no permanent course was confirmed.

australian-rules-football.how: The Atlanta Kookaburras, founded in 1998, field men's and women's teams in the United States Australian Football League.

billiards-snooker.how: Pool halls such as Red Fox Billiards Club, Morgan Falls Billiards and Mr Cue's Billiards II host league play (APA/TAP) and table rentals across the metro.

horse-polo.how: Atlanta Regional Polo Center runs matches and a polo school at Vinings from May to October and a Tyrone arena from November to April.

netball.how: Netball America ran a free youth netball programme at Redan Recreation Center in Lithonia (DeKalb County) in 2021 and 2023; no adult league was confirmed.
netball.venue: Netball America at Redan Recreation Center

onsen.how: Jeju Sauna & Spa in Duluth is a 24-hour Korean-style bathhouse with mineral baths and themed saunas, and Gangnam Sauna operates a similar bathhouse in Atlanta.

treetop-walk.how: The Atlanta Botanical Garden's Kendeda Canopy Walk is a 600-foot skywalk reaching into the treetops of the garden's woodland.

moocs.how: Georgia Tech Professional Education, based in Atlanta, offers online courses and MOOCs through Georgia Tech Online, and the online format is open to any resident.

rodeo.how: Spectator rodeos and pro bull riding visit the metro area, such as the annual Celebrate Freedom Rodeo at Wills Park Equestrian Center (Alpharetta) and PBR events at Gas South Arena (Duluth); no regular participation found.

chinese-opera.how: No Teochew-specific group was found; Atlanta Drama Club, a mostly Chinese non-profit founded in 2016, stages Chinese opera among its shows, including a spring festival gala at Infinite Energy Center.

ancient-ruins-excavation.how: No ancient ruins nearby, but the Greater Atlanta Archaeological Society has held public volunteer dig days on Native American sites, and Fernbank Museum has put out calls for archaeology volunteers.

paragliding.how: No suitable launch slopes in the metro area; the nearest school is Lookout Mountain Flight Park in Rising Fawn, GA (about 2 hours north), with one- and two-day beginner courses.

freediving.how: Diventures in Alpharetta lists freediving courses and trains year-round in an indoor heated pool with a 12-foot diving well; Freediving Passion also runs courses around Marietta.

meteorite-hunting.how: Hunting needs arid strewn fields where dark stones stand out; the best areas are Arizona's Franconia and Gold Basin fields and other US Southwest deserts, about 4 hours by air.

snorkeling.how: Diventures in Alpharetta lists a snorkeling program alongside swim and scuba lessons in its indoor pool; open-water snorkeling requires a trip to the coast.

bungee-jumping.how: No bungee site found; Six Flags Over Georgia's Sky Coaster hoists riders more than 18 stories and drops them into a bungee-style free fall.

taiko.how: Matsuriza Taiko, a metro Atlanta Japanese drum troupe, performs at JapanFest and community events, but no regular open beginner classes were confirmed.

tea-ceremony.how: The Chado Urasenke Tankoukai Atlanta Association meets at Nakato Restaurant and tea ceremony workshops appear at the annual JapanFest.

pottery-wheel.how: Chastain Arts Center's pottery studio runs eight-to-nine-week wheel-throwing courses for beginners and intermediate students on weekday and weekend slots.

perfumery.how: INDIEHOUSE runs guided custom-perfume workshops using professional perfumer's oils, with each guest taking home a 30 ml bottle.

irish-dance.how: Atlanta Irish Dance by Burke Connolly teaches Irish dance to all ages and abilities at its Faulkner Road studio and branches in Marietta, Decatur and Sandy Springs.

mahjong.how: 1 Dot Mah Jongg, Two Sparrows and Atlanta Mahjong Studio run lessons, guided play and leagues, and a Decatur social club hosts supervised beginner games.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: Boat Rock, a granite bouldering area southwest of the city, offers hundreds of boulder problems in the Greater Atlanta area, with classics such as Yellow Wall Arete.

geocaching.how: Stone Mountain Park hosts long-running caches including the multi-cache tour of Stone Mountain, and Atlanta has thousands of caches in city parks.

camping.how: Stone Mountain Park offers a campground plus yurt rental sites inside the park.

nature-guided-walks.how: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area offers ranger-led hikes, and Chattahoochee Nature Center runs trail and education programs.

orienteering.how: The Georgia Orienteering Club holds regular park events with a beginner guide, though many courses are in state parks beyond the metro radius.

birds-of-prey-watching.how: Chattahoochee Nature Center in Roswell has licensed wildlife staff rehabilitating birds of prey with resident raptors on display, plus riverside trails for wild hawks.

coastal-cleanup.how: No beach exists in the metro area, but Chattahoochee Riverkeeper's annual Sweep the Hooch river cleanup has dozens of sites in Metro Atlanta counties and the national recreation area.

genealogy.how: The National Archives at Atlanta in Morrow holds federal records for eight southeastern states, with a research room open by appointment.

meetups.how: Meetup lists large Atlanta groups for hiking, board games, mahjong, crafts and journaling, with weekly events.

latte-art.how: Opo Coffee Training Lab in Decatur runs small beginner latte-art classes led by an SCA-authorized trainer.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The APEX Museum on Sweet Auburn Avenue preserves and presents Black history with exhibits on the Sweet Auburn district.

creative-writing.how: The Atlanta Writers Club holds monthly meetings and periodic workshops, with critique groups across the metro and a free first visit.

dim-sum-making.how: Cozymeal and Classbento list chef-led Chinese and dumpling-making classes in Atlanta covering folding techniques and dim sum menus.

sourdough-baking.how: Atlanta Botanical Garden runs Sourdough 101 classes where each student takes home a starter, and The Cook's Warehouse in Midtown offers hands-on sourdough classes.

chocolate-making.how: XOCOLATL Small Batch Chocolate at Krog Street Market offers micro-factory tours and bean-to-bar tastings, though hands-on making classes were not confirmed as ongoing.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Cultured South, a kombucha taproom on the BeltLine Westside Trail, hosts occasional fermentation classes and Atlanta Utility Works runs hands-on fermentation events.

tango.how: Local teachers run beginner to advanced Argentine tango classes through Meetup and a weekly class at Daza Dance on Peachtree Road.

drone-racing.how: Georgia Tech's RotorJackets host MultiGP regional qualifier races at Couch Park Field, and the DRC Atlanta chapter races FPV drones.

sup-yoga.how: Atlanta SUP Yoga holds seasonal sessions, including night classes, on Lake Lanier and earlier reports mention classes at Morgan Falls on the Chattahoochee.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Atlanta GAA (Clan na nGael), founded in 1996, fields men's and women's Gaelic football, hurling and camogie teams and runs a coed league.

allotment-gardening.how: Atlanta has hundreds of community gardens with rentable plots, including Blue Heron Community Garden's 30-plus organic plots and city park plots reserved through Atlanta Recreation.

mushroom-foraging.how: The Urban Food Forest at Browns Mill, Atlanta's first food forest, allows visitor foraging including mushrooms, though no organised mushroom forays were confirmed.
mushroom-foraging.venue: Urban Food Forest at Browns Mill

language-exchange.how: Language Exchange Atlanta meets every other Sunday on Buford Highway in Doraville, splitting members into practice groups by language.

philosophy-cafe.how: A Philosophy Cafe discussion group meets monthly at Moe's in Buckhead, listed on Philosophy Now's events page.

toastmasters.how: Buckhead, Peachtree and iNCRedible Toastmasters clubs meet weekly in Atlanta, and guests can usually visit free.

chinese-calligraphy.how: Library and cultural-centre workshops such as a Fulton County Library calligraphy session at Buckhead Library offer one-off Chinese calligraphy, with no regular class confirmed.

rug-tufting.how: TuTu Tufting on Peachtree Road runs rug-tufting and other fluid-art activities.

wartime-history.how: Atlanta History Center hosted the Their Finest Hour WWII exhibit (closed March 2026) and traveling WWII exhibits, and holds the Veterans History Project oral histories.

lion-dance.how: Lion and dragon dances are performed at metro Atlanta Chinese New Year events, though no regular lion-dance class was confirmed.
lion-dance.venue: Metro Atlanta Chinese New Year events

outdoor-skydiving.how: No drop zone operates inside the metro area because of airspace and safety constraints; the nearest tandem operator, Skydive Monroe at Monroe-Walton County Airport, is about an hour east of Atlanta.

clay-sculpture.how: Cherrylion Studios in Atlanta teaches classical and contemporary sculpting in clay, plaster and other media to adults and teens, from basic forms to finished works.

coffee-roasting.how: Epicurean Atlanta hosted a two-hour Coffee Connoisseur class with a master roaster and live roasting demonstration, though the latest listing found was from 2023.

sake-tasting.how: Vino Venue has listed a WSET introductory sake course and Savi Provisions in Inman Park has hosted sake festivals with over 30 sakes to taste.

kite-flying.how: The Meadow at Piedmont Park hosts the annual Atlanta World Kite Festival and Expo, and the open park is used for casual kite flying year-round.

temple-activities.how: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Lilburn, among the largest Hindu temples in the US, is open free to visitors daily with a daily Arti ritual.

hang-gliding.how: The flat Piedmont terrain around Atlanta has no soaring sites; the nearest flight park is Lookout Mountain Flight Park at Rising Fawn, Georgia, roughly two hours' drive northwest.

luge.how: No luge track exists in the Southeast; the nearest permanent tracks are in Lake Placid, New York and Park City, Utah, and Atlanta's climate rules out natural-track sliding.

buzkashi.how: Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback game played mainly in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries, with no organised play in Georgia.

hot-spring-bathing.how: No bathing hot springs exist in the metro area; the nearest natural warm springs are at Warm Springs, Georgia, about 90 minutes south, and the region's geology offers none closer.

archery.how: Atlanta Archery Club in Dunwoody offers try-archery sessions, private lessons and open range time with certified coaches.

big-wall-climbing.how: Georgia has no big walls; the nearest multi-pitch cliffs are Looking Glass Rock and Linville Gorge in North Carolina (about 4 h by car), and true big-wall climbing is in Yosemite (air travel).

bmx.how: Brook Run Skatepark in Dunwoody is the largest skatepark in metro Atlanta and is open to both skateboards and BMX bikes; no dedicated BMX race track was found.

bobsled.how: No ice track exists in Georgia; the nearest bobsleigh and skeleton track is Lake Placid, New York (about 2 h flight plus 3 h drive), where public ride-along bobsled runs are offered.

bouldering.how: Stone Summit Midtown is a dedicated bouldering gym; Georgia Tech and Georgia State campus gyms and The Overlook on the BeltLine also have boulder walls.

camel-racing.how: Camel racing is not run in Georgia for lack of a camel-keeping tradition; the nearest regular races are the Virginia City Camel and Ostrich Races in Nevada (about 4.5 h flight plus 5 h drive).

capoeira.how: Capoeira Maculele in Decatur and Capoeira Training Club on Nabell Avenue teach Afro-Brazilian capoeira classes; Georgia Tech campus recreation also lists a class.

cheese-rolling.how: The cheese-rolling race is tied to one annual event at Cooper's Hill, Gloucestershire, England (about 9 h flight plus 2.5 h drive from Atlanta); no equivalent is held in Georgia.

cricket.how: Cricket leagues and the Atlanta Cricket Academy play on grounds in Forsyth County (Cumming), with youth cricket growing and more large grounds planned in the region.
cricket.venue: Atlanta Cricket Academy / Atlanta Cricket League fields

curling.how: The Atlanta Curling Club runs two-hour Learn-to-Curl sessions at the Atlanta IceForum in Duluth, with all equipment supplied, plus leagues for members.

hunting.how: Deer hunting is permitted on state wildlife management areas such as Dawson Forest and Paulding Forest WMA north and west of the city (about 60-70 km), with Georgia licences and seasons.

dinghy-sailing.how: Beginner sailing classes covering boat handling and sail trimming run on Lake Lanier or Lake Allatoona, listed through CourseHorse.
dinghy-sailing.venue: Lake Lanier / Lake Allatoona sailing classes (CourseHorse listing)

disc-golf.how: Perkerson Park and DeKalb Memorial Park each have free 18-hole disc golf courses, and J.P. Moseley Park in Stockbridge has 27 holes.

elephant-polo.how: Elephant polo needs working elephants and is played in Thailand, Nepal and India; none are kept for sport in Georgia (nearest regular tournament is Hua Hin, Thailand, over 24 h of travel).

fencing.how: Beginner and advanced foil, epee and sabre classes for adults and kids are listed for Atlanta through CourseHorse.

horse-riding.how: Chastain Horse Park in Buckhead runs a riding school for beginner to advanced riders from about age 6, alongside boarding and therapeutic riding.

ice-hockey.how: Center Ice Arena offers public skating, hockey leagues and learn-to-skate classes in the Atlanta area.

ice-skating.how: The Roof at Ponce City Market has a seasonal outdoor rooftop ice rink with skate rental included in admission.
ice-skating.venue: The Roof at Ponce City Market

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Stone Summit on Presidential Parkway is one of the largest climbing gyms in the US, with walls up to 60 ft with top-rope, lead, bouldering and auto-belay; Georgia Tech also has a rope climbing wall.

judo.how: Atlanta Judo Midtown has taught judo for over 30 years from its dojo on Faulkner Road NE, with a youth cadet program for ages 5-13.

padel.how: PATL and ITA Atlanta run four public padel courts in Chamblee, with other indoor padel courts at Let's Go Pickleball & Padel in Peachtree City.

pickleball.how: Atlanta Pickleball Center in Ellsworth Industrial has 10 indoor courts, and Dill Dinkers is opening a large club in West End.

rugby.how: Atlanta Bucks Rugby Club (founded 2003) is a dues-paying inclusive men's rugby union club listed among Atlanta adult sports leagues.

skateboarding.how: Historic Fourth Ward Park has the city's first public skatepark on the BeltLine, with other city parks at Arthur Langford Jr. and Harper Park and an indoor park at Skate ATL.

ski-jumping.how: Georgia has no ski jumps or reliable snow; the nearest jumps are at Lake Placid, New York (about 2 h flight plus 3 h drive).

snowboarding.how: Metro Atlanta has no snow-sports terrain; the nearest snowboarding on artificial snow is in the North Carolina mountains such as Cataloochee or Sugar Mountain (about 3.5-4.5 h by car).

taekwondo.how: Master Moreland Tae Kwondo & Hapkido on Old National Highway teaches taekwondo to adults and children, and a Decatur martial arts gym also lists taekwondo.

ultimate-frisbee.how: Atlanta Sport & Social Club listed recreational ultimate leagues, and the Atlanta Hustle play professional ultimate in the AUDL.

freshwater-fishing.how: The Chattahoochee River below Buford Dam is a year-round stocked rainbow and wild brown trout fishery, and Lake Lanier is known for striped and spotted bass.

fishing.how: Chattahoochee River trout fishing and guided charters on Lake Lanier for striped bass are listed near Atlanta (state licence and trout stamp needed).

urban-foraging.how: Outdoor Afro and local guides describe foraging for wild onions, muscadines, blackberries and greens at Constitution Lakes, the South River Trail and Arabia Mountain, advising beginners to go with an expert.
urban-foraging.venue: Constitution Lakes / Arabia Mountain (Outdoor Afro guidance)

hiking.how: Stone Mountain, Arabia Mountain and Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park all have marked hiking trails with skyline views from summits.

intertidal-walking.how: Atlanta is inland with no tidal shoreline; the nearest tidal flats are Tybee Island and the Georgia coast (about 4-4.5 h by car).

mountain-biking.how: Southside Park has a beginner 1.2-mile loop maintained by MTB Atlanta (SORBA), and Cochran Mill Park offers about 18 miles of cross-country trails.

trail-running.how: Panola Mountain and the Chattahoochee East Palisades trails are popular trail running venues around Atlanta.

stargazing.how: Fernbank Science Center's observatory with a 36-inch telescope holds free public viewing nights Thursday and Friday evenings, and the Atlanta Astronomy Club holds dark-sky events.

hydroponics-urban-farming.how: The City of Atlanta's AgLanta runs guided farm and food-forest bus tours of urban farms around the city.
hydroponics-urban-farming.venue: AgLanta Grown farm tours (City of Atlanta)

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Georgia has no mangroves, which stop at northeast Florida; the nearest guided mangrove paddling is around Jacksonville or St. Augustine, Florida (about 5 h by car).

rc-aircraft.how: Cobb County Radio Control Modelers Club (founded 1962, AMA chartered) flies at its field with a training program, and other clubs fly in Cumming and Peachtree City.
rc-aircraft.venue: Cobb County Radio Control Modelers Club

drone-flying.how: Recreational drone flying is allowed in designated areas of county parks such as Tribble Mill Park, while Piedmont Park sits in controlled airspace.

sailing.how: Sailing classes cover boat handling and sail trimming on Lake Lanier or Lake Allatoona, listed through CourseHorse.
sailing.venue: Lake Lanier / Lake Allatoona sailing classes (CourseHorse listing)

scuba-diving.how: Scuba certification courses near Atlanta, typically US$199-400, are offered by shops such as RT Divers and Dive Haven, with open-water dives at lakes or quarries.

surfing-ocean.how: Atlanta is inland and Georgia's Atlantic coast has only small surf; the nearest ocean surfing is Tybee Island (about 4 h by car) or Cocoa Beach, Florida (about 6.5 h).

acting.how: Alliance Theatre offers acting courses for stage, film and TV, with Catapult Acting Studios and The Basement Theatre (improv) also running adult classes.

bagpipes.how: The Atlanta Pipe Band, a nonprofit, teaches Scottish bagpiping and drumming, with free lessons for youth aged 8 and up.

ballet.how: Atlanta Ballet's Centre for Dance Education offers ballet for ages 2 to adult, including drop-in adult classes at Midtown, Buckhead and Cobb studios.
ballet.venue: Atlanta Ballet Centre for Dance Education

bharatanatyam.how: KA Academy of Indian Music and Dance teaches classical Indian dance and vocal music in classes grouped by age and skill level.
bharatanatyam.venue: KA Academy of Indian Music and Dance

breakdancing.how: A Lessons.com listing for Atlanta Ballet's Virginia-Highland centre names breakdancing among its dance styles; no dedicated breaking school was confirmed.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Challenge Aerial on Cherokee Ave teaches silks and lyra with a four-week adult intro course, and Trapeze Atlanta and Atlanta Kick Fitness also run aerial classes.

choir.how: The Choral Guild of Atlanta (founded 1939) is a long-running amateur chorus, and Atlanta Master Chorale is a further choral organization.

flamenco.how: Atlanta Ballet's Centre for Dance Education lists flamenco among its disciplines at its Midtown, Buckhead and Cobb studios.
flamenco.venue: Atlanta Ballet Centre for Dance Education

gamelan.how: Emory University's community gamelan ensemble, founded in 1997 and directed by Javanese master Darsono, plays Central Javanese gamelan.

guitar.how: Atlanta School of Musical Arts teaches guitar, piano, voice and drums to kids and adults.

harp.how: Cooper Music School (Ensemble Schools) lists harp lessons in Atlanta for any age and level, and independent teachers at the Atlanta Harp Center teach adults from scratch with rental harps.

improv-comedy.how: Dad's Garage Theatre runs improv and sketch classes for adults with free open-house sample classes, and The Basement Theatre also offers improv classes.

music-production.how: Atlanta School of Musical Arts on Lavista Road teaches piano and music production lessons, including for adults.

piano.how: Atlanta School of Musical Arts and The Music Studio Atlanta offer piano lessons for adults and children, and Georgia Academy of Music is a nonprofit teaching piano to all ages.

pole-dance.how: Beginner and intro pole classes run at The Milan Method, The Secret Garden Pole Fitness Boutique and Vertical Joe's Westside Midtown, bookable through ClassPass.
pole-dance.venue: The Milan Method Dance Fitness Studio
pole-dance.area: West End / Joseph E. Lowery Blvd

salsa-bachata.how: Dance With Me in Midtown teaches salsa and bachata to solo students, and SALSAtlanta, PASOFino and Aatma Dance Studio run group classes for all levels.

stand-up-comedy.how: Laughing Skull Lounge hosts open mics Monday to Wednesday and a multi-week stand-up class with a graduation show, and Dad's Garage runs stand-up sample classes.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Dance With Me lists swing dance lessons in Atlanta, taught to solo students without partners.

tabla.how: An Atlanta Indian arts directory lists a tabla teacher and the Indian Music Academy in Marietta among local Indian classical music schools.

sitar.how: The Indian Music Academy in Marietta and other schools in an Atlanta Indian arts directory teach Indian classical instruments.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Callanwolde Fine Arts Center runs eight-week beginning handbuilding courses teaching pinch, coil and slab methods.

glassblowing.how: Decatur Glassblowing offers beginner hot-shop classes for one to three people, typically making a sculpted flower or blown ornament, and Duckbill Studios in Scottdale also offers classes.

lampworking.how: FlameTree Glass is a torchwork studio offering public and private lampworking classes.

stained-glass.how: Atlanta Glass runs an in-person Stained Glass Fundamentals course covering cutting, foiling and soldering.

etching.how: Atlanta Printmakers Studio offers multi-week courses and one-day workshops in etching alongside screen printing and relief printing.

printmaking-screenprint.how: Atlanta Printmakers Studio runs screen printing courses and workshops with open studio access.

lithography.how: Atlanta Printmakers Studio teaches relief, etching, screen and letterpress printing; stone lithography itself was not found among its listed courses.

woodworking.how: MASS Collective, a Castleberry Hill makerspace, offers workshop memberships and classes in wood, metal and leather, and Decatur Makers and Freeside Atlanta also have woodshops.

leatherwork.how: MASS Collective lists classes and memberships covering leather alongside wood, metal and glass.

blacksmithing.how: MASS Collective offers metal workshop access and classes, though a dedicated beginner blacksmithing forge class was not confirmed.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: CourseHorse lists Atlanta jewelry classes covering wire wrapping, beading and metalworking, and MASS Collective offers metal classes.

candle-making.how: Candlefish's chandlery studio at Ponce City Market runs candle-making workshops where participants pour two jar candles.

macrame.how: Fabricate Studios runs weaving, sewing and macrame wall-hanging workshops.

weaving.how: Fabricate Studios offers weaving instruction from about $40 as part of its craft workshops.

knitting-crochet.how: Atlanta Craft Club hosts bring-your-own-craft nights and workshops, and The Beehive offers knitting and felting courses.

embroidery.how: CourseHorse lists Atlanta embroidery classes from basic stitches to advanced designs.

film-photography-darkroom.how: Callanwolde Fine Arts Center runs black-and-white darkroom workshops with chemistry included, and The Photographer's Studio is a nonprofit community darkroom.

filmmaking.how: A 2-hour Intro to Cinema Cameras class is offered in Atlanta for beginners.

photography.how: Digital Photo Academy runs guided photo shoots such as at Oakland Cemetery, and Callanwolde offers photography courses.

origami.how: CourseHorse lists beginner and advanced origami classes in Atlanta.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: Chastain Arts Center offers figure drawing and ACCC runs adult life-drawing courses with live models.

oil-painting.how: Dawn Art Studios teaches acrylic and oil painting to adults of all levels, and Chastain Arts Center and the High Museum run painting classes.

watercolour-painting.how: Chastain Arts Center and CourseHorse listings offer watercolor classes for adults in Atlanta.

3d-printing.how: Decatur Makers (Decatur) and Freeside Atlanta (West End) offer 3D printers and classes to members and the public.

laser-cutting.how: Decatur Makers lists laser cutters among its shop tools, and Freeside Atlanta has a CO2 laser cutter and runs classes.

cnc-machining.how: Freeside Atlanta has a small CNC router and metal shop, and Decatur Makers has metalworking and CNC-capable tools.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Freeside Atlanta is a nonprofit hackerspace in West End and Decatur Makers has an electronics shop, both hosting classes.

robotics-arduino.how: Freeside Atlanta and Decatur Makers host electronics and Arduino-style classes and open build nights.

amateur-radio.how: The North Fulton Amateur Radio League in Roswell lists entry-level license classes and exam sessions in the ARRL club directory.

hackathons.how: Georgia Tech hosts hackathons such as Ramblin' Hacks and the 36-hour AI ATL, though participation may favor students.

ctf-security.how: The DC404 meetup at Manuel's Tavern ran a hands-on CTF session, and OWASP Atlanta holds security meetups.

coding-meetups.how: Atlanta has an active meetup scene including Refactr.Tech code jams and many tech groups listed in a local meetup tour.

watchmaking-horology.how: The Atlanta Watch Society hosted half-day watchmaking classes with the Horological Society of New York in January 2026; they are occasional rather than regular.

arcade-games.how: The Escape Gamebar in Brookhaven combines pinball, arcade and light-gun games with escape rooms, and Joystick Gamebar is another game bar.

board-games.how: Manuel's Tavern hosts a weekly beginner-friendly board game meetup, and local game stores run learn-to-play sessions.

chess.how: Atlanta Checkmate Club runs weekly chess nights in bars such as Ladybird Grove and Politan Row, and Atlanta Chess Mess meets at Manuel's Tavern.

contract-bridge.how: The Bridge Club of Atlanta is an ACBL-sanctioned duplicate club, among the largest in North America, with Midtown Bridge Club and others in the metro.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Atlanta RPG Meetup runs D&D and other tabletop RPG games several nights a week, providing dice and character sheets to first-timers.

escape-rooms.how: The Escape Gamebar and Time to Escape in Brookhaven and Beat the Bomb on the Upper Westside run escape rooms.

esports-gaming.how: Gaming lounges with high-end PCs and consoles offer hourly or day-pass play and tournaments across Midtown, Downtown and suburbs.

vr-gaming.how: Atlanta has VR arcades and free-roam arenas with wireless headsets and staff help, plus VR escape rooms.

trading-card-games.how: Atlanta-area game stores run regular Magic: The Gathering, Pokemon and Yu-Gi-Oh! tournaments including Friday Night Magic.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Battle & Brew in Sandy Springs is a game bar hosting tabletop and geek events, and Atlanta game stores stock Warhammer.

pub-trivia.how: Battle & Brew in Sandy Springs runs weekly Geek Trivia nights.

cosplay.how: Dragon Con in downtown Atlanta hosts a major cosplay contest and Battle & Brew runs cosplay nights.

ten-pin-bowling.how: The Painted Pin in Buckhead is a boutique bowling bar, and Pin and Proper in Grant Park offers bowling variants.

homebrewing-beer.how: Schoolhouse Brewing in Marietta runs a homebrew supply store and Homebrew University classes.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Cook's Warehouse in Piedmont Heights teaches baking and cake classes at $99-110, though bread-specific sessions were not confirmed.

mixology.how: The Distillery of Modern Art in Chamblee offers monthly cocktail creation classes and CourseHorse lists Atlanta mixology classes.

beekeeping-honey.how: The Metro Atlanta Beekeepers Association runs an annual one-day beginner course with in-hive sessions at teaching apiaries, and Dunwoody Nature Center has offered beekeeping classes.

snow-sculpture.how: Atlanta gets too little snow for snow sculpture; the nearest reliable snow is in the North Carolina mountains, about 3 hours away by car.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: CocuSocial and Classpop! run hands-on fresh-pasta and other cuisine classes at several metro locations, with ingredients supplied.

sushi-making.how: CocuSocial offers beginner sushi-rolling classes with no experience needed, and Classpop! runs Sushi 101 sessions at Chattahoochee Row.

hawker-crawling.how: Food halls such as Ponce City Market, Krog Street Market and Pine Street Market give a multi-stall, many-cuisine grazing experience, though not a hawker-centre culture.
hawker-crawling.venue: Ponce City Market Central Food Hall

whisky-society.how: H&F Whisk(e)y Society runs whiskey-focused tasting and education events in Atlanta.

whisky-tasting.how: Atlanta Whiskey Academy teaches an in-person Whiskey 101 class on history, production and tasting different styles.

wine-tasting-wset.how: Atlanta Wine School runs formal instructor-led wine classes including certification-style courses, and shops such as Highland Fine Wine and Barcelona Wine Bar host sommelier-led tastings.

birdwatching.how: Birds Georgia (formerly Atlanta Audubon) and Chattahoochee Nature Center host guided bird walks in metro parks and wetlands; Georgia Tech also runs a weekly birdwatchers club.

butterfly-watching.how: Chattahoochee Nature Center holds a seasonal Butterfly Encounter/festival with live butterflies, and its gardens attract wild butterflies.

coin-collecting.how: Northlake Stamp & Coin, open since 1969, buys, sells and appraises coins alongside stamps and cards.

stamp-collecting.how: Northlake Stamp & Coin sells, buys and appraises stamps and collections.

comic-collecting.how: Oxford Comics & Games (30+ years) and Titan Games & Comics are long-running comic shops in the metro area.

rock-fossil-collecting.how: The Georgia Mineral Society in Norcross holds monthly meetings, fossil and mineral section meetings, workshops and regular field trips to collecting sites.

sneaker-collecting.how: Premium Kicks is a sneaker resale boutique on Cheshire Bridge Road.

trading-cards.how: The Card Shop on Cheshire Bridge Road sells sports and trading cards, and Atlanta has many card shops across the metro.

vinyl-records.how: Criminal Records in Little Five Points is a long-running independent shop selling new and used vinyl.

archival-research.how: Atlanta History Center's Kenan Research Center and the Georgia Archives hold public research collections.

art-gallery.how: The High Museum of Art is the region's main art museum, with African, American and European collections.

museums.how: Atlanta has major museums including the High Museum of Art, Fernbank Museum of Natural History and Atlanta History Center.

science-museum.how: Fernbank Museum of Natural History has dinosaurs, fossils, live animals, a giant-screen theater and 75 acres of old-growth forest trails.

poetry-slam.how: A weekly Sunday slam and open mic at Bar Crema in Decatur descends from the Java Monkey Speaks series, and the Art Amok! slam team runs a second venue.

public-lectures.how: Atlanta History Center hosts author talks, film screenings and public programs.

history-walks.how: Atlanta Preservation Center offers volunteer-led 1.5-hour guided walking tours (Historic Downtown, Grant Park, Sweet Auburn, Inman Park) March to November; History Afoot Atlanta also runs neighborhood tours.

heritage-trails.how: Atlanta Preservation Center's Sweet Auburn and Historic Downtown walking tours cover heritage districts, and the Atlanta History Center runs related tours.

french-language.how: Alliance Francaise d'Atlanta teaches French to adults and youth, with private and corporate classes and DELF/DALF preparation.
