german-language.how: Atlanta Institute of Language teaches German in group and one-on-one classes.

japanese-language.how: Atlanta Institute of Language teaches Japanese in group and one-on-one classes.

spanish-language.how: Atlanta Institute of Language and Hyperfluent offer Spanish group and private lessons.

sign-language.how: American Sign Language is taught at some metro colleges and community programs; no specific Atlanta provider confirmed.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Atlanta Humane Society takes volunteers for dog walking, fostering, shelter medicine help and outreach, with training at its Atlanta and Marietta locations; PAWS Atlanta in Decatur also needs volunteers.

volunteering.how: Atlanta Humane Society and PAWS Atlanta run volunteer programs with orientations, including court-required service hours.

pet-adoption.how: Atlanta Humane Society and PAWS Atlanta adopt out dogs and cats.

dog-parks.how: Piedmont Park lists dog parks among its amenities, with off-leash areas across the city.

yoga.how: Evolation Yoga, Yonder Yoga and Mysore Yoga Atlanta offer heated, vinyasa and Ashtanga classes.

pilates.how: Club Pilates offers small-group reformer classes and Evolation Yoga lists Pilates classes.

sauna.how: Perspire Sauna Studio (Pharr Road) and Refresh Cryo and Sauna sell infrared sauna sessions.

cold-plunge.how: Refresh Cryo and Sauna offers contrast-therapy suites combining infrared sauna with cold plunge.

tai-chi.how: Body & Brain Yoga Tai Chi offers tai chi, qigong and meditation classes at Atlanta and Marietta locations.

qigong.how: Body & Brain Yoga Tai Chi teaches qigong with breathing and meditation.

meditation.how: Studios like Yonder Yoga and Mysore Yoga Atlanta, plus community and senior centers, offer guided meditation and breathwork.

massage.how: Wellness and recovery studios such as Wellhaus and STAT Wellness offer massage and bodywork on ClassPass.

running-club.how: Atlanta Track Club, a large metro running club, hosts group runs and events.

urban-exploration.how: Guided history and architecture walks along the BeltLine and in Grant Park and Old Fourth Ward offer sanctioned city exploration.

high-ropes-course.how: Treetop Quest Dunwoody has 60+ obstacles across four levels with a briefing; Level 4 is a difficult strength-and-balance course (ages 12+).

zip-lining.how: Treetop Quest Dunwoody's Level 3 course is all zip lines; Levels 1 and 2 suit beginners from age 7.

indoor-skydiving.how: iFLY Atlanta, a vertical wind tunnel on Cobb Parkway, takes first-time flyers after a short briefing.

clay-shooting.how: Atlanta-area gun clubs such as Atlanta Gun Club offer sporting clays and skeet shooting; not confirmed on an operator page.

safari.how: Zoo Atlanta offers giraffe feeding, Wild Encounters and NightCrawler overnights as a safari-like experience.

indoor-snow-play.how: Stone Mountain Park runs a seasonal artificial-snow tubing and play area in winter.

whale-watching.how: Atlanta is inland; whale and dolphin watching is on the Georgia/Florida coast around Savannah or Jacksonville, roughly 4-5 hours away, with right whales only in winter.

white-water-rafting.how: No sustained whitewater exists in the Piedmont metro; the Ocoee River on the Tennessee line, about 1.5 hours north, is the nearest commercial rafting (Raft One and others).

snow-skiing.how: Atlanta's climate lacks reliable snow and elevation; the nearest ski resorts (Sugar Mountain, Beech Mountain) are in western North Carolina, about 4 hours away.

dog-sledding.how: Dog sledding needs deep snow, which the Georgia Piedmont does not get; the nearest options are in the northern US or Canada, a flight away.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers exist in the Southeast; the nearest are in Alaska or the Rockies, a 4-5 hour flight away.

volcano-boarding.how: No volcanoes exist in Georgia; Cerro Negro in Nicaragua is the classic site, a few hours' flight away.

sandboarding-desert.how: Georgia has no large desert dune fields; the nearest dunes are coastal sand dunes on the Georgia coast, about 4 hours away, and true desert is in the US Southwest.

canyoning.how: Canyoning needs steep waterfall gorges, which the Piedmont lacks; the nearest guided canyoning is in the western North Carolina mountains, about 3-4 hours away.

cave-diving.how: Atlanta sits on crystalline Piedmont rock with no flooded cave systems; the nearest cave-diving springs are in north Florida, around 5-6 hours away.

cave-exploring.how: The metro lies on non-karst Piedmont rock; the nearest accessible caves are in northwest Georgia limestone (e.g. Kingston Saltpeter Cave, Cloudland Canyon), roughly 1-1.5 hours away.

base-jumping.how: BASE jumping needs legal cliffs or fixed structures, which the metro lacks; the nearest recognised site is the New River Gorge Bridge in West Virginia (Bridge Day), around 7 hours away.

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is outlawed or absent in Georgia; the nearest traditions are in Spain, Portugal or Mexico.

mountaineering.how: There are no alpine mountains in the metro; the Southern Appalachians of North Georgia and North Carolina, 1.5-4 hours away, offer hiking and rock climbing, and true mountaineering is in the Rockies.

whale-watching.how: Fantasea Cruising runs seasonal whale watching cruises from Circular Quay, including a 2-hour express cruise and a multi-cruise explorer pass.

fencing.how: Sydney University Fencing Club trains at the Arena Sports Centre in Camperdown and is listed with NSW Fencing, which hosts open competitions for members and non-members.
fencing.venue: Sydney University Fencing Club (Arena Sports Centre)

board-games.how: Meetup lists many weekly board-game nights across Sydney, for example Sydney Central Board Games (Mondays), Board Games in a Bar (Surry Hills) and Fortress Sydney's free Wednesday board games.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: The Sydney DnD Meetup group runs weekly 5th-edition campaigns including a learn-to-play night, and Fortress Sydney hosts a Sunday Dungeons & Flagons session.

language-exchange.how: Sydney Language Exchange, Speak Easy International and several Japanese, Spanish and Italian conversation groups hold regular in-person exchange nights listed on Meetup.

coding-meetups.how: Recurring developer meetups such as SydJS, Golang Sydney and Ruby Sydney hold regular talks and socials.

ctf-security.how: SecTalks Sydney runs regular Ninja Night security events (capture-the-flag style hacking challenges and talks).

toastmasters.how: Many Toastmasters clubs meet across Sydney, including Burwood, Drummoyne (Club 5 Dock), Chatswood Communicators, Epping and Dundas.

robotics-arduino.how: OzBerry IoT Makers meets at Chatswood Library for Raspberry Pi and IoT tinkering, and a monthly AI in Robotics meetup is listed.

heritage-trails.how: The City of Sydney's free Sydney Culture Walks app offers seven self-guided walks, including Hidden laneways, Chinatown to Circular Quay, and the Yananurala Walking on Country trail.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: Sydney Cooking School in Neutral Bay offers over 30 hands-on classes covering world cuisines, barbecuing and desserts.

latte-art.how: Sydney Bar School's Coffee School teaches espresso and barista skills in a CBD classroom course.

mixology.how: Sydney Bar School runs bar skills and cocktail courses in the CBD, per its course listings and reviews.

science-museum.how: Sydney Observatory (Powerhouse) at Millers Point is open Thursday to Sunday, and Powerhouse Castle Hill and the new Parramatta museum cover science, design and technology.

museums.how: The Australian Museum at 1 William Street is open daily with free general entry and permanent natural history exhibitions.

art-gallery.how: The Art Gallery of NSW in the Domain and the Museum of Contemporary Art at Circular Quay are major public galleries.

gamelan.how: A directory lists four Sydney gamelan groups: Langen Suka (Javanese), Sekaa Gong Tirta Sinar, Suara Jaya and Suwitra Jaya (Balinese, UNSW students, alumni and staff).

padel.how: Padel.com.au describes Sydney as one of the most active padel markets, with about 65 indoor and outdoor courts across the eastern suburbs, inner west and northern beaches, booked via Playtomic with racket hire at most venues.
padel.area: Eastern suburbs, inner west, northern beaches

trading-cards.how: Good Games, a retailer of trading card games, board games and miniatures, opened a Marrickville store in September 2026 and promotes organised play programs such as Pokemon events.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Good Games stocks Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar ranges and paints at its Sydney store; organised in-store play is not shown on the page.

beekeeping-honey.how: Sydney Community College lists beekeeping among its Home, Garden and Cooking courses.

woodworking.how: Sydney Community College lists wood among its handcraft course materials, alongside metal, clay, resin and yarn.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Sydney Community College lists baking among its Home, Garden and Cooking courses.

wartime-history.how: The Anzac Memorial in Hyde Park is a heritage-listed war memorial and museum, and Cockatoo Island and Fort Denison offer guided harbour-heritage tours.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The Sydney Jewish Museum in Darlinghurst documents Jewish and Holocaust history, and the Chinese Garden of Friendship sits at Darling Harbour.

chess.how: The Sydney Mechanics' School of Arts runs a weekly Social Chess Group on Thursdays open to all skill levels, and a chess club also meets weekly at Esperanto House.
chess.venue: Sydney Mechanics' School of Arts (Social Chess Group)

mahjong.how: The Sydney Mechanics' School of Arts runs weekly Western Mah Jong groups, one for beginners (Wednesdays) and one for advanced players (Tuesdays).

contract-bridge.how: The Sydney Bridge Centre on Goulburn Street hosts WEA Sydney's Learn to Play Bridge course, and the Sydney Mechanics' School of Arts runs a weekly Friday Social Bridge Group.

book-club.how: The Sydney Mechanics' School of Arts hosts a Saturday Mystery and Crime Reading Group (book discussion), and Meetup lists further clubs such as the Western Classics Book Club.

pub-trivia.how: A Time Out guide lists weekly pub trivia nights across Sydney, including the Toxteth Hotel (Glebe), Union Hotel (Newtown), Imperial Hotel (Erskineville), Welcome Hotel (Rozelle) and Ivanhoe Hotel (Manly).

german-language.how: WEA Sydney runs in-person German courses from beginner A1 to advanced C1 conversation at its Bathurst Street centre.

spanish-language.how: WEA Sydney runs ten-plus in-person Spanish courses from beginner A1 to advanced C1 conversation at its Bathurst Street centre.

wine-tasting-wset.how: WEA Sydney runs wine-tasting courses such as Semillon, Sauvignon Blanc and a Champagne Masterclass at its Bathurst Street centre; formal WSET certification is not shown on the page.

history-walks.how: WEA Sydney runs guided historical walks such as the Victorian and Federation CBD walk, Kirribilli, Vaucluse mansions and South Head, with fixed meeting points.

creative-writing.how: WEA Sydney offers short creative writing workshops, such as Writing Your Legacy Memoir and a three-week practical writing workshop, at its Bathurst Street centre.

public-lectures.how: WEA Sydney's One Night Only evening talks (for example Agatha Christie, Cinema of the 1970s and an Elvis evening) run on Friday nights at its Bathurst Street centre, and the University of Sydney hosts the Sydney Ideas public lecture series.

philosophy-cafe.how: WEA Sydney runs a Philosophy Club course and other philosophy discussion courses in person, and Meetup lists open philosophical discussion nights at Humanist House.

japanese-language.how: WEA Sydney runs in-person beginner and intermediate Japanese courses, and the Japan Foundation Sydney in Chippendale runs Japanese language courses (J-Course).

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: Manly Kayak Centre, Let's Go SUP (La Perouse) and Cronulla SUP offer paddleboard lessons, and several harbour and river operators hire boards.

freshwater-fishing.how: Sydney.com names Manly Dam, Clifton Gardens, Camp Cove and Cronulla beaches as popular fishing spots around the harbour and northern beaches.

tea-ceremony.how: Meetup lists an Urasenke Chakai traditional matcha ceremony in Sydney, and Eventbrite lists ceremonial matcha sessions at Nakano Darling in Ultimo.

birdwatching.how: Meetup lists Great Aussie Bird Count events at Manly and bird-hide sessions at Homebush Bay (Sydney Olympic Park wetlands).
birdwatching.venue: Bicentennial Park bird hide, Homebush Bay

coastal-cleanup.how: Take 3 For The Sea runs community programs encouraging beach and waterway clean-ups, and Meetup lists Dive Against Debris clean-up dives in Sydney.
coastal-cleanup.venue: Take 3 For The Sea / Dive Against Debris

esports-gaming.how: Meetup lists social PC gaming nights at Fortress Sydney and a 50-player in-person LAN party with PCs provided; organised competitive leagues are not shown.

sushi-making.how: Eventbrite lists sushi cooking classes, including a Superfood Sushi class and a weekend Japanese ramen and sushi course, at Radio Cairo restaurant in Cremorne.

film-photography-darkroom.how: Eventbrite lists a film-look photography event at Ted's World of Imaging, and a Sydney photography Meetup group runs sessions on a monochromatic film look; darkroom printing courses are not shown.

poetry-slam.how: Northern Beaches Council libraries list an Open Mic Night among adult programs, and Meetup lists open mic nights such as Soultrap in Surry Hills; dedicated poetry slams are not shown.

archival-research.how: The City of Sydney Archives gives access to more than one million items through an online catalogue, records requests and an archives enquiry service; Northern Beaches libraries host a Family History Group.

whisky-tasting.how: Time Out lists many Sydney whisky bars, including Grain Bar in The Rocks (200+ whiskies, flights from about A$30), Uncle Ming's (90+ whiskies, 60 Japanese) and The Baxter Inn.

acting.how: Sydney Community College runs acting and drama courses (beginner acting intro, monologue, scene and play levels) and a musical theatre course for beginners at its Rozelle campus.

french-language.how: Sydney Community College offers French courses from Beginner L1 to Intermediate L3, delivered online and in Sydney.

korean-language.how: Sydney Community College runs Korean Beginners Level 1 (Monday evenings, ten weeks) and Level 2 courses.

sign-language.how: Sydney Community College offers Introduction to Auslan 1 and Auslan Level 2, taught by Deaf Connect, in person at Rozelle and online.
sign-language.venue: Sydney Community College (Deaf Connect Auslan courses)

weaving.how: Sydney Community College runs a Coiled Basket Weaving Workshop for Beginners as a one-day workshop at Rozelle.

chinese-ink-painting.how: Sydney Community College offers Chinese Brush Painting (Beginners, Orchids) and Chinese Landscape Painting courses.

qigong.how: Sydney Community College runs a Qi Gong Course for Beginners at its Rozelle campus; a free online and Parramatta tai chi and qigong group also meets via Meetup.

kintsugi.how: Sydney Community College runs an Art Kintsugi Beginners Workshop (four-hour Saturday session) in the Visual Arts room at Rozelle.

clay-sculpture.how: Sydney Community College lists Papier-Mache Sculpture for Beginners plus hand-building pottery and ceramic animal-sculpture courses.

community-gardening.how: The City of Sydney lists 22 community gardens (for example Glebe Community Gardens, Newtown Community Garden, Sydney City Farm in St Peters) that residents can join.

chinese-orchestra.how: The Sydney Chinese Orchestra is a professional ensemble performing traditional Chinese music (concerts, arts education, community events); amateur participation is not described on its site.

orchestra.how: Sydney Philharmonia runs open-entry community choirs (Festival Chorus, ChorusOz, Christmas Choir) that perform with orchestra at the Sydney Opera House; instrumental community orchestras were not confirmed.

trading-card-games.how: Fortress runs regular in-store card-game events such as Mana on Tap at its Chippendale store, with free walk-in entry.

running-club.how: Active Locals hosts social group runs through Meetup (for example Tuesday 6pm Darling Harbour and Wednesday Manly runs).

sourdough-baking.how: Hands-on sourdough bread classes for beginners (and a sourdough pizza masterclass) are listed on Eventbrite, held in Ryde.
sourdough-baking.venue: Sourdough Bread Beginner Hands On Class

sauna.how: Bondi Icebergs Club's ocean pool complex has a sauna (its cleaning schedule lists daily sauna closure), alongside the pool open to the public.

treetop-walk.how: Wild Ropes Treetops at St Ives and Taronga Zoo offer self-guided aerial ropes courses with swinging bridges and ziplines set 2-25 m up in the trees (a high-ropes course rather than a walkway).

outrigger-canoe.how: Sydney Outrigger Canoe Club (oldest outrigger club in NSW) runs six-week Novice Programs at Balmoral Beach, teaching paddle stroke, crew roles and safety before joining club training.

comic-collecting.how: Kings Comics, a Sydney comic shop (open since 1986), sells new and graded comics, graphic novels, manga and facsimile editions, with a CBD location.

stamp-collecting.how: Sydney Philatelics is a dealer selling and buying Australian, Pacific and Commonwealth stamps, covers and albums, mostly by mail order and online.

vinyl-records.how: Crosstalk Records in Leichhardt is an independent record store hosting vinyl launches; Sydney also has vinyl listening nights at venues such as The Vinyl Room.

cold-plunge.how: A one-off Ice Baths and Wellness Brand pop-up was listed at Beach Road Hotel in North Bondi; regular cold-plunge venues were not confirmed.

speedcubing.how: The World Cube Association lists regular Sydney speedcubing competitions, including the Tramsheds series at Harold Park Community Hall (Glebe) several times a year and events at North Sydney Boys High School.
speedcubing.venue: Tramsheds speedcubing competitions (Harold Park Community Hall)

hawker-crawling.how: Sydney Chinatown (Dixon Street and surrounds) hosts a Friday-evening night market with Asian street-food stalls, plus food courts in Market City, Haymarket.

temple-activities.how: Sze Yup Temple (Kwan Ti temple, 1898-1904) in Glebe is an active Taoist temple serving the Chinese community and hosting celebrations such as Chinese New Year.

dog-parks.how: The City of Sydney lists 50+ off-leash dog areas, including Sydney Park (Alexandria), Moore Park, Prince Alfred Park and Wentworth Park.

pet-adoption.how: Cat Protection Society of NSW runs an adoption centre in Newtown (by appointment after an online questionnaire); RSPCA NSW (Yagoona) and others also list adoptions.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Cat Protection Society of NSW recruits adult volunteers for shelter care, foster care and the cattery at Enmore Road, Newtown, though shelter-care applications were closed as of February 2026 and waiting lists are common.

volunteering.how: Sydney City Farm in St Peters runs volunteer working bees (after an induction session) and Cat Protection Society of NSW recruits adult volunteers, alongside event volunteering listed on Eventbrite.

hydroponics-urban-farming.how: Sydney City Farm in St Peters is a City of Sydney urban farm growing organic seasonal produce with volunteer working bees and horticulture workshops; hydroponic growing is not specified.

urban-foraging.how: Sydney City Farm schedules a Bush food discovery tour (14 November) and seasonal guided walks; dedicated urban foraging walks were not found.

cnc-machining.how: The City of Sydney's Ideas Lab makerspace at Darling Square Library has a laser cutter, 3D printer and electronics kit with open-access Makertime sessions for ages 16+; CNC milling is not listed.

billiards-snooker.how: A Sydney Introverts Meetup group has hosted pool nights at the Shark Hotel in the CBD; dedicated snooker clubs were not confirmed.

animation-2d.how: Sydney Community College offers Adobe After Effects: Animation and Video for Beginners, and Monster Mouse Studios in Marrickville ran a stop-motion collage animation workshop.

high-ropes-course.how: Treetops Adventure St Ives runs self-guided tree ropes courses 1-15 m above ground with swinging bridges and cargo nets, graded from beginner to expert; the park is about 30 minutes from the CBD.

zip-lining.how: Ziplines are part of the tree ropes courses at Treetops Adventure St Ives (Showgrounds, Mona Vale Rd).

cave-exploring.how: No caves open for adventure caving in the metro area; the nearest is Jenolan Caves, about 175 km west (roughly 3 hours by road), which offers abseiling and adventure cave tours.

snow-skiing.how: No snow fields near Sydney; the nearest resorts are Thredbo and Perisher in the Snowy Mountains, about 500 km south (roughly 6 hours by road, or a flight to Cooma).

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers in mainland Australia; the nearest guided glacier walks are at Franz Josef, New Zealand (heli-hikes), a trans-Tasman flight plus onward travel of most of a day.

hot-spring-bathing.how: No natural hot springs in the Sydney area; the nearest are the artesian hot spring baths at Moree, about 628 km north-west (roughly 8 hours by road or a short flight).

volcano-boarding.how: No volcanoes within reach of Sydney; volcano boarding is done at Cerro Negro (Nicaragua) and Mount Yasur (Vanuatu, the closest, a flight of several hours).

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is not practised in Australia (illegal in most countries); the nearest traditions are in Spain, Portugal, southern France and Latin America, a full day or more of travel away.

safari.how: No wild-animal safari in the Sydney area; the nearest open-range experience is Taronga Western Plains Zoo in Dubbo, about 400 km west (roughly 5 hours by road), and true safaris are in Africa.

sandboarding-desert.how: No large dunes or desert near Sydney; the nearest big mobile dunes are at Stockton Bight near Newcastle, roughly 2.5 hours north by road.

canyoning.how: No canyons within the metro area; the nearest canyoning is in the Blue Mountains, roughly 100 km west (about 2 hours by road).

archery.how: Sydney Bowmen Archery Club (Coogee) runs a two-hour introductory session for newcomers with equipment provided, and Sydney Community College and Northern Archers of Sydney run multi-week beginner courses.

australian-rules-football.how: Auskick junior programs and AFL Sydney club football (for example Balmain, Newtown, Glebe) operate across the metro, with the Sydney Swans as the local AFL team.
australian-rules-football.venue: AFL Sydney clubs (Balmain AFC, Birchgrove Oval)

bouldering.how: Dedicated bouldering gyms include BlocHaus (Marrickville), 9Degrees (Alexandria) and NOMAD (Annandale), with beginner courses and shoe rental.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Sydney Indoor Climbing Gym (St Peters) and Edge Rock Climbing Centre (Castle Hill, 100+ top-rope routes) offer belay inductions, courses and gear rental.

bmx.how: Sydney Park has a skate park and BMX-friendly zones plus a kids bike track; private BMX lessons run at indoor skate parks.

skateboarding.how: Sydney Park skate park has zones for all abilities and has hosted free beginner skateboarding lessons in school holidays; many council skate parks exist.

capoeira.how: Several schools run classes, including Capoeira Angola ECAMAR (Redfern), Capoeira Bondi, ABADA-Capoeira (Five Dock, Penrith) and Capoeira Topazio.

cricket.how: Cricket NSW runs social and indoor cricket and indoor net hire at Cricket Central (Sydney Olympic Park); The Rec Club (Miranda) runs social indoor cricket, and many suburban clubs play in summer.

ice-skating.how: Macquarie Ice Rink is open seven days for walk-in public sessions with skate hire, plus a Learn to Skate program and drop-in lessons; Ice Zoo and Liverpool Catholic Club also have rinks.

ice-hockey.how: The Sydney Bears (Ice Hockey NSW) play out of Macquarie Ice Rink, which schedules ice hockey sessions; junior and senior divisions run through Ice Hockey NSW.

pickleball.how: The Pickleball Association of NSW lists regular club and social sessions across Sydney (Blacktown, Crows Nest, Menai, The Ponds) and describes the sport as suitable for all levels.

judo.how: Judo NSW publishes a club locator and directory of judo clubs across Sydney and a "Play Judo" registration for newcomers.

bobsled.how: No bobsleigh or skeleton track exists in Australia; the nearest tracks are in the northern hemisphere (e.g. Lake Placid, USA; Nagano, Japan).

rugby.how: Sydney University Football Club (Camperdown) fields teams in the Shute Shield club competition, and suburban clubs across Sydney run community rugby union.

stargazing.how: Sydney Observatory (Millers Point, run by Powerhouse) offers guided tours and night photography workshops Wednesday to Sunday; amateur astronomy societies also hold public viewing nights.

kayaking.how: Sydney Harbour Kayaks at Spit Bridge (Mosman) rents sea kayaks and runs eco, sunrise and sunset tours, with free intro and safety lessons for beginners.

rowing.how: Sydney Rowing Club at Abbotsford Point on the Parramatta River (est. 1870) is a long-established club; other Sydney clubs run learn-to-row programs.

hiking.how: Royal National Park has 25 listed walking tracks including the Coast Track, about an hour south of the CBD, with a visitor centre and day entry fee.

camping.how: Bonnie Vale and Uloola Falls campgrounds in Royal National Park are bookable through NSW National Parks.
camping.venue: Bonnie Vale Campground, Royal National Park

fishing.how: Royal National Park lists fishing options, and Sydney Harbour and the beaches allow recreational saltwater fishing under a NSW licence regime.

allotment-gardening.how: City of Sydney lists community gardens (Glebe, Newtown, Ultimo) where members tend shared or individual beds; allotment-style plots are limited and the page does not say how to get one.

scuba-diving.how: Pro Dive runs open-water courses and gear hire from dive centres in St Peters and Manly, with shore dives in Sydney harbour and coastal sites.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Sydney Community College runs a 6-week hand-building course in Rozelle and hand-building workshops at Silky Shapes Studio in Willoughby.
pottery-handbuilding.venue: Sydney Community College (Rozelle) / Silky Shapes Studio

pottery-wheel.how: An 8-week wheel-throwing course for beginners runs at Silky Shapes Studio, Willoughby, via Sydney Community College, with many start dates.

photography.how: Sydney Community College runs beginner photography courses and one-day workshops in Rozelle; the Sydney Photography Community also meets on Meetup.

filmmaking.how: Sydney Community College offers a videography course (DSLR and mirrorless) in Rozelle and an online video editing and production course.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: Sydney Community College runs a six-session beginners Life Drawing course; Meetup lists Art Models and Photoshoot in Sydney for model-based sessions.

urban-sketching.how: Sydney Community College runs a two-session Urban Sketching drawing course.

watercolour-painting.how: Sydney Community College lists beginners watercolour painting and watercolour and sketching courses, including botanical art.

oil-painting.how: Sydney Community College lists an Oil Painting Course in its painting program.

bookbinding.how: Sydney Community College runs a two-day Bookbinding Course for Beginners.

candle-making.how: Sydney Community College runs a one-evening Candle Making Workshop.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Sydney Community College runs a Precious Metal Clay silver jewellery course (clay-based rather than traditional silversmithing).

knitting-crochet.how: Sydney Community College runs a Crochet Course for Beginners over four Saturdays.

dj-turntablism.how: Sydney Community College runs a Learn to DJ beginners course.

guitar.how: Sydney Community College runs Guitar Lessons for Beginners.

piano.how: Sydney Community College runs piano lessons for beginners (levels 1-3) and continuers.

choir.how: Sydney Philharmonia Choirs runs community choirs open to everyone (Festival Chorus, ChorusOz, Christmas Choir) and Sydney Community College runs a choir.

taiko.how: Taikoz has a home dojo in Ultimo and runs beginner to advanced taiko classes, kids and teens classes and workshops.

ballet.how: Sydney Community College runs 8-week Adult Ballet Classes for Beginners at Saint John's Church Hall, Birchgrove.
ballet.venue: Saint John's Church Hall (Sydney Community College)

stained-glass.how: Sydney Community College runs a leadlight Stained Glass Course for Beginners in Rozelle plus a glass fusing workshop.

stand-up-comedy.how: Sydney Community College runs a Stand-up Comedy Course for Beginners taught by a working comedian.

embroidery.how: Sydney Community College runs hand-stitch workshops (Textile Collage and Slow Stitch, beading and appliqué) in Rozelle; no dedicated embroidery course was listed.

salsa-bachata.how: Tropical Soul Dance Studio (Stanmore) runs beginner salsa and bachata classes and Australia Hall (Surry Hills) hosts Sydney salsa classes.

tango.how: Sydney Tango Collective runs free and regular Argentine tango classes in Paddington.

improv-comedy.how: Improv classes and shows run at The Chippo Hotel (Chippendale), The Abercrombie Hotel (Broadway) and Newtown Neighbourhood Centre, including a free improv class.

music-production.how: A 10-week mixing and recording course runs at Redfern Community Centre, and the Academy of Music and Performing Arts (Surry Hills) teaches music production.

pole-dance.how: Achieve Pole Studio in Rosebery runs pole dance classes and competitions.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Airmazing Studio in North Sydney is an aerial arts studio that hosts aerial events and classes.

surfing-ocean.how: Bondi Beach (about 7 km east of the CBD) has a surfboard-riding zone at its south end, and Bondi and North Bondi surf life saving clubs; surf schools operate on Sydney beaches.

sailing.how: Sydney Amateur Sailing Club (Cremorne Point, est. 1872) runs racing and events on the harbour; Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron (Kirribilli) is a members-only club.

dinghy-sailing.how: Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron (Kirribilli) runs a Youth Sailing program in Laser, Optimist and Pacer dinghies; it is a private members club.

keelboat-yachting.how: Sydney Amateur Sailing Club (Cremorne Point) members race keelboat yachts on Sydney Harbour, including Sydney to Hobart entrants.

horse-riding.how: Centennial Parklands has equestrian schools and a dirt horse-riding track on Grand Drive.

hang-gliding.how: Hang gliding and paragliding are flown from Bald Hill at Stanwell Park, about 59 km south of Sydney; no site was found within the metro area.

buzkashi.how: Buzkashi is played on the Central Asian steppe (Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan); no horse-and-carcass buzkashi exists in Australia.

camel-racing.how: Camel racing is held in outback Australia (the Camel Cup at Alice Springs, the Boulia Camel Races in Queensland), more than 2,000 km from Sydney; no regular races within the metro area.

cheese-rolling.how: The Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling and Wake is a single annual event on a specific hill in Gloucestershire, England.

elephant-polo.how: Elephant polo needs working elephants and is played in Thailand, Nepal and India; Australia has no suitable animals.

ski-jumping.how: No ski-jumping hill exists in Australia; the nearest hills are in Japan and Europe.

snow-sculpture.how: No snow in the Sydney metro area; snow sculpting is possible only in the Snowy Mountains (Perisher or Thredbo, roughly 5-6 hours by road) in winter.

snowboarding.how: No snow in the Sydney metro area; the nearest snowboarding is in the Snowy Mountains (Perisher or Thredbo, roughly 5-6 hours by road) in winter.

trail-running.how: Sydney Trail Series (since 2013) runs trail races at St Ives / Ku-ring-gai Chase and Manly Dam / Garigal National Park for all abilities including first-timers.

dragon-boat.how: DSA Dragon Boat Club at Meadowbank and Rowers On Cooks River (Wolli Creek) run come-and-try dragon boating sessions.

nature-guided-walks.how: Guided bird walks, bushfood walks and forest therapy walks run in Royal National Park, Lucas Heights, Nielsen Park and other reserves; Sydney Harbour National Park lists guided bushwalking tours.
nature-guided-walks.venue: Royal National Park / Sydney Harbour National Park

swing-lindy-hop.how: Swing Patrol lists Sydney as one of its locations, teaching swing and Lindy hop classes.

leatherwork.how: A Leather Journal Making Workshop runs at Woolloomooloo on a recurring weekly schedule.

perfumery.how: DIY CRAFTS in South Penrith runs a recurring Perfume Making Workshop.

etching.how: Hurstville Museum and Gallery runs a drypoint etching for beginners workshop (an intaglio technique), listed as sold out.

printmaking-screenprint.how: Hurstville Museum and Gallery runs a printmaking open art room on Saturdays; no dedicated screenprinting class was found.

chinese-calligraphy.how: A multi-date Chinese calligraphy workshop is listed at Darling Square Community Bank branch, Haymarket.

taekwondo.how: Taekwondo open training sessions run at Ultimo Public School and a free kids class at Guildford Community Centre.

ultimate-frisbee.how: Inner West Ultimate runs seasonal social leagues for all skill levels from Tempe and Earlwood with free beginner sessions before each league; Sydney Uni Ultimate Frisbee Club also competes.

breakdancing.how: Crossover Dance Studio teaches weekly breaking classes alongside hip hop and K-pop, with casual single-class passes.

flamenco.how: The Sydney Flamenco Studio in Chippendale runs classes for all levels, and Bondi Flamenco holds casual beginner classes near Town Hall.

glassblowing.how: A Marrickville studio runs Level 1 beginner flameworking glass classes and taster sessions that are bookable through City of Sydney What's On and ClassBento.

escape-rooms.how: Many escape room venues operate in the CBD and suburbs, including Next Level Escape, The Cipher Room in St Peters and Scram in Parramatta.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Kingpin Darling Harbour has 20 lanes and a bar, with further alleys such as Tenpin City in Lidcombe and AMF centres; Sydney Rams run a social league.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Several GAA clubs field men's and women's Gaelic football, hurling and camogie in Sydney, including Michael Cusacks, Cormac McAnallen's, Clan Na Gael and Young Ireland.

paintball.how: Spitfire Paintball in Concord and Die Hard Indoor Paintball in Turrella offer urban-style indoor paintball; larger outdoor parks near Camden lie beyond the metro area.

3d-printing.how: Darling Square Library in Haymarket has a makerspace with 3D printers and runs 3D printing workshops and open Makertime sessions for ages 16 and up.

irish-dance.how: Callanan Academy of Dance teaches adult Irish dance in Surry Hills, and the Sydney Irish Ceili Dancers hold step and set dancing every Thursday in Kingsgrove during term.

tap-dance.how: Beginner adult tap classes run through ClassBento (Lindfield), Sydney Community College (Birchgrove), and Sydney Dance Company's adult program.

kathak.how: Ruchi Sanghi Enterprize teaches Kathak from beginner to professional level, and Swastik Institute of Dance in Harris Park also offers Kathak.

bharatanatyam.how: Nrityasagara School of Dance in Glenhaven teaches Kalakshetra-style Bharatanatyam in group and private classes for different ages and levels.

netball.how: Sydney Uni Sport runs social netball competitions on Sundays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays at its Darlington centre, open to community members.

go-weiqi.how: The Sydney Go Club in Surry Hills has a professional in residence and runs monthly beginner classes, and the University of Sydney Go Society welcomes novices.

amateur-radio.how: Waverley Amateur Radio Society (formed 1919) and Manly-Warringah Radio Society operate in Sydney, and Amateur Radio NSW provides licence training.

ikebana.how: Sydney Community College runs a one-day Ikebana workshop on Japanese flower arranging at its Rozelle visual arts studio.

dim-sum-making.how: Sydney Community College runs a DIY Chinese Dumpling Making workshop in its Rozelle kitchen.

tai-chi.how: Sydney Community College runs Tai Chi courses for beginners and continuers in Rozelle.

meditation.how: Sydney Community College runs a Calm Mind meditation course for beginners in Rozelle.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Sydney Community College runs Fermenting and Pickling workshops in its Rozelle kitchen.

yoga.how: Sydney Community College runs Gentle Yoga for Wellness courses in Rozelle and a free Hatha yoga intro workshop.

rug-tufting.how: Tufttea Studio in North Strathfield runs a 4-hour Tufting 101 class, and Biu Biu Studio and other studios run beginner tufting classes via ClassBento.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Robots And Dinosaurs is a Sydney hackerspace with a laser cutter, open to first-time visitors for free on Saturdays and available through paid membership.

laser-cutting.how: City of Sydney libraries offer a laser cutting service at Darling Square Library for members, and Robots And Dinosaurs hackerspace has a laser cutter.

parkour.how: AAPES in Botany is a warehouse parkour and freerunning gym with year-round classes including first-timers sessions, and Ninja Parc in South Granville also runs parkour classes.

lacrosse.how: UNSW Lacrosse Club trains on Wednesday nights and plays in the Sydney Lacrosse League, with NSW Lacrosse based in Kingsford.

disc-golf.how: Newington Armory at Sydney Olympic Park has a free 18-basket disc golf course with discs available at the Visitor Centre, plus Whalan Reserve in Blacktown and Sefton Golf Course.

orienteering.how: Orienteering NSW clubs run weekly beginner-friendly events including the Sydney Summer Series, Saturday Orienteering Series and the Sydney MetrO League in parks and bushland.

lawn-bowls.how: Bondi Bowling Club offers walk-in social bowls and Chatswood Bowling Club lends bowls to newcomers, with many other clubs across Sydney.

pilates.how: Studio Pilates on Bathurst Street offers 40-minute reformer classes through the day, alongside other CBD studios such as PilatesBarre and City Physio & Pilates.

mountain-biking.how: Manly Dam, Old Man's Valley in Hornsby and Cascades Trail in Garigal National Park offer marked mountain bike trails across skill levels.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: The Sydney Rockclimbing Club (Sydney Rockies) and Sydney Uni Rockclimbing and Mountaineering Club run outdoor trips to local crags and the Blue Mountains for all skill levels.

homebrewing-beer.how: Sydney Community College runs a Home Beer Brewing for Beginners workshop series, and Country Brewer in Prospect gives home brew lessons.

game-development-jams.how: AIE Sydney has hosted a Global Game Jam site since 2009, and SXSW Sydney runs an annual game jam.

hackathons.how: Hack Club's Daydream runs a game-making hackathon for ages 13 to 18 in Kensington, and SXSW Sydney runs a remote game jam.

arcade-games.how: 1989 Arcade Bar in Newtown, B. Lucky & Sons at the Entertainment Quarter and Fortress Sydney in the CBD offer retro arcade and pinball games.

vr-gaming.how: Hyper Reality at the Entertainment Quarter has a VR arena for up to eight players, and VR Kingdom and Entermission in the CBD offer VR games and escape rooms.

coffee-roasting.how: The Roasting Club in Mascot runs hands-on roasting workshops on commercial equipment, and a guided tour with a roasting demo and cupping visits two Sydney roasteries.

massage.how: Sydney Community College runs Massage Course for Beginners (levels 1 and 2) at its Rozelle campus.

escape-rooms.how: Around 80 escape games in Paris and inner suburbs (e.g. Le Bureau des Legendes, The Greenhouse, Aladdin) bookable per team of 2-6 players.
escape-rooms.venue: Escape Game Le Bureau des Legendes

vr-gaming.how: Virtual Room VR arcades in Paris 11e and 17e, plus a VR arena at EVA in Boissy-Saint-Leger, sell timed multiplayer VR sessions.

paintball.how: Several paintball grounds in the Ile-de-France suburbs (Neuilly-sur-Marne, Pontault-Combault, Bruyeres-le-Chatel, indoor at Cergy-Pontoise) sell adult and child sessions.

wine-tasting-wset.how: Oenology courses and guided wine tastings run at Les Caves du Louvre and other Paris venues, including a 4-hour level 1 tasting course.

toastmasters.how: Many Toastmasters clubs meet in Paris (Lutece 75, Les Ailes in Paris 8, Paris La Defense, Forum des Rives de Seine), mostly weekly evening meetings in French or English.

language-exchange.how: Weekly language-exchange meetups run in Paris bars and cafes (Denfert Polyglottes, Afterwork Paris, Paris Multi-Language Meetup, ChitChat) for French, English, Japanese, Korean, Italian and more.

book-club.how: Dozens of French- and English-language book clubs meet in Paris (e.g. English-speaking Book Club in Paris, Paris Great Books Club, Club de lecture Les Mots Passants), several events per week.

philosophy-cafe.how: Cafe philo discussion evenings run in Paris, including Groupe Meetup Paris Philosophie (Sunday cafe philo) and a weekly English-language Cosy Cave Conversations cafe philo in the 10th.
philosophy-cafe.venue: Cosy Cave Conversations (Cafe Philo in English)

poetry-slam.how: Paris Lit Up runs a weekly Thursday open mic, and the Paris Poetry Circle holds English-language poetry readings in bars.

creative-writing.how: Writing workshops and sessions run across Paris (Paris Lit Up Right Bank Writers' Group, Libre d'ecrire, Ecrivaines Parisiennes Sunday atelier, Ready-Set-Write) in French and English.

running-club.how: Social running groups meet weekly in Paris and nearby (Paris Running Club beginner runs along the Seine, Founders Running Club Paris, La Team Fit Rueil, Paris Hash House Harriers).

meditation.how: Group meditation sessions run in Paris, e.g. Muraqaba silent Sufi meditation, Heartfulness meditation, and free Sahaj meditation in the 17th.

yoga.how: Many yoga studios and workshops in Paris and nearby (kitten yoga, parent-child yoga, face yoga, pilates/yoga in infrared sauna) bookable per session; classes from about 25 EUR on Funbooker.

sauna.how: Public and private saunas in Paris and inner suburbs, including hotel spas (Hotel Este, 10e), private infrared saunas (13e), a Japanese sauna (2e) and spa-sauna-hammam sites in Vitry-sur-Seine and Romainville; sessions from about 18 EUR.

massage.how: Massage, scrubs and hammam packages (Thai massage in the 12th, hammam-gommage-massage in the 13th and 17th) and sound massage sessions are bookable across Paris.

whisky-tasting.how: Whisky tasting workshops and blending sessions run in Paris (Atelier assemblage de whisky in the 7th, whisky tastings in the 11th, whisky and chocolate pairings in the 1st), from about 49 EUR.

latte-art.how: Barista and latte art workshops are offered in Paris 9e and 10e, alongside coffee tasting and caffeology classes.

fermentation-kombucha.how: A kimchi and home-fermented vegetables workshop is offered in Paris 11e as part of the city's cooking-class scene.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Pastry baking workshops (croissants and pains au chocolat in Paris 2e, gingerbread house) are bookable; dedicated bread-only courses were not seen in the listing.
artisan-bread-baking.venue: Atelier croissants et pains au chocolat, Paris 2e

history-walks.how: Many guided walking tours of Paris (Paris peu frequentable, Paris du crime, street-art in the Butte-aux-Cailles, Montmartre drawing walk) can be booked.
history-walks.venue: Visite guidee Le Paris du crime

science-museum.how: The Cite des sciences et de l'industrie (Universcience) in La Villette runs permanent and temporary science exhibitions, a Cite des enfants and a planetarium.
science-museum.venue: Cite des sciences et de l'industrie

public-lectures.how: The College de France gives free public lectures open to all on a first-come basis (arrive about 30 minutes early), mostly at the Marcelin-Berthelot site.

wartime-history.how: The Musee de la Liberation de Paris - Musee du General Leclerc - Musee Jean Moulin covers the Liberation of Paris in WWII, with free permanent collections and the Rol-Tanguy command post.
wartime-history.venue: Musee de la Liberation de Paris

museums.how: Paris has hundreds of museums, from the Louvre (with a Zurbaran retrospective running into 2027) to the Centre Pompidou and city museums, many with timed ticketing.

art-gallery.how: The Louvre, Centre Pompidou (with Cezanne et nous at the Grand Palais) and many other galleries and art museums show ongoing exhibitions in Paris.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The Institut du monde arabe hosts a museum, exhibitions, talks, film and music events and Arabic language courses.

archival-research.how: The Archives nationales operate reading rooms at Pierrefitte-sur-Seine and in Paris (Marais) plus an online virtual reading room with about 31,000 inventories.

spanish-language.how: The Instituto Cervantes Paris (rue Quentin Bauchart, 8e) runs Spanish courses by semester with a placement test and online enrolment.

japanese-language.how: The Maison de la culture du Japon a Paris offers Japanese-language courses (IRODORI programme, JLPT information) alongside a tadoku reading salon.
japanese-language.venue: Maison de la culture du Japon a Paris (MCJP)

cosplay.how: Japan Expo Paris at Paris-Nord Villepinte hosts cosplay contests and guest cosplayers each July (Extreme Cosplay Gathering finale); year-round cosplay is otherwise informal.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Several bowling alleys operate in the Paris region, including the Front de Seine alley in the 15th; French Wikipedia lists the Paris-region halls.

support-groups.how: Alcoholics Anonymous France runs a searchable directory of in-person and online meetings, including in Paris and Ile-de-France.

snowboarding.how: No snow terrain exists within the Paris basin; the nearest real snowboarding is in the Alps (about 6 hours by road or train) or the Vosges (about 4 hours).

canyoning.how: The Paris region has no gorges or canyon rivers; the nearest canyoning is in the Alps, Pyrenees or Vosges, roughly 4-8 hours away.

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is not practised in the Paris region; corridas are held only in southern France (Nimes, Arles, Bayonne), roughly 6-8 hours away.

hot-spring-bathing.how: No natural hot springs exist in the Paris basin; the nearest thermal-spring resorts are several hours away (e.g. Bourbonne-les-Bains, Haute-Marne, about 3.5 hours).

pilates.how: Pilates classes run in Paris studios (e.g. The Pilates Project, which also hosts yoga classes) and as Meetup pilates sessions such as Pilates & Girls Talk.

beekeeping-honey.how: The Rucher-Ecole of the Jardin du Luxembourg (Societe centrale d'apiculture, since 1856) trains adults in beekeeping with theory and practice and a diploma.

allotment-gardening.how: Allotment (jardins familiaux/ouvriers) gardens exist across the Paris region, e.g. the Fort d'Aubervilliers family gardens, Versailles and Saint-Cloud.

mountaineering.how: No high mountains in the Paris basin; the nearest alpine mountaineering is Chamonix (Mont Blanc massif), about 6 hours away by TGV and road.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers in the Paris region; the nearest is the Mer de Glace at Chamonix, about 6 hours away by train and road.

snow-skiing.how: No snow-reliable mountains near Paris; the nearest resorts are the Vosges (about 5 hours) and the Alps such as Chamonix (about 6 hours).

dog-sledding.how: Needs reliable snow and mountain terrain; the nearest options are in the Alps or Vosges, roughly 5-6 hours from Paris.

luge.how: Alpine luge/toboggan runs need mountain slopes; the nearest are in the Vosges or Alps, roughly 5-6 hours from Paris.

base-jumping.how: No cliffs or tall natural exits in the Paris area and jumping from structures is illegal; the nearest sites are the Alps (about 6 hours) or Normandy cliffs (about 2.5 hours).

cave-diving.how: No flooded natural cave systems near Paris; the nearest cave-diving regions are the Lot/Ardeche karst areas, roughly 6-8 hours away.

sandboarding-desert.how: No desert or large dunes near Paris; the nearest big dune is the Dune du Pilat near Arcachon (about 6 hours by train/road) and true desert is in North Africa.

volcano-boarding.how: No active or ash-slope volcano in the Paris region; volcano boarding is done at sites such as Cerro Negro in Nicaragua, with the nearest French volcanic range (Auvergne) about 4 hours away.

whale-watching.how: Paris is inland on the Seine; the nearest whale and dolphin watching is on the Atlantic coast (Brittany), roughly 4-5 hours away.

safari.how: No free-roaming large African wildlife in the Paris region; the nearest wildlife park drives are about 45 km out (Thoiry) and real safaris are in Africa.

hot-air-ballooning.how: A tethered helium balloon rises to about 150 m for roughly 10-minute flights over Paris, rather than a free-flying hot air balloon.

archery.how: Around ten clubs in Paris proper (Paris Arc Club, Inter-Activites, Arc Club Paris 12, Archers de Paris) and about 80 more in the Ile-de-France suburbs offer discovery sessions and club archery; clubs lend equipment.

cricket.how: The Paris Universite Club cricket section trains beginners and experienced players from age 7 at Stade Pershing in the Bois de Vincennes, with women's and junior groups.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Paris Gaels GAA (founded 1995) trains Gaelic football, hurling/camogie and handball at Stade Louis Lumiere (20e) and in Pantin, with free first trials and annual membership of about 80 EUR.

bouldering.how: Arkose runs a dozen bouldering and rope-climbing gyms across Paris and its inner suburbs (Nation, Montmartre, Pantin, Montreuil, Saint-Denis, Nanterre), with a discovery first entry for 10 EUR.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Arkose gyms in and around Paris (e.g. Chevaleret, Issy-les-Moulineaux voie, Massy, Nation) offer roped wall climbing for all levels with a 10 EUR discovery entry.

improv-comedy.how: Multiple Paris improv theatre groups run weekly shows, beginner workshops and free trial classes (Improvibes, Impro Studio, Kpten Impro), listed on Meetup.

tango.how: Danse a Paris cours et soirees runs weekly Argentine tango classes and open practice (practica) on Friday evenings, listed on Meetup.
tango.venue: Danse a Paris cours et soirees

stand-up-comedy.how: English-language stand-up shows and open mics run several nights a week in Paris (Green Mic Comedy, Kuhl Comedy open mic, Dissident Club, Wokistan Comedy Club in Pantin); French-language clubs also exist.

salsa-bachata.how: Several Paris schools and groups run weekly salsa, bachata and kizomba classes with a free first trial class (The Paris Salsa Bachata Kizomba, Studio Jahido, Queer Salsa Dance).

piano.how: Beginner piano initiation sessions and jazz-jam evenings with piano are listed on Meetup in Paris; conservatoires and private teachers provide regular lessons.

guitar.how: Guitar classes are listed on Meetup in Paris alongside open-mic and jam nights; private teachers and music schools offer regular lessons.

music-production.how: SuperSample Paris holds a weekly beatmaking and music-creation workshop, and Let's Make a Song runs paid studio sessions.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: Several groups run drop-in life drawing with nude models for about 13-35 EUR a session (Life Drawing Montmartre, Paris Modele Vivant, Conservatoire de dessin et de peinture de Paris).

urban-sketching.how: Drawing-from-nature workshops and bistro drawing evenings are listed on Meetup in Paris; no dedicated Urban Sketchers outing was confirmed.
urban-sketching.venue: The Art Club (Le Bistrot des Artistes)

hiking.how: Meetup groups (Paris Hiking, Rando/Hike Ile de France, Power Hiking Paris, Plein air Paris) run weekend group hikes of 11-27 km in forests around Paris such as Rambouillet, Fontainebleau and Rougeau, many reachable by train.

photography.how: Recurring Meetup photo walks (Take a Photo Walk Paris, Free Photo Walks Paris) and beginner studio workshops run across Paris.

watercolour-painting.how: The Wild Watercolor Workshop runs weekly beginner watercolour and drawing classes in Paris, with further watercolour ateliers listed on Meetup.

oil-painting.how: A weekly oil painting and drawing class (about 30 EUR) is run by the Meetup group Initiation a la peinture a l'huile in Paris.
oil-painting.venue: Initiation a la peinture a l'huile

camping.how: Camping Indigo Paris in the Bois de Boulogne is a seven-hectare campsite with about 510 pitches for tents, caravans and camper vans.

skateboarding.how: Bercy Skatepark is a covered 800 sq m skatepark with ramps in Parc de Bercy, used by skateboarders, rollerbladers and BMXers.

bmx.how: Bercy Skatepark in Parc de Bercy is open to BMX riders alongside skaters and rollerbladers; dedicated BMX track clubs exist in the suburbs.

ice-skating.how: Public ice rinks include Patinoire Sonja-Henie and Espace Pailleron in Paris, plus suburban rinks at Courbevoie, Asnieres, Champigny, Vitry, Fontenay-sous-Bois and Neuilly-sur-Marne.

fencing.how: Multi-sport clubs Paris Universite Club (Stade Charlety, 13e) and Racing Club de France (Bois de Boulogne) run fencing sections.

judo.how: Judo sections run at Paris Universite Club (Stade Charlety) and Racing Club de France, alongside many neighbourhood dojos.

rugby.how: Paris has Top 14 club Stade Francais (Stade Jean-Bouin, 16e) plus amateur rugby union sections at Paris Universite Club and Racing Club de France.

dinghy-sailing.how: The Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines leisure base offers sailing and windsurfing on its lake; Lac de Creteil in the east of the metro area also lists sailing, dinghy and windsurf clubs.
dinghy-sailing.venue: Base de plein air et de loisirs de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines

sailing.how: Dinghy sailing and windsurfing on the lakes of Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines and Creteil; no open-sea sailing within the metro area.
sailing.venue: Base de plein air et de loisirs de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines

kayaking.how: Canoe-kayak is offered at the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines leisure base and kayak clubs operate at Lac de Creteil.

rowing.how: Rowing clubs are listed at Lac de Creteil, and rowboats can be rented on the Lac Inferieur in the Bois de Boulogne.

dragon-boat.how: A dragon boat club is listed among the clubs at Lac de Creteil.
dragon-boat.venue: Lac de Creteil dragon boat club

horse-riding.how: Riding stables operate in the Bois de Boulogne (horse and pony rides at weekends) and at the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines base, which offers riding year-round from age two.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: No natural crags lie within the metro area; the sandstone boulders of the Fontainebleau forest (about 60 km southeast, roughly 1 hour by train) are the nearest outdoor climbing and bouldering.

nature-guided-walks.how: Meetup walking groups lead forest walks in the Paris region (Rambouillet forest nature hike, Plein air Paris hikes for about 2 EUR), reachable by train.

leatherwork.how: Lekrea runs a leather craftsmanship workshop with many dates in Bastille-Popincourt, listed on Eventbrite.

chinese-calligraphy.how: A2Z Atelier runs a weekly calligraphy and Chinese painting workshop at A2Z Art Gallery in Saint-Germain-des-Pres.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Friday evening ceramic classes are listed on Eventbrite at Faubourg du Temple near Hopital Saint-Louis (10e).

printmaking-screenprint.how: La Fourche-Guy Moquet (17e) hosts creative workshops including linocut (linogravure) printmaking; screenprinting itself was not confirmed.

bobsled.how: No track exists in the Paris region; France's only bobsleigh track is at La Plagne in the Alps, roughly 7 hours away by road or rail.

ski-jumping.how: Requires alpine terrain and snow; the nearest ski jumps are in the Alps (Courchevel, Chamonix), roughly 7-8 hours from Paris.

big-wall-climbing.how: Needs high mountain rock faces; the Paris basin is flat, and the nearest big walls are in the Alps (Chamonix area), roughly 7-8 hours away.

camel-racing.how: A desert-region tradition with no camel-racing scene in the Paris region; races are held in the Gulf states, North Africa and Australia.

buzkashi.how: A Central Asian horseback sport played in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries; no buzkashi is played in the Paris region.

elephant-polo.how: Requires working elephants, available in Nepal, Thailand and India; none are kept for sport in the Paris region.

cheese-rolling.how: The event is held only at Cooper's Hill near Gloucester, England; there is no equivalent in the Paris region.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Mangroves need a tropical coast; the Paris region has none, and the nearest are in French overseas territories or the tropics.

intertidal-walking.how: Needs a tidal coast; the nearest are the Normandy bays (Mont-Saint-Michel, Baie de Somme), roughly 2.5-4 hours from Paris.

surfing-ocean.how: No ocean coast in the Paris region; the nearest surfable Atlantic waves are in Brittany, Vendee or the Basque coast, roughly 3-6 hours away.

hang-gliding.how: Needs hills or cliffs for launch; the Paris basin is flat, and the nearest launch sites are on the Normandy cliffs or in the Alps, several hours away.

snow-sculpture.how: Requires reliable deep snow; Paris winters rarely provide it, and snow-sculpture events take place in the Alps.

ice-hockey.how: Les Francais Volants train at the Accor Arena rink (12e) with a hockey school open to all from age 3, and Patinoire Pailleron (19e) runs an ice school with adult groups.

taekwondo.how: Taekwondo Club Saint-Germain Paris (founded 1985) and several municipal-hall associations teach adult beginners, with trial classes offered.

scuba-diving.how: Introductory dives (bapteme) run in the 20 m deep dive pit at Villeneuve-la-Garenne, about 10 km north of the centre, with instructor and gear supplied.

ballet.how: The City of Paris runs beginner adult ballet classes (Vaugirard-Littre gym on Sundays, Saturday beginner workshop) and associations such as MAKO Danse (19e) offer adult beginner classes.

pottery-wheel.how: Several studios in Paris (Atelier Setsuko, Studio Inoui, Atelier Arts Rose Selavy) teach wheel throwing, from single 2-3 hour introductions to multi-week courses.

pickleball.how: 4PADEL Paris 20 has three bookable pickleball courts and the Pickleball Paris club runs open-play lunchtime sessions in gyms; Issy-les-Moulineaux also has courts.

dj-turntablism.how: Schools such as DJ Network (3-hour weekend initiation), All Music Four School and Rythmik Academy teach DJing on turntables and CDJs, plus private tutors.

pole-dance.how: Pole Dance Paris runs small-group pole classes for all levels in three studios on rue d'Avron near Nation.

capoeira.how: ANGA Capoeira Paris, Jogaki (free trial class) and Vida de Capoeira run adult capoeira classes in several districts.

padel.how: Municipal Padel Ladoumegue (19e) plus private indoor clubs (Paris Padel, Les Padelistes, Forest Hill Aquaboulevard) rent courts and racquets.

flamenco.how: Flamenco en France (11e) and Ida Flamenca (6e/7e) offer weekly adult flamenco dance classes at several levels, with trial classes.

glassblowing.how: Glassblowing introduction workshops (2-3 hours, make a piece to take home) are bookable through Wecandoo with artisans in Arcueil and Paris.

ultimate-frisbee.how: PUC Ultimate (Paris 13e), Lutece Ultimate and other clubs in Paris and Montrouge run recreational and competitive ultimate with beginner-friendly training.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Swing Cotton (Studio Breguet, 11e), Paris Anim' Bessie Smith and Brotherswing teach beginner Lindy Hop courses and discovery classes.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Paris Anim' centres (e.g. Wangari Maathai, 20e), the Village de cirque (12e) and Colectivo Newen run aerial fabric (tissu aerien) classes and workshops for adults.

curling.how: The only curling club in Ile-de-France is in Viry-Chatillon (Essonne), with introductory sessions by arrangement rather than open walk-in play.

breakdancing.how: Breakin'13 (13e) runs weekly breakdance classes for children, teens and adults with a free trial class, and Paris Anim' centres offer beginner breaking courses.

bharatanatyam.how: Anusha Cherer teaches Bharatanatyam in Paris with beginner classes on Wednesday evenings in the 10e and intermediate classes on Saturdays in the 18e, via the Shantam association.

kathak.how: Triwat International teaches Kathak, Bollywood and Indian folk dance classes and workshops in Paris, and a Kathak teacher is listed at Espace Sylvia Monfort (15e).

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Beginner silver jewellery workshops (rings, bracelets, hoops; 1.5-3 hours, work taken home) run in Paris 9e, 16e and 18e, plus a 70-hour professional jewellery course.

stained-glass.how: Tiffany copper-foil stained glass introductions (3-4 hours, make a panel to take home) are offered in Paris 17e, and A Fleur de Verre (3e) and Paris Ateliers teach the technique.

board-games.how: Meetup groups and bars such as Jovial (19e), Au Bonheur des Jeux de Societe and English-speaking Boardgamers of Paris host board game nights several times a week.
board-games.venue: Jovial Bar a Jeux de Societe

chess.how: The Rencontres d'echecs Meetup group holds chess meetups in Paris cafes (Cafe Cayo, The Irishman) and in Montreuil and Asnieres-sur-Seine.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: English-speaking Roleplayers of Paris and Tables ouvertes au De 12 host open tabletop RPG tables and campaigns in Paris.

coding-meetups.how: Regular developer meetups run in Paris, such as Rust Paris and the C++ Francophone user group.

game-development-jams.how: Paris Indie Games Developers (PIGD) meets at the Cite des Sciences et de l'Industrie; a game-development community exists though no jam event was seen.

australian-rules-football.how: Paris Cockerels (founded about 1998, oldest active French Australian football club) train and play at Stade du Polygone in Vincennes with a second team, the Cockatoos.

perfumery.how: Perfume-making workshops (1-3 hours, leave with your own bottle) run at Molinard (1er), Galimard (9e), 5eme Sens (7e) and a parfumeur studio in the 4e.

choir.how: Beginner-friendly amateur choirs include the Choeur de la Cite internationale (about 100 singers, all levels) and Le Sacre-Coeur choir (drop-in rehearsals on Tuesdays).

fishing.how: Angling is allowed on the Seine quays, Canal Saint-Martin, Canal de l'Ourcq and the Bois lakes with a day card (about 10 EUR); the federation runs Tuesday-evening street-fishing afterworks.

freshwater-fishing.how: Freshwater coarse fishing is practised in the Seine, Marne, canals and lake ponds with a day or annual card; the FIAAPPMA 75-92-93-94 federation runs street-fishing afterworks (Tuesdays, May to November).
freshwater-fishing.venue: Union des Pecheurs de Paris et de la Seine

rug-tufting.how: Beginner tufting workshops (2-3 hours, use a tufting gun and take home a small rug) run at Tufting Studio and with independent studios in Paris 1er, 5e and 14e.

knitting-crochet.how: Une Maille a l'Endroit (shops in Paris and the inner suburbs) teaches 1.5-hour knitting and crochet classes for beginners, and the Brin de Cousette haberdashery runs classes.

embroidery.how: Beginner hand-embroidery workshops (2.5-3 hours, materials provided) run in Paris 8e and 11e (Boutique Flanelle), with longer gold-embroidery courses at GRETA (10e).

candle-making.how: Scented-candle workshops (1.5-3 hours, take home your candles) are bookable across Paris in the 2e, 5e, 11e, 13e, 15e and 20e arrondissements.

chocolate-making.how: Chocolate workshops (tablets and truffles, 1-2 hours, from prepared couverture; also at the Musee du Chocolat) run in central Paris; no bean-to-bar roasting course was seen.

mixology.how: Two-hour cocktail workshops with a bartender (Parisian Cocktail Club, Colada, Les Raffineurs, La compagnie du mieux boire) run across the 2e, 8e, 11e, 15e and 18e.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: Hands-on cooking classes cover pasta and ravioli (2e, 4e), Japanese, Vietnamese and Thai cuisine in many arrondissements.

sushi-making.how: Sushi workshops with tasting are held in Paris 6e (traditional sushi) and at Le Labo Culinaire (17e).

stargazing.how: The Societe astronomique de France, headquartered in Paris, runs observation sessions, courses and monthly lectures for amateurs.

woodworking.how: Funbooker lists a 2.5-hour beginner woodworking initiation in Paris 18e covering saws and basic joints, with a level 2 photo-frame follow-up.

film-photography-darkroom.how: Centre Verdier-Photo (Ville de Paris) runs weekly black-and-white film development and darkroom printing courses for beginners and advanced students; Juste un Labo / Inactinique offers intensive darkroom workshops.

3d-printing.how: Volumes, a public fab lab in Paris 19e, offers 3D printers and other digital fabrication machines open to all; Homemakers (15e) and the Tumo fab lab at the Academie du Climat also provide 3D printing.

laser-cutting.how: Volumes (Paris 19e) and Homemakers (Paris 15e) list laser cutting and engraving among their open-access fab lab machines; the Academie du Climat fab lab also has a laser cutter.

cnc-machining.how: Volumes fab lab in Paris 19e lists CNC milling machines and a precision mill among its open-access equipment.

go-weiqi.how: Go players meet weekly at the Antony go club (Thursday and Saturday evenings) and at Paris-Saclay weekly beginner-friendly sessions; the Paris international go tournament is held yearly.

wargaming-warhammer.how: French Wargame Café in Paris 10e is a bar dedicated to miniature wargaming with decorated tables for Warhammer games and weekend tournaments.

arcade-games.how: Reset Bar (1er) offers free access to retro arcade cabinets, and La Tete dans les Nuages (2e) is a large arcade room selling tokens from about 2 EUR.

birdwatching.how: LPO members lead a free guided bird walk in the Bois de Boulogne every Sunday morning (running since 1946), beginners welcome; the Bois de Vincennes has a bird reserve with observation hides.
birdwatching.venue: LPO Ile-de-France, Bois de Boulogne walk

tai-chi.how: Association Atout Chine (Paris 5e) runs a weekly all-levels tai chi workshop, and Paris Anim' centres, the Chinese Cultural Centre and Kordiane (14e) offer adult tai chi classes.

contract-bridge.how: Bridge Club des Buttes-Chaumont (Paris 19e, FFB-affiliated) holds pair tournaments and beginner initiation courses; Paris Universite Club (13e) has a bridge section with initiation classes.

parkour.how: Culture Parkour and other associations hold parkour classes in the covered Centr'Halles Park at Forum des Halles; Pink Parkour runs an adult evening class and the city offers free introductory sessions.

cold-plunge.how: Paris Ice Club (Paris 9e) sells guided Wim Hof-method breathing and ice-bath sessions at 4-10 C, and a cryotherapy cold bath is bookable in Paris 17e.

pet-adoption.how: The SPA shelter in Gennevilliers (RER C) is the nearest to Paris and handles dog and cat adoptions with ID and address documents, plus a Maison des Chats in the Marais.

esports-gaming.how: Espot (Paris 1er) is a 2,000 m2 gaming venue with 120+ PCs, consoles and an arena; Milk Paris, V.Hive and the Maison de l'esport (20e) also host PC play and esports events.

kintsugi.how: Funbooker lists about seven kintsugi (gold ceramic repair) workshops in Paris, from Amo Studio (5e) to Ceramicafe Genevieve (11e) and L'Espace Japon (10e), open to beginners.

clay-sculpture.how: Funbooker lists self-hardening clay sculpture and modelling workshops across Paris (9e, 10e, 11e, 17e), roughly 25-75 EUR per person.

whisky-society.how: Guided whisky tastings are sold in Paris by Pro Degustation (9e), La Compagnie du mieux boire (11e) and Maison Benjamin Kuentz (7e), with shops such as La Maison du Whisky running tastings.

horse-polo.how: Polo de Paris, a private members' club at Bagatelle (Bois de Boulogne) and the only polo club in Paris, plays polo; access requires sponsorship and a waiting list.

stamp-collecting.how: Rue Drouot in Paris 9e hosts many philatelist dealers' shops serving stamp collectors.

pedal-boating.how: Rowing boats (not pedal boats) can be rented in season on Lac Daumesnil (Bois de Vincennes) and the Lac Inferieur (Bois de Boulogne).

irish-dance.how: Irish dance (claquettes irlandaises) lessons are offered by private teachers in Paris and the Association irlandaise de Paris runs ceili dance events.

tap-dance.how: City of Paris Paris Anim' centres run weekly adult beginner tap (claquettes) classes, e.g. Thursday evenings at Centre Paris Anim' Arras.

tea-ceremony.how: Paris tea schools and shops run Japanese tea ceremony (chanoyu) demonstrations with hands-on bowl preparation, e.g. Takamatsu Somi sessions and Maison Jugetsudo sencha workshops.

ikebana.how: Association Art Levant runs an ikebana workshop in Paris 12e for beginners and advanced students; Manako Jafas Paris is the local ikebana association (listing dated 2016).

homebrewing-beer.how: La Beer Fabrique and Brew Unique run hands-on beer brewing workshops in central Paris where participants brew their own batch with a professional brewer.

coffee-roasting.how: A Paris 6e workshop listed on Cap Adrenaline lets participants roast their own batch with a master roaster and take home about 200 g.

taiko.how: Tsunagari Taiko Center runs weekly Japanese taiko drum classes and weekend workshops for beginners in Paris 11e.

tabla.how: Private tabla teachers give lessons in Paris (18e, 14e) and online, for all levels at roughly EUR 25 per lesson.

sake-tasting.how: Sake tasting workshops with an expert run at the Caves du Louvre (7 sakes with food pairings) and at a Paris 16e venue via Funbooker.

sourdough-baking.how: A baker in Paris 12e runs a 2.5-hour sourdough bread workshop (rue Montgallet) where participants shape and bake loaves and take them home.
sourdough-baking.venue: Atelier pain au levain, rue Montgallet

dim-sum-making.how: Mama Ly in Vincennes runs 2 to 2.5-hour dumpling and dim sum cooking workshops; Chefsquare Bastille offers a Hong Kong menu class.

german-language.how: The Goethe-Institut Paris (av. d'Iena) runs German courses from A1 for adults, teens and children, in person and online.

trading-cards.how: Specialist shops such as MEiSiA (Paris 10e) host Pokemon TCG events and tournaments, and the Royaume du TCG convention is held at Paris Nord Villepinte.

trading-card-games.how: Pokemon TCG tournaments run at partner shops such as MEiSiA (Paris 10e) and at the Royaume du TCG convention; Magic-specific shop events were not confirmed.

mahjong.how: Magic Mahjong Social Pung, a Paris club founded in 2005, runs introductory sessions on MCR and Riichi rules and informal play twice a week; Tri Nitro Tiles meets in Paris 8e.

volunteering.how: JeVeuxAider.gouv.fr lists thousands of volunteer missions in Paris (Secours populaire, Serve the City Paris, Protection civile Paris Seine and others).

hackerspace-electronics.how: La Paillasse is an open community lab in Paris where members with a project get keys for self-service experimentation; TMP Lab is an older Paris hacker group (source article undated).

robotics-arduino.how: Sorbonne Universite continuing education runs a 14-hour introduction to digital electronics and Arduino programming at its FabLab on the Jussieu campus.

hackathons.how: Paris hosts frequent hackathons, e.g. Adopt AI Hackathons at the Grand Palais (Dec 2026) and the InnovHer women's health hackathon (Nov 2026).

ctf-security.how: Student cybersecurity associations in the Paris area run CTF competitions, e.g. DaVinciCTF (Pole Leonard de Vinci, La Defense) and the 404 CTF by HackademINT and Telecom SudParis.

lion-dance.how: Lion dance groups perform around Chinese New Year in Paris 13e and Belleville and in suburbs such as Aubervilliers and Noisy-le-Grand, per the national intangible heritage inventory.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: SPA shelters near Paris (e.g. Gennevilliers) and associations such as Reves de Chiens (Viry-Chatillon) recruit volunteers; the SPA also seeks volunteer investigators in Paris.

trail-running.how: Team Trail Paris (18e) holds three themed training sessions a week plus a monthly long run outside Paris; Trail in Paris trains Wednesdays below Montmartre.

geocaching.how: Hundreds of geocaches sit around Paris (e.g. the Eiffel TB Palace cache) and the club Les Geofranciliens organises events across Ile-de-France.

pub-trivia.how: The Paris Quiz Mistress runs English-language pub quiz nights in Paris, and an expat trivia night is listed on Wednesdays at La Pomme d'Eve.

filmmaking.how: The Atelier cinema ENAC (City of Paris) is a weekly adult course from screenwriting to shooting a short film, open to beginners, September to June.

acting.how: City-listed theatre schools such as La Fabrique du Comedien (Paris 1er) run weekly adult acting classes for beginners and experienced actors with end-of-year performances.

orchestra.how: Orchestre Impromptu, a Paris-area amateur symphony orchestra founded in 1994, accepts musicians without audition and rehearses Thursday evenings; Paris has about ten amateur orchestras.

poker.how: Paris card clubs such as Club Pierre Charron (8e), Club Circus (16e) and Cercle Clichy Montmartre run regular poker tournaments including free-entry freerolls.

harp.how: Paris municipal arrondissement music academies and private teachers give harp lessons (Celtic or pedal harp) to adults.

breakdancing.how: Old Town School of Folk Music lists a beginner Breakdancing class and Hip-Hop Dance 1 and 2 for adults.
breakdancing.venue: Old Town School of Folk Music

3d-printing.how: Pumping Station: One hackerspace has FDM and resin (Form 3 SLA) 3D printers available to members.

laser-cutting.how: Pumping Station: One lists laser cutters among its member equipment.

cnc-machining.how: Pumping Station: One has a ShopBot CNC wood mill, Tormach CNC metal mill and CNC plasma cutter for members.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Pumping Station: One is a volunteer-run hackerspace of about 450 members with soldering stations, oscilloscopes and PCB milling.

woodworking.how: Pumping Station: One's wood shop has table saw, planer, jointer, lathe and CNC router for members.

robotics-arduino.how: Pumping Station: One hackerspace offers electronics benches and tools used for microcontroller and robotics projects.

australian-rules-football.how: The Chicago Swans (USAFL, founded 2008) play Australian rules football at Waveland Field.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: The Chicago Patriots Gaelic Football Club plays Gaelic football in the city.

board-games.how: Meetup lists many Chicago board game groups (Chicago Tabletop & Board Games, Chicago Game Lovers, South Side Gaming) with regular events.

chess.how: Chicago Chess, Queer's Gambit and Evanston and Northshore chess clubs hold regular chess meetups.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Chicago Alternative RPG Meetup and Northwest Side Chicago Board Game Friends (monthly D&D at Stay and Play Game Cafe) host tabletop RPG sessions.

mahjong.how: Several mahjong groups meet in the northern suburbs, including Glenview Mahjong Club, NorthShore Mahjongg Meetup and Evanston Riichi Mahjong.

go-weiqi.how: Fox Valley Go/Baduk Club holds Saturday Go meetups in the western suburbs.

language-exchange.how: Meetup lists INT'L CAFE Chicago, Spanglish Exchange Chicago and Japanese Language Exchange Chicago groups.

japanese-language.how: Japanese Language Exchange with Native Japanese - Chicago meets via Meetup.

german-language.how: Goethe-Institut Chicago runs German programming and a German conversation Meetup group.

spanish-language.how: Spanglish Exchange Chicago runs Spanish-English language exchange events.

book-club.how: Dozens of Chicago book clubs meet through Meetup, e.g. Chicago Silent Book Club - Lakeview and Chicago SciFi and Fantasy Book Club.

philosophy-cafe.how: The Symposium, The Chicago Philosophy Meetup and Chicago Philosophy Association host philosophy discussion events.
philosophy-cafe.venue: The Symposium: Philosophy Community of Chicago

hackathons.how: Chicago Meetup groups host hackathons, e.g. Obvious Community Events - Chicago and Chicago Microsoft Power Platform Users Group.

coding-meetups.how: Chicago developer meetups include ChicaGo (Go language), Chicago AI Developers Group and People of Color Code.

toastmasters.how: Toastmasters clubs listed on Meetup include Town Criers Toastmasters and Bridge Builders Toastmasters.

birdwatching.how: Chicagoland Birding Meetup runs group birdwatching outings.

cosplay.how: Chicago anime and geek groups (AnimeChicago, Chicago Anime Hangouts) host cosplay-related events.

etching.how: Lillstreet Art Center offers Beyond the Basics of Etching, a multi-week fall class for students with some prior etching experience.

history-walks.how: Chicago Architecture Center runs guided walking tours on city history, including Old Town Triangle, Historic Wicker Park, Graceland Cemetery and Humboldt Park.

science-museum.how: The Museum of Science and Industry in Hyde Park houses the U-505 submarine, a coal mine tour and Giant Dome Theater, with ticketed general admission.

museums.how: The Field Museum (1400 S. DuSable Lake Shore Drive) is open daily 9am to 5pm, alongside the Museum of Science and Industry and the Art Institute.

poetry-slam.how: The Uptown Poetry Slam has run at the Green Mill on the third Sunday of each month since 1986.

archival-research.how: The Newberry Library reading rooms are open Tuesday to Saturday to researchers, with strong genealogy and manuscript archives.

public-lectures.how: The Newberry Library lists public programs, lectures and adult education classes on its calendar.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: PAWS Chicago volunteers socialise and care for adoptable pets at its Pippen Fasseas Adoption Center on Clybourn Avenue and its medical center.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Chicago Aerial Arts in Old Irving Park runs adult and kids aerial classes and holds regular student showcases.

pole-dance.how: The Brass Ring in Humboldt Park holds pole student showcases, indicating pole instruction, and pole shows run at Chicago venues.

dj-turntablism.how: Dig + Disconnect runs Intro to DJing workshops at Miyagi Records in Washington Park, and other Chicago DJ workshops are listed.

rug-tufting.how: Rug tufting workshops run at 5127 N Clark St in Andersonville and at 2927 S Archer Ave, with hundreds of dated sessions listed.

sushi-making.how: Cooking with Cass in Lakeview East and Gateway To Learning in Lincoln Square run sushi-making classes.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: The Chopping Block in Lincoln Square runs hands-on cooking classes at foundation and skill levels, and Eataly Chicago and Classpop! run pasta-making classes.

perfumery.how: Fragrance-making workshops run in Gold Coast and North Park (e.g. Create Your Own Signature Scent and DIY perfume workshops).
perfumery.venue: Reggie Hathorn Candles and Home Fragrances

dim-sum-making.how: Dumpling-from-scratch classes run in Chicago (e.g. Authentic Dumplings from Scratch, Asian Dumplings at Pilot Project Brewing), but no dedicated dim sum course was listed.

mixology.how: The Chopping Block in Lincoln Square offers wine and cocktail classes alongside its cooking programme.

wine-tasting-wset.how: The Chopping Block offers wine classes; no WSET-accredited course was confirmed.

escape-rooms.how: Escape-game experiences run in Chicago, including an outdoor escape game at Navy Pier and Escape the Museum at the Museum of Science and Industry.

latte-art.how: Counter Culture Coffee Chicago and Sip Society Coffee Education Center run beginner latte art and home barista classes.
