coffee-roasting.how: Intelligentsia runs a Home Barista Class plus roastery tour at its Chicago Roasting Works, and Counter Culture holds cupping and brewing classes; hands-on roasting itself was not listed.

whisky-tasting.how: Spirits & Spice Chicago runs a World of Whiskey class with many dates, and Warehouse Liquors hosts single-malt tastings.

whisky-society.how: Whisky Jewbilee Chicago, run by the Single Cask Nation whisky society, celebrates 15 years in Chicago; no local chapter membership page was read.

sourdough-baking.how: Baker Bettie teaches Sourdough for Beginners in Little Sicily, and sourdough classes also run at Prairie Food Co-Op.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Baker Bettie runs bread classes in Little Sicily, and Gateway To Learning in Lincoln Square teaches French macarons.

tea-ceremony.how: A Chabako Temae tea ceremony demonstration was held at the International Museum of Surgical Science, and the Japanese Culture Center in Lakeview runs related Japanese arts workshops.

arcade-games.how: Galloping Ghost Arcade in Brookfield has over 885 games on free play for a flat door fee, billed as the largest video arcade in the USA.

creative-writing.how: Chicago Meetup groups such as Just Write Chicago, Shut Up & Write Chicago and West Loop Writers run regular writing sessions and critique groups.

vinyl-records.how: Reckless Records has three Chicago stores (Wicker Park, Lakeview, Loop) selling and buying vinyl.

comic-collecting.how: Chicago Comics, billed as the city's oldest comic shop, sells new comics and discounted back issues on Clark Street.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The National Museum of Mexican Art in Pilsen has free admission, and the Polish Museum of America in West Town documents Polish American history.

art-gallery.how: The National Museum of Mexican Art in Pilsen is a free-admission art museum with Mexican and Chicano art, alongside many Chicago galleries.

heritage-trails.how: The Chicago Riverwalk is a public path along the river's south bank with a Vietnam Veterans Memorial Plaza and architectural districts, and the Chicago Architecture Center lists neighbourhood heritage walks.

clay-sculpture.how: Evanston Art Center lists adult Intro to Figurative Sculpture, Ceramic Sculpture and Evening Figure Sculpture courses.

dog-parks.how: Chicago Park District lists 34 designated off-leash Dog Friendly Areas in parks and beaches such as Montrose Beach and Puptown.

community-gardening.how: Chicago Park District lists about 98 community gardens where residents rent allotment plots, share space or volunteer.

acting.how: The Second City Training Center offers acting, improv and comedy classes plus drop-in sessions; Piven Theatre in Evanston also runs adult acting classes.

mushroom-foraging.how: The Illinois Mycological Association holds monthly talks and mycologist-led forays (surveys) to find and identify wild fungi, with dates posted.

magic.how: Chicago Magic Lounge stages close-up and stage magic and runs the six-week Chicago Magic College Level One course for beginners (21+).

support-groups.how: NAMI Chicago runs free, confidential peer-led support groups for adults with mental health conditions and for family members and caregivers.

pet-adoption.how: PAWS Chicago operates the Pippen Fasseas Adoption Center in Lincoln Park with online pet listings and adoption events, plus volunteer programs.

butterfly-watching.how: The Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum's Judy Istock Butterfly Haven is a 2,700 sq ft greenhouse with over 1,000 free-flying butterflies, plus an outdoor Woody Wickham Butterfly Garden.

birds-of-prey-watching.how: Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary on the lakefront is a major migration birding site with wintering roosting owls reported, but no dedicated raptor-watch programme was found.

sign-language.how: Chicago Hearing Society offers adult, youth and family American Sign Language classes (the local sign language rather than Singapore Sign Language).

meditation.how: The Zen Buddhist Temple of Chicago holds Sunday public meditation services and a four-session introductory meditation course open to non-Buddhists.

lion-dance.how: Lion dances feature in Chinatown festivals such as the Double Ten Parade; no regular lion dance troupe class was confirmed.

volunteering.how: The Chicago Park District Community Stewardship Program lets volunteers do litter pickup, trail maintenance, invasive plant removal, seed collection and native planting in natural areas.
volunteering.venue: Chicago Park District Community Stewardship Program

kitesurfing.how: The Chicago Park District permits kiteboarding at Montrose Beach on Lake Michigan.

wartime-history.how: The Griffin Museum of Science and Industry displays the captured WWII German submarine U-505 (a National Historic Landmark) with on-board tours and Enigma and patrol exhibits.
wartime-history.venue: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry (U-505)

orienteering.how: Orienteering USA lists the Chicago Area Orienteering Club (CAOC) as the local club running events in the region.

rock-fossil-collecting.how: The Chicago Rocks and Minerals Society for rock, mineral and fossil enthusiasts of all levels meets monthly in Skokie and co-runs the annual Chicagoland Gem, Mineral & Fossil Show.

ancient-ruins-excavation.how: No local digs; the University of Chicago's Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures museum (formerly Oriental Institute) shows Near Eastern galleries and offers docent and volunteer roles.
ancient-ruins-excavation.venue: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Museum

poker.how: Meetup lists Chicago-area live poker groups such as Sub Rosa Poker Club and Chicago Poker Players Club hosting $1/$2 and 1/3 no-limit hold'em cash games; no casino poker room was confirmed.

meetups.how: Meetup lists many Chicago interest groups such as Chicago Hiking Outdoors & Social Group and NW Chicago Social Group over 50 that run regular events.

indoor-skydiving.how: Vertical wind tunnel flights for first-timers at iFLY Chicago Rosemont near O'Hare, simulating freefall.

luge.how: No artificial luge track in the Chicago area; nearest is Utah Olympic Park near Park City, Utah (about 3.5 h flight) or Lake Placid, New York (about 2 h flight plus a drive).

mountaineering.how: Chicago is flat glacial plain with no mountains; nearest real mountaineering is the Rockies near Denver (about 2.5 h flight).

canyoning.how: No canyons or gorge streams in the flat Chicago region; nearest canyoning is in the Rockies/Utah (about 3 h flight).

cave-diving.how: No flooded caves in the Chicago area; nearest cave diving is Florida springs (about 3 h flight).

cave-exploring.how: No natural caves in the Chicago region (glacial till over bedrock); nearest show caves are in southern Wisconsin or Illinois (about 3-5 h drive).

base-jumping.how: No cliffs or tall legal jump sites in the Chicago area; nearest regular legal BASE jumping is New River Gorge, West Virginia (about 2 h flight plus drive).

whale-watching.how: Lake Michigan is a freshwater lake with no cetaceans; nearest whale watching is the Atlantic coast near Boston (about 2.5 h flight).

intertidal-walking.how: Lake Michigan has no tides; nearest tidal flats are on the Atlantic or Gulf coasts (about 2-3 h flight).

archery.how: Chicago Park District runs public archery ranges (e.g. Belmont Harbor and 72nd St) for first-timers and practiced shooters, and Archery Bow Range Chicago rents bows by the session.

curling.how: Chicago Curling Club in Northbrook runs two-hour Learn2Curl sessions on its dedicated ice for adults, with no experience needed, October to March.

bouldering.how: Movement (Lincoln Park and Wrigleyville), Brooklyn Boulders and First Ascent climbing gyms offer bouldering day passes with shoe rental.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Movement Lincoln Park, Brooklyn Boulders and First Ascent Avondale offer top-rope walls up to about 50-60 ft, and Maggie Daley Park has an outdoor climbing wall.

cricket.how: Chicago has an amateur cricket scene of about 100 teams in leagues such as the American Cricket Conference and Illinois Premier League Cricket Conference, with matches at Warren Park and elsewhere.

fencing.how: Lincoln Square Fencing teaches foil and sabre from beginner to elite, and Windy City Fencing and Illinois Fencers Club (Mt. Prospect) also run beginner classes.

sailing.how: Sail Chicago teaches adults on small keelboats from downtown harbors, and SailTime Chicago runs ASA courses from Burnham Harbor.

keelboat-yachting.how: SailTime Chicago runs ASA 101-106 keelboat courses on 33-36 ft Hunters from Burnham Harbor, and Sail Chicago teaches Basic to Skipper Prep on small keelboats.

kayaking.how: Urban Kayaks, Chicago Kayak and Kayak Chicago run lessons and tours on the Chicago River, Lake Michigan and Skokie Lagoons, including four-hour beginner classes.

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: Urban Kayaks, Chicago Paddle Company (Osterman Beach) and Chicago SUP offer beginner SUP lessons, yoga and rentals on the lakefront harbours.

scuba-diving.how: Learn Scuba Chicago and Dive Right In Scuba run PADI/NAUI Open Water courses with pool sessions in Chicago-area pools and quarry checkout dives.

ice-skating.how: Maggie Daley Park has a quarter-mile ice skating ribbon with skate rental, open in winter.

hiking.how: Forest Preserves of Cook County maintain 13 trail systems (Des Plaines River Trail, Palos, Thorn Creek and others) for hiking.
hiking.venue: Forest Preserves of Cook County trails

camping.how: Forest Preserves of Cook County operate five campgrounds (as of 2023) within the metro area.
camping.venue: Forest Preserves of Cook County campgrounds

stargazing.how: Adler Planetarium's Doane Observatory has a 20-inch telescope, the largest available to the public in the Chicago area, with public viewing and Adler After Dark events.

improv-comedy.how: The Second City Training Center runs Improv 1, Improv 1A and drop-in improv classes for beginners in Chicago.

stand-up-comedy.how: The Second City offers a Stand-Up 1 course and open stages for testing stand-up material.

guitar.how: Old Town School of Folk Music teaches guitar, banjo and mandolin in group classes and private lessons, with instrument rentals available.
guitar.venue: Old Town School of Folk Music

pottery-wheel.how: Evanston Art Center runs multi-week wheel-throwing courses, and Color Cocktail Factory (18th St, Pilsen) offers one-off beginner wheel sessions.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Evanston Art Center offers Pinch, Slab, Coil handbuilding courses and ceramic sculpture, and Color Cocktail Factory runs clay sculpting workshops.

bookbinding.how: Evanston Art Center runs 'Bookbinding: Basics & Beyond' and Chicago Botanic Garden offers a Botanical Covers bookbinding workshop.

printmaking-screenprint.how: Remade in Chicago holds screen printing workshops (BYO T-shirt) at its Logan Square studio.

watercolour-painting.how: The Paintbrush on N Clark St runs an Adult WaterColors class.

candle-making.how: Popcraft on W Division St runs candle DIY classes.

knitting-crochet.how: Discovery Center (N Elston Ave) offers an Intro to Knitting class.

tap-dance.how: Discovery Center offers a six-session beginning tap dance class.

salsa-bachata.how: Dance Center Chicago on N Lincoln Ave runs Bachata 101 and Kizomba classes.

judo.how: Tohkon Judo Academy, a non-profit dojo at the Japanese American Service Committee building, teaches Kodokan-style judo starting with breakfall training.

taekwondo.how: ChampYon TaeKwonDo USA Academy (since 1982) and Legacy TKD Academy run Olympic-style taekwondo classes with forms and sparring.

rugby.how: Chicago Lions Rugby Football Club (founded 1964, USA Rugby) plays in the Midwest Rugby Premiership.

ultimate-frisbee.how: Meetup lists Suburban Ultimate Frisbee (Schaumburg) and other Chicago-area ultimate pickup groups.

pickleball.how: Meetup groups such as We Pickleball for Fun! and Cube Chicago Padel run recurring pickleball sessions in the city.

padel.how: Cube Chicago Padel hosts padel and pickleball events and college nights listed on Meetup.

skateboarding.how: Chicago Park District runs free public skate parks (Grant Park Skate Park, Burnham 31st Street, Wilson Skatepark) for novice to advanced riders.

bmx.how: Grant Park's skate park is designed for skateboards, scooters, inline skates and BMX bikes, and Logan Boulevard Skate Park is shared by skaters and BMX riders (closed for expressway repairs at last check).

ice-hockey.how: Blackhawks Ice Center, Fifth Third Arena and Morgan Park Sports Center run learn-to-play programs and adult leagues such as the Blackhawks Adult Hockey League, with some gear rental.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: Figure Drawing Chicago and Studio 215 host drop-in and class figure drawing sessions with live models.

urban-sketching.how: Meetup groups such as Chicago Gay Drink and Draw and Chicago Creative Collaborators hold regular sketching sessions.

photography.how: Chicago Streets and Beyond Photography Group, Chicago Photography Community and West Suburban Photography Group run regular photo meetups.
photography.venue: Chicago Streets and Beyond Photography Group

film-photography-darkroom.how: Evanston Art Center runs a six-session Intro to Darkroom Photography covering black-and-white film development and gelatin silver prints.

choir.how: Choral-Aires Chorus holds weekly Monday rehearsals in the Chicago area.

tango.how: Dance Center Chicago teaches Intro, Beginner and Intermediate Argentine Tango in four-session courses for adults.

ballet.how: Lou Conte Dance Studio offers drop-in basic and beginning ballet for adults and teens, and Dance Dynamics runs Adult Ballet.

stained-glass.how: Circle Studio and Discovery Center in Chicago run one-day beginner stained glass workshops, and Evanston Art Center and Highland Park Art Center offer courses.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Evanston Art Center runs multi-week beginning jewelry and metalsmithing courses, and Chicago Jewelry and Lapidary Art School teaches wire-wrapping workshops.

horse-riding.how: Suburban stables such as Danada Equestrian Center (Wheaton), Double J Riding Club (Countryside) and Freedom Woods (Morton Grove) offer lessons from beginner level, and Cook County forest preserves have bridle trails.

irish-dance.how: Trinity Academy of Irish Dance (Southport Ave), McNulty School, Dennehy School and the Irish American Heritage Center teach Irish dance classes across Chicago and suburbs.

flamenco.how: Ensemble Espanol Spanish Dance Theater, based at Northeastern Illinois University, teaches flamenco and Spanish dance and has operated for about 40 years.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Dance Center Chicago teaches Intro, Beginner and Intermediate Swing leading to Lindy Hop, and Big City Swing runs swing courses on W Randolph St.

leatherwork.how: Ausrine's Arts Room offers a leather surface design book cover class, and Evanston Art Center runs wet-formed leatherwork.

embroidery.how: Linda Z's Sewing Center runs Embroidery for Newbies and machine embroidery classes; Chicago Botanic Garden and Evanston Art Center offer hand embroidery courses.

oil-painting.how: Evanston Art Center runs oil painting courses such as Painting the Still Life in Oils and Painting with Texture (oil and acrylic).

ikebana.how: Evanston Art Center teaches Ohara Ryu ikebana in a five-session course, and Morton Arboretum has run ikebana workshops.

chinese-calligraphy.how: Chicago calligraphy classes (Evanston Art Center, Spudnik Press, Discovery Center) teach Western italic, brush and modern lettering; no Chinese calligraphy class was found on the listing.

rowing.how: Chicago Rowing Foundation (Clark Park Boathouse), Lincoln Park Boat Club and Chicago Rowing Union run learn-to-row sessions on the Chicago River.

dragon-boat.how: Greater Chicago Dragon Boat Club runs beginner paddling sessions on the Chicago River with no experience or equipment needed.

fishing.how: Chicago Park District lists 13 stocked lagoons, 22 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline and nine harbors open for fishing year-round, with pier and parking passes for some sites.

freshwater-fishing.how: Stocked lagoons in Chicago parks and Lake Michigan harbours and piers allow fishing for perch, trout and other freshwater species.

allotment-gardening.how: NeighborSpace holds land for community gardens across Chicago, with individual plots leased seasonally (e.g. 94 raised beds at the 62nd Street Garden in Woodlawn, $50 per full plot).

nature-guided-walks.how: Meetup groups such as Chicago Hiking, Outdoors, & Social Group, Southwest Suburban Weekday Woods Walkers and Slow Walking, Meandering Mornings run guided walks at nature centers and forest preserves.

music-production.how: The Windy City .Wavs Producer's Meetup hosts regular beat and song feedback sessions for music producers.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: The Chicago area is flat glacial plain with no natural crags; the nearest outdoor climbing is Devil's Lake, Wisconsin (about 3 hours' drive) or Wisconsin's Sauk Prairie.

big-wall-climbing.how: No big walls exist in the flat Chicago area; the nearest are in the Rockies and Yosemite (a long flight away).

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Mangroves need a subtropical coast; the nearest are in Florida, about a 2-hour flight from Chicago.

surfing-ocean.how: Ocean surfing is impossible on an inland lake; the nearest ocean waves are on the Atlantic or Gulf coasts, about a 2-3 hour flight from Chicago.

camel-racing.how: Camel racing is not practised in the Midwest; it is a Gulf and South Asian tradition (e.g. the UAE or Saudi Arabia).

buzkashi.how: Buzkashi is played in Central Asia (Afghanistan) and has no organised presence in Chicago.

cheese-rolling.how: The Cooper's Hill cheese-rolling event is held annually near Gloucester, England, and there is no Chicago equivalent.

elephant-polo.how: Elephant polo requires elephants and is played in Nepal, Thailand and India; none are available in the Chicago area.

bobsled.how: There is no bobsled track in the Chicago area; the nearest are Lake Placid, New York, and Park City, Utah.

piano.how: PianoForte Piano Performance Meet Up holds regular piano meetups in Chicago, and online piano lessons are listed for the city.

capoeira.how: Axé Capoeira Chicago teaches adult, family and samba classes in West Town and advertises a $39 two-week introductory offer; Gingarte and Capoeira Angola FICA also hold Chicago classes.

ten-pin-bowling.how: About a dozen bowling alleys remain in the city, including Fireside Bowl (Logan Square) and Timber Lanes (North Center), plus Lucky Strike and 10Pin downtown.

glassblowing.how: Chicago Glass Collective lists glass blowing and blown-glass ornament classes (torch-based ornament workshop has no prerequisites); Ignite Glass Studios in Pilsen teaches furnace glassblowing.

lampworking.how: Chicago Glass Collective lists Flameworking & Beadmaking classes and short Dabble! torch sessions.

filmmaking.how: Chicago Filmmakers runs adult classes in digital filmmaking, cinematography and lighting, editing and screenwriting.

vr-gaming.how: Redline VR rents VR headsets by the hour with games such as Beat Saber and runs VR escape rooms.

homebrewing-beer.how: CHAOS (Chicago Homebrew Alchemists of Suds) provides a shared brewhouse at 2417 W Hubbard with a 45-day trial membership and public monthly meetings.

weaving.how: The Chicago Weaving School in Irving Park teaches loom and basket weaving; The Weaving Workshop in Pilsen teaches basketry and off-loom weaving.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Chicagoland Games (Dice Dojo) lists weekly events for Warhammer and other miniatures games with play space.

bharatanatyam.how: Soham Dance Space (922 N Damen Ave) and Natya Dance Theatre list Bharatanatyam training; Natraj Dance Academy teaches it at north and northwest suburban locations.

tabla.how: Sandip Burman teaches tabla lessons in person in Chicagoland through The World Music Foundation, with tabla available to borrow.

parkour.how: Kinetic Mobility Arts (Ian Patete) posts weekly outdoor parkour classes at Humboldt Park and Ward Park with a first-class coupon.

amateur-radio.how: Chicago Suburban Radio Association (W9SW) meets monthly in Westchester and Ham Radio Chicago (W9HRC) offers entry-level license classes and test sessions.

trading-cards.how: Chicagoland Games Dice Dojo in Edgewater hosts Magic: The Gathering prereleases and a Pokemon league; Good Games Chicago in Lincoln Park runs Magic and Pokemon league nights.

pub-trivia.how: Weekly trivia runs at bars such as The Globe Pub (Tuesdays), Ramova Theatre Taproom (Sundays) and Hopleaf Bar.

taiko.how: Tsukasa Taiko at the Japanese American Service Committee ran introductory taiko classes and Kaiju Daiko lists amateur classes, but only dated (2006-2010) listings were found.

sauna.how: Eastend (Fulton Market) and Contrast Hot + Cold (738 N Milwaukee Ave) offer infrared sauna sessions; gyms such as Life Time River North have cedarwood and steam saunas.

cold-plunge.how: Contrast Hot + Cold offers community or private-room cold plunge sessions paired with sauna; Eastend sells drop-in contrast therapy.

yoga.how: Many studios offer drop-in and membership yoga, e.g. Big Shoulders Yoga in Bucktown, Yoga Six and Half Moon Yoga in the South Loop.

pilates.how: Better Posture Pilates (West Loop) and Pilates Center of Chicago run reformer and mat classes; Centered Chicago and Half Moon Yoga combine yoga and mat Pilates.

running-club.how: The Chicago Area Runners Association (CARA) runs free weekday group runs, run crews, a Beginner 5K training program and marathon training.

temple-activities.how: Midwest Buddhist Temple in Chicago holds services and meditation sessions and welcomes visitors.

stamp-collecting.how: The Chicago Philatelic Society (founded 1886) holds monthly meetings, mostly over Zoom with an in-person November meeting, and runs the annual CHICAGOPEX stamp show in Itasca.

geocaching.how: GONIL is the Chicago-area geocaching organisation that has held Cache-apalooza, cache-in-trash-out and picnic events at forest preserves such as Schiller Woods.

orchestra.how: The Chicago Citywide Orchestra is an all-volunteer orchestra of amateur and retired musicians inviting players with their own instruments; Music Institute of Chicago runs a Community Symphony in Winnetka.

massage.how: The Spa at Virgin Hotels (203 N Wabash) and Spa Space (West Loop) offer massages, and the Chicago School of Massage Therapy student clinic offered 60-minute massages.

beekeeping-honey.how: Garfield Park Conservatory Alliance ran a Beginning Beekeeping class ($70) leading to its volunteer beekeeper program; Chicago Honey Co-op has run public classes at a rooftop apiary.

bouldering.how: Mission Cliffs (Touchstone Climbing) has a 2,000 sq ft bouldering area with day passes and intro-to-climbing classes.

chinese-calligraphy.how: Saint Mary's Chinese Language School in Chinatown runs recurring beginner and intermediate Chinese calligraphy classes; the Japanese American Association of Northern California holds Japanese calligraphy workshops.

embroidery.how: Maker Studio in Hayes Valley lists a Sewing Social Club session with an intro to embroidery, and other embroidery workshops are offered around the Bay.

nature-guided-walks.how: GGNRA offers ranger-led walks, and Meetup groups run weekly nature walks at Fort Funston and the Presidio.

intertidal-walking.how: GGNRA lists tide pooling among its visitor activities, with sites such as Mori Point.
intertidal-walking.venue: Golden Gate National Recreation Area (Mori Point)

breakdancing.how: Beginner hip hop dance classes run in Mission Bay and Potrero Hill studios, but no breaking-specific class was confirmed.

allotment-gardening.how: Community volunteer gardening runs at Alemany Farm through Nature in the City, and an East Bay permaculture guild meets at PLACE, but personal allotment plots were not confirmed.

rug-tufting.how: Rug tufting workshops run daily at studios at 575 Sutter St (Union Square) and 360 Ritch St (SoMa).

board-games.how: Gamescape SF is a Divisadero Street board game store and event space with weekly game nights; Victory Point Cafe in Berkeley offers open board game play for a small fee.

chess.how: The Mechanics' Institute Chess Club at 57 Post St hosts USCF/FIDE-rated tournaments, monthly socials and classes from beginner to advanced; Pawn Shop Chess Club SF also meets free at Alamo Square.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Gamescape SF stocks D&D and Pathfinder and hosts RPG nights, while Meetup groups (SF LGBT D&D Group, Bay Area Table Top RPG Network) run Adventurers League and Pathfinder campaigns.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: Hands On Gourmet in Dogpatch runs hands-on cooking classes such as handmade ravioli, and other SF hosts list pasta and dumpling classes.

sushi-making.how: Breakthrough Sushi holds sushi-making dinner classes several evenings a week at Hotel Kabuki in Japantown.

woodworking.how: Noisebridge hackerspace runs Woodhacking Mondays (all skill levels) and fabrication safety classes; equipment is free to use with donations welcome.

3d-printing.how: Noisebridge teaches a 3D printing class every other Sunday and members can use the printers; equipment is free with donations welcome.

amateur-radio.how: A San Mateo Radio Club monthly meeting (Southern Peninsula Emergency Communications System) is listed on Meetup.

coding-meetups.how: Noisebridge hosts weekly software-infrastructure and hacking nights and Meetup lists groups such as SF Rust Study Group and Hackers/Founders.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Noisebridge hosts Circuit Hacking Monday and an Arduino for Total Newbies class, with soldering and electronics benches open to the public.

game-development-jams.how: SF Bay Area Game Jamming & Game Design and Noisebridge (weekly Gamebridge and a monthly Godot meetup) run game development meetups.

laser-cutting.how: Noisebridge runs laser cutter safety certification sessions on Sundays (limited availability).

arcade-games.how: Emporium Arcade Bar in Alamo Square is an arcade bar with classic machines and events.

escape-rooms.how: Lore Speakeasy and Escape Room in the Inner Mission operates an escape room alongside game events.

mahjong.how: Bay Area Mahjong Meetup holds Mahjong Monday drop-ins at Mamahuhu in Noe Valley and Marin Mahjong runs free social play at libraries and rec centres.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Gamescape SF has a Miniature Games department stocking Warhammer 40K, Age of Sigmar and Kill Team and runs a weekly game-night schedule.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Mission Bowling Club in the Inner Mission and Lucky Strike in Mission Bay run bowling leagues and community nights.

chocolate-making.how: Chocolate classes and tasting events (e.g. a Recchiuti chocolate experience, Manny's chocolate club) are listed, but no bean-to-bar course was confirmed.

mixology.how: Elixir in Mission Dolores and The Alembic in the Haight run cocktail classes, including "Great Cocktails: An Introduction to Mixology".

dim-sum-making.how: Hands On Gourmet in Dogpatch lists a Dim Sum Cooking Class covering soup dumplings and more.

latte-art.how: Telescope Coffee in SoMa runs espresso and milk steaming classes, which cover the barista skills behind latte art.

wine-tasting-wset.how: Mechanics' Institute in Union Square runs a multi-session Wine Appreciation Series, and wine dinners and tastings are listed across the city.

art-gallery.how: SFMOMA, 151 Third St, houses modern and contemporary art galleries; adult admission is $30 and under-19s are free.

language-exchange.how: SpanFran runs Spanish/French language exchanges at Muddy Waters Cafe and several Meetup groups run Japanese, Mandarin, German and French exchanges.

museums.how: SFMOMA, 151 Third St, is one of many major museums; adult admission is $30 and under-19s are free.

science-museum.how: The California Academy of Sciences in Golden Gate Park combines an aquarium, planetarium, rainforest and natural history museum; Chabot Space & Science Center in Oakland adds free Friday and Saturday telescope nights.

toastmasters.how: Toastmasters clubs such as Townsend Toastmasters, Oakland Warehouse Toastmasters and Peninsula Toastmasters hold regular meetings listed on Meetup.

hackathons.how: Hackathons are listed on Meetup, e.g. an ODSC AI x Nebius hackathon, alongside weekly civic-tech hack nights.

robotics-arduino.how: Noisebridge runs Arduino for Total Newbies and a robotics meetup that requires no prior experience.

cosplay.how: Ace Makerspace in Oakland offers costume-making workshops and an SF anime club meetup lists cosplay guests, but no dedicated cosplay club was confirmed.

esports-gaming.how: Noisebridge hosts fortnightly fighting-game nights (School of Melee) and Meetup lists local gaming groups, but no dedicated esports venue was confirmed.

go-weiqi.how: San Francisco Go Club holds Play Go and Socialize sessions on Fridays and Sundays, and Tri-Valley Go Players meet weekly in Pleasanton.

pub-trivia.how: San Francisco Pub Quiz runs trivia on Mondays at The Sycamore and Wednesdays at The Willows; Oakland Trivia Night meets at Ghost Town.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Hands On Gourmet in Dogpatch and other hosts run baking classes covering sourdough starters, challah and pastry.

homebrewing-beer.how: Mercurius Beer Lab in the Inner Mission teaches beer brewing classes (Brew It Yourself: Beer Making at Home, and a full-grain 102 course).

tea-ceremony.how: Shumei San Francisco Center runs Japanese tea meditation sessions and ChaTo in Japantown hosts Japanese tea tastings, but a formal chado school was not confirmed.

sourdough-baking.how: Sourdough Starter and Sip & Sourdough baking workshops are listed in SoMa and at the Blue Heron Boathouse in Golden Gate Park.

whisky-tasting.how: The Whisky Shop in Union Square holds frequent single-malt and bourbon tasting events.

birdwatching.how: EcoCenter at Heron's Head Park in the Central Waterfront lists guided bird walks (e.g. Birds, Bay and Belonging), and GGNRA lists birding among visitor activities.

trading-cards.how: Gamescape SF has a trading card games department (Magic: The Gathering, Pokemon, Lorcana, One Piece) and hosts prerelease events; a Magic Casual Players Meetup meets Sundays.

archival-research.how: The Koshland San Francisco History Center on the 6th floor of the Main Library holds the city archives, manuscripts, photographs, maps and newspapers for public research.
archival-research.venue: San Francisco History Center, SF Main Library

book-club.how: Many Meetup book clubs meet monthly, such as SF Saturday Book Club, SF "not quite a book club" and Oakland Bookclub.
book-club.venue: SF "not quite a book club" Book Club

creative-writing.how: San Francisco Public Library hosts a workshop on writing memoir, short story and essay at the Main Library, and Union Arts Center runs book-writing classes.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The Japanese American Association of Northern California in Japantown hosts regular cultural workshops, e.g. Japanese calligraphy.
cultural-heritage-centres.venue: Japanese American Association of Northern California

history-walks.how: San Francisco Historical Society operates a walking-tours programme (sfhistory.org/tours) and Meetup runs neighbourhood history tours such as Duboce Park Victorians.

german-language.how: SF German Stammtisch holds monthly German-speaking meetups at Paprika and Salesforce Park, but no formal German course was confirmed.

japanese-language.how: SF Japanese Language Exchange meets Wednesdays and a Berkeley Japanese-English exchange meets Tuesdays, but no formal course was confirmed.

spanish-language.how: Spanish-English language exchanges run in SF and Berkeley (SpanFran at Muddy Waters Cafe, Berkeley Language Exchange), but no formal Spanish course was confirmed.

philosophy-cafe.how: SF Philosophy Club and San Francisco Philosophy Reading Group hold paper and reading discussions, and a Socrates Cafe runs online.

poetry-slam.how: Poetry in SF Chinatown holds a monthly 3rd Saturday poetry event and Meetup lists poetry-inclusive open mics.

public-lectures.how: San Francisco Historical Society runs a History Live! lecture series and events schedule.

wartime-history.how: Golden Gate National Recreation Area manages WWII-era sites including Fort Point and Battery East.

coastal-cleanup.how: Refuse Refuse - San Francisco Cleanups runs weekly KEEP Ocean Beach cleans and monthly Crissy Field and Fort Miley cleanup days; Save the Bay also runs volunteer shoreline restoration.

cold-plunge.how: East Bay Dipping Society holds group ocean dips and Alameda Open Water Swimming meets weekly, but no dedicated ice-bath venue was confirmed.

meetups.how: Meetup lists many hobby groups and events across San Francisco and the East Bay.

fishing.how: The Golden Gate Angling & Casting Club in Golden Gate Park runs a Learn to Fly Fish program (multi-level), casting programs and club fishing outings.
fishing.venue: Golden Gate Angling & Casting Club (Anglers Lodge)

blacksmithing.how: The Crucible in West Oakland has a Blacksmithing department with 3-hour taster sessions and multi-week Blacksmithing I and II classes.

mushroom-foraging.how: The Mycological Society of San Francisco runs single-day mushroom walks and camping forays for identification and collection.

genealogy.how: The California Genealogical Society runs genealogy research classes, workshops and a research library in Berkeley and online.

french-language.how: Alliance Francaise de San Francisco offers onsite and online French classes for adults, kids and teens at all levels, plus DELF/DALF exam prep.

poker.how: Oaks Card Club in Emeryville is a 24-hour card room spreading Texas Hold'em and other poker games plus tournaments; Lucky Chances in Colma is another.

birds-of-prey-watching.how: The Golden Gate Raptor Observatory staffs Hawk Hill in the Marin Headlands during the autumn raptor migration, with public hawk talks, banding and raptor-release events.

orienteering.how: The Bay Area Orienteering Club holds regular orienteering meets (for example at Tilden Regional Park and Joaquin Miller Park) with a first-event guide for beginners.

acting.how: Berkeley Rep School of Theatre runs fall, winter, spring and summer acting classes and workshops for youth, teens and adults.
acting.venue: Berkeley Repertory Theatre School of Theatre

comic-collecting.how: Comix Experience is a long-running comic and graphic-novel shop (since 1989) with weekly preorders, creator events and a graphic novel club.

windsurfing.how: Cal Sailing Club at the Berkeley Marina teaches windsurfing (beginner lessons, ratings and club gear) on San Francisco Bay.

kitesurfing.how: Boardsports California offers kiteboarding and kitesurfing lessons and rentals from bases in Alameda, San Francisco and San Mateo.

yoga.how: Berkeley Yoga Center (open since 1997) runs ongoing classes for beginners through advanced practitioners.

lawn-bowls.how: The San Francisco Lawn Bowling Club has played on its green in Golden Gate Park since 1901 and advertises free lessons.

support-groups.how: NAMI San Francisco runs free peer-led support groups and classes for people with mental health conditions and their families (English, Spanish, Cantonese).

volunteering.how: The San Francisco-Marin Food Bank takes volunteers for warehouse and community shifts; sign-up is online.

heritage-trails.how: The Barbary Coast Trail is a self-guided walking route of sidewalk medallions and arrows linking historic sites, with audio tours and guides.

community-gardening.how: Alemany Farm in the Excelsior holds community workdays where volunteers garden and harvest.

hydroponics-urban-farming.how: Alemany Farm is a volunteer-run soil-based urban farm in San Francisco with workshops; hydroponic setups were not shown on the page.

trading-card-games.how: Games of Berkeley sells TCG singles and hosts events and open gaming for RPGs, wargames and trading card games.

sitar.how: The Ali Akbar College of Music in San Rafael teaches North Indian classical sitar, sarode and tabla in group classes each term.

temple-activities.how: San Francisco Zen Center (City Center) offers zazen meditation, chanting, dharma talks, classes and retreats, plus beginner resources.

sake-making.how: Sequoia Sake brews sake in San Francisco from locally grown rice and runs a public tasting room; brewing classes were not shown.

mountain-biking.how: Mount Tamalpais in Marin is regarded as the birthplace of mountain biking and has many trails open to cyclists.

moocs.how: Coursera and similar platforms offer online courses and certificates from any location, including San Francisco.

dog-parks.how: Fort Funston in the Golden Gate National Recreation Area is widely used as an off-leash dog park, the only GGNRA park allowing off-leash dogs.

kite-flying.how: Marina Green is a 74-acre waterfront lawn beside the Bay where people fly kites.

speedcubing.how: The World Cube Association lists regular speedcubing competitions in Berkeley (for example Berkeley Fall 2026 and monthly weekday events) and nearby San Mateo.

pilates.how: Club Pilates Alameda runs Reformer Pilates classes with a full weekly schedule.

cnc-machining.how: The Crucible's Machine Shop teaches lathes, milling machines and drill presses with open lab time; CNC-specific teaching was not shown.

clay-sculpture.how: The Crucible has a Ceramics department with 3-hour taster workshops and longer clay classes.

tai-chi.how: The Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco in Chinatown listed weekly Chen-style Tai Chi classes taught by Master Debbie Au (page may be dated).
tai-chi.venue: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco

geocaching.how: East Bay Regional Park District publishes geocaching guidelines and permits caches in its parks across Alameda and Contra Costa counties.

rc-aircraft.how: East Bay Regional Park District allows model airplanes (gliders) and radio-controlled model boats only at designated locations; the Model Mariners Club is the contact for model boats.

vinyl-records.how: Amoeba Music sells new and used records at its Berkeley (original, 1990) and San Francisco (1997) stores.

mentoring.how: 826 Valencia in the Mission runs after-school programs, workshops and in-school projects staffed by volunteer tutors and mentors for students aged 6-18.

butterfly-watching.how: San Bruno Mountain State and County Park, next to San Francisco's southern edge, is habitat for rare butterflies including the Mission blue and has summit trails.
butterfly-watching.venue: San Bruno Mountain State and County Park

rodeo.how: The Grand National Rodeo is held annually each autumn at the Cow Palace on the San Francisco-Daly City boundary, with professional rodeo events plus trick riding.

whale-watching.how: Oceanic Society runs whale-watching and wildlife expeditions to the Farallon Islands from the San Francisco Bay Area.

onsen.how: Kabuki Springs & Spa is a Japanese-inspired bathhouse with communal baths in Japantown, an approximation of an onsen using heated pools rather than a volcanic source.

hot-spring-bathing.how: Kabuki Springs & Spa describes a Japanese-style bathhouse with natural thermal spring soaking in the city; the natural springs of Calistoga and Sonoma are well beyond 30 km.

snow-skiing.how: No snow or ski slopes in the Bay Area; nearest ski resorts are around Lake Tahoe, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours by car.

dog-sledding.how: Mild coastal climate with no snow; nearest dog sledding is around Lake Tahoe/Truckee, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours by car.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers in the region; the nearest are on Mount Shasta, roughly 5 hours north, or in the high Sierra.

white-water-rafting.how: No suitable whitewater rivers in the metro area; nearest commercial rafting is on the American River near Coloma, roughly 2 to 2.5 hours away.

hot-air-ballooning.how: Ballooning is not offered in the metro area; nearest commercial flights are over Napa Valley, roughly 1.25 hours north.

volcano-boarding.how: No suitable volcano nearby; the standard site is Cerro Negro in Nicaragua, a long-haul flight away.

cheese-rolling.how: Single annual event held at Cooper's Hill in Gloucestershire, England; nothing equivalent in the Bay Area.

buzkashi.how: Traditional Central Asian sport played mainly in Afghanistan; no regular play in the Bay Area.

mountaineering.how: No alpine terrain in the metro area; nearest mountaineering is in the Sierra Nevada, roughly 4 to 5 hours by car.

archery.how: San Francisco Rec & Park runs a free first-come public archery range in Golden Gate Park at 47th Ave and Fulton St; bows can be rented at the nearby SF Archery Pro Shop, and Palomo Archery holds fortnightly Friday-night sessions.

cricket.how: Bay Area Competitive Cricket and San Ramon Tri-Valley Cricket host weekend practice and league games listed on Meetup, part of a large Bay Area amateur cricket scene.

fencing.how: Halberstadt Fencers' Club in the Mission runs an introduction to fencing course covering foil, epee and sabre with equipment provided, followed by beginner classes per weapon.

ice-skating.how: Yerba Buena Ice Skating & Bowling Center in Yerba Buena Gardens has a public ice rink open for recreational skating, with skate rental.
ice-skating.venue: Yerba Buena Ice Skating and Bowling Center

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Touchstone's Mission Cliffs has top-rope and lead walls plus bouldering, with classes and private lessons; day passes are listed at $30-35.

judo.how: San Francisco Judo Institute, a non-profit dojo on Taraval Street, and Soko Joshi Judo Club run judo classes for ages 8 to adults.

taekwondo.how: Korean Martial Arts Center on Ocean Ave teaches taekwondo to kids and adults, and SF Martial Arts Club at the African American Art & Culture Complex offers taekwondo alongside boxing and muay thai.

capoeira.how: ABADA-Capoeira San Francisco in the Mission offers a free fundamentals class for new adults on the first Tuesday of each month, and ABADA-Capoeira Oakland holds drop-in classes.

ultimate-frisbee.how: Pickup ultimate groups such as South Bay and Peninsula Pickup Ultimate (Belmont) and social frisbee meetups in San Francisco run regular open games.
ultimate-frisbee.venue: South Bay and Peninsula Pickup Ultimate

camping.how: East Bay Regional Parks run family tent sites, cabins, group and backpacking campsites bookable via ReserveAmerica, including at Anthony Chabot above Oakland.
camping.venue: East Bay Regional Park District campgrounds

dragon-boat.how: Bay Area Dragons (Foster City) offer free weekend dragon boat lessons, and Oakland Renegades train at the Alameda Grand Street ramp with the first three sessions free.

kayaking.how: City Kayak at Pier 40, South Beach Harbor, runs seatouring kayak and surfski classes and rents kayaks for the bay and McCovey Cove.

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: City Kayak at Pier 40 teaches a Beginning SUP lesson and rents stand-up paddleboards.

rowing.how: The Dolphin Club and South End Rowing Club, both on Aquatic Park Cove, run member rowing programmes with an introductory orientation, and Open Water Rowing Center in Sausalito offers a beginner clinic.

curling.how: San Francisco Bay Area Curling Club runs 90-minute learn-to-curl sessions at its dedicated Oakland facility (8450 Enterprise Way), no experience needed.
curling.venue: San Francisco Bay Area Curling Club

horse-riding.how: City-run Oakland Stables on Skyline Blvd offers riding lessons and training, and Miwok Livery in Mill Valley runs trail rides in the Marin Headlands.

hang-gliding.how: Fort Funston's coastal cliffs are a long-established hang gliding site, flown from the old Nike site above the beach.

stargazing.how: Chabot Space & Science Center in the Oakland hills holds free public telescope viewings on Friday and Saturday evenings, weather permitting, using three historic telescopes.

guitar.how: San Francisco Community Music Center offers a Beginning Group Guitar for Adults class with no prerequisites, plus private lessons on guitar-family instruments.

choir.how: San Francisco Community Music Center's Anything Goes Chorus I welcomes singers with little to no experience, and San Francisco Gay Men's Chorus runs auditions each season.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Circus Center in Cole Valley offers adult classes in aerial, acrobatics, flying trapeze, contortion, juggling and clown, including a beginners track.

ballet.how: San Francisco Ballet School runs adult classes from absolute beginner level, in person at 455 Franklin St and on Zoom.

tango.how: La Bruja in Berkeley and Come Dance Marin run weekly tango classes and milongas, and San Francisco Bay Area Tango hosts a beginner-friendly milonga.

urban-sketching.how: SF Sketchers organise regular outdoor sketching meetups such as Dock of the Bay Sketching around the Bay Area.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: Sketchboard Co. runs weekly nude figure drawing sessions at Monument in San Francisco and Oakland Grove, and Abrams Claghorn Gallery in Albany holds Figure Drawing Fridays.

oil-painting.how: Art School of SF Bay in San Rafael runs a 16-session Oil and Acrylic Painting course.

candle-making.how: Arts & Crafts for Team on Ritch St runs a 45-minute Botanical Soy Candle Making workshop for beginners.

glassblowing.how: Public Glass in Bayview offers beginner hot-glass workshops such as Play With Fire (3 hours, no experience needed).

lampworking.how: Public Glass in Bayview lists an intro flameworking class alongside its hot-glass workshops.

pottery-wheel.how: Richmond Art Center runs eight-week beginning and intermediate wheel courses.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Richmond Art Center runs Evening and Afternoon Hand & Wheel courses combining handbuilding and throwing.

sailing.how: Modern Sailing School & Club in Sausalito and Berkeley teaches ASA 101 and later courses on 30-32 ft keelboats over two weekends or four weekdays.

keelboat-yachting.how: Tradewinds Sailing runs a three-day ASA 101 Basic Keelboat course on Catalina Capri 22s on San Francisco Bay, with three students per instructor.

scuba-diving.how: San Francisco SCUBA Schools offers PADI Open Water courses with pool sessions in Pacifica, and Pinnacles Dive Center in Marin certifies in San Francisco and Monterey.

piano.how: San Francisco Conservatory of Music's Adult Extension Division runs a 13-week Class Piano I & II, and Blue Bear School of Music offers adult group classes and private lessons at Fort Mason and Mission Bay.
piano.venue: San Francisco Conservatory of Music Adult Extension

improv-comedy.how: San Francisco Comedy College on Post St teaches improv, sketch and stand-up classes, and The Improv's Bayfront Theater has listed improv courses.

stand-up-comedy.how: San Francisco Comedy College on Post St teaches stand-up courses, and a veteran who performs at the Punch Line and Cobb's taught a four-week stand-up class in Oakland.

surfing-ocean.how: Ocean Beach is one of the Bay Area's top surf spots with several surf shops, and guided beginner lessons with boards and wetsuits run from near Judah St.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: Indian Rock Park in Berkeley has long been a practice site for rock climbing and bouldering, used by Sierra Club climbers since the 1930s.

hiking.how: Mount Tamalpais in Marin has over 100 miles of trails and fire roads with bay and ocean views, and the Presidio has more than 24 miles of hiking trails.

trail-running.how: Mount Tamalpais fire roads and trails are widely used for running, and the Dipsea Race from Mill Valley to Stinson Beach is the oldest cross-country trail race in the US.

pickleball.how: Bay Pickleball hosts PickleFun sessions in San Francisco, and Marin Pickleball for All runs open play at indoor and outdoor courts.

bobsled.how: Requires a dedicated ice track; none exists in the Bay Area, and the nearest US tracks are at Park City, Utah and Lake Placid, New York.

ski-jumping.how: Requires snow-covered jumping hills; none exist in the Bay Area, and the nearest facilities are around Lake Tahoe or farther east.

snowboarding.how: No snow at sea level in the Bay Area; resorts in the Lake Tahoe area in the Sierra Nevada are roughly 3.5 to 4 hours' drive away.

snow-sculpture.how: The Bay Area has no snow season; the nearest snowfall is in the Sierra Nevada around Lake Tahoe, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours' drive away.

big-wall-climbing.how: The Bay Area has no big walls; the nearest are in Yosemite Valley (El Capitan), roughly 4 hours' drive away.

camel-racing.how: No camel racing tradition or tracks exist in the Bay Area; the sport is centred in the Gulf states, Australia and Central Asia.

elephant-polo.how: Requires working elephants, which are not kept for recreation in the Bay Area; the sport is played in Nepal, Thailand and India.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Mangroves do not grow naturally this far north on the California coast; bay and salt-marsh sea kayaking is available instead.

salsa-bachata.how: Golden City Dance Collective on Mission St runs progressive bachata and salsa classes on Mondays with no partner or experience needed, and Dance Fridays at Space 550 offers beginner bachata and salsa lessons before its social.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Lindy in the Park holds a free beginner swing lesson on Sundays behind the de Young Museum in Golden Gate Park, and The 9:20 Special on Sutter St is the Bay Area's largest Lindy Hop venue.
swing-lindy-hop.venue: Lindy in the Park (Golden Gate Park)

flamenco.how: Theatre Flamenco of San Francisco, founded 1966, runs weekly flamenco classes for all levels at 670 S. Van Ness Ave, and Studio Danza on Mission St also offers flamenco classes.

irish-dance.how: Murphy Irish Dancers teach beginners from age 4 to adults in San Francisco and on the Peninsula, and the Irish Center SF lists several schools including Healy and Kennelly.

pole-dance.how: Songbird Dance Studio on Fern St offers a Pole Foundation Level 1 class, and Empress Ouroboros on Laguna St runs beginner pole choreography.

tabla.how: Ali Akbar College of Music in San Rafael teaches tabla in the North Indian classical tradition in person and online, with group sessions each term.

kathak.how: Chitresh Das Institute teaches Kathak at all levels including beginners, with Fall 2026 classes in Cupertino, San Mateo and San Ramon and its office in San Francisco.

filmmaking.how: Bay Area Video Coalition offers short courses on cinematography, DaVinci Resolve colour correction and audio post-production through learn.bavc.org.

knitting-crochet.how: Knit One Crochet, Too, Richmond Knit & Crochet (San Francisco) and East Bay Knitting Community run regular open knit and crochet meetups.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Metalworks SF in North Beach teaches jewelry making to beginners and experienced makers, and Richmond Art Center runs a six-session Introduction to Silversmithing course.

film-photography-darkroom.how: Low Light Darkroom, a volunteer-run nonprofit lab in Union Square, offers studio time for developing film and printing, and Sixth Street Photography Workshop runs a weekly darkroom workshop at SOMArts.

music-production.how: Garnish Music Production in San Francisco and Blue Bear School of Music offer music production and DJ courses, with CourseHorse listing further classes.

dj-turntablism.how: Blue Bear School of Music runs group and private DJ classes taught by local DJs, and DJ4LIFE Academy in SoMa offers three levels of DJ instruction.

rugby.how: San Francisco Fog RFC, an inclusive club in the Northern California Rugby Football Union, runs a free beginner crash course on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and San Francisco Golden Gate RFC fields several teams.
rugby.venue: San Francisco Fog Rugby Football Club

ice-hockey.how: Oakland Ice Center (Sharks Ice) runs adult beginner and intermediate hockey classes feeding into the Sharks Ice Adult Hockey League, plus drop-in pickup and stick time.

taiko.how: San Francisco Taiko Dojo, the oldest taiko school in the US, runs beginning adult and child taiko classes with registration through its website.

tap-dance.how: CourseHorse lists San Francisco tap classes at all levels, the San Francisco Tap Festival at Dance Mission Theater welcomes adult beginners, and the City of South San Francisco runs an adult tap course.
tap-dance.venue: San Francisco Tap Festival (Dance Mission Theater)

printmaking-screenprint.how: ClassBento lists San Francisco screen printing classes at around $110 per session, and RayKo's print studio has hosted screen printing teaching.

bookbinding.how: San Francisco Center for the Book at 375 Rhode Island St teaches bookbinding and letterpress, including a three-hour Introduction to Bookbinding, and Graphic Arts Workshop has run two-day hardcover bookbinding workshops.
bookbinding.venue: San Francisco Center for the Book

stained-glass.how: Maker Studio on Octavia St runs a beginner three-hour stained glass workshop, and Cradle of the Sun Stained Glass is a long-running studio teaching cutting, foiling and soldering.

leatherwork.how: Richmond Art Center runs a belt-making class (cut, tool, stain and bevel heavy leather), and Timmy May's in Alameda offers leather workshops such as a valet tray.

skateboarding.how: Potrero del Sol skatepark (about 16,000 sq ft with a bowl, snake run and street section) and SoMa West Skate Plaza are free public skateparks, and San Francisco Skate Club teaches kids.

watercolour-painting.how: Art School of SF Bay in San Rafael runs a 10-session Watercolor 101, and Richmond Art Center offers beginning and intermediate watercolor courses.

photography.how: Digital Photo Academy runs camera-controls classes and in-the-field photo workshops at the Ferry Building, Chinatown, the Embarcadero and Golden Gate Park.

padel.how: Bay Padel runs indoor padel and pickleball courts on Treasure Island with online court reservations; Park Padel also ran public courts at Embarcadero Plaza.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: San Francisco GAA runs Gaelic football, hurling and camogie clubs (Na Fianna, Pearse Og, St. Joseph's, Eire Og) playing at Pairc na nGael on Treasure Island.

australian-rules-football.how: The Golden Gate Australian Football League fields the Roos (men) and Iron Maidens (women), training in San Francisco, Oakland and Palo Alto, with non-contact intro sessions for beginners.

perfumery.how: One-hour custom perfume blending classes (30 essential oils, bottle to take home) are listed at 405 Sansome St, with other fragrance workshops at hotels and studios.

ikebana.how: City College of San Francisco Extension teaches a Saturday Seasonal Ikebana class at Ocean Campus, and Ikebana International Chapter 31 holds monthly demonstrations.
ikebana.venue: City College of San Francisco Extension (Ocean Campus)

etching.how: Richmond Art Center offers beginner drypoint and solar etching classes with an etching press, and CCA runs etching and electro-etching print courses at its San Francisco campus.

vr-gaming.how: Sandbox VR has a downtown location with four full-body-tracking VR rooms for group games, and Immersive Gamebox operates at Stonestown Galleria.

beekeeping-honey.how: San Francisco Beekeepers Association (est. 1976) meets monthly at the Randall Museum, and members teach beginner beekeeping classes at Garden for the Environment.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: The SF SPCA recruits adult volunteers (info session, six-month commitment) for dog walking, cat socialising, fostering and mobile vaccine clinics.

weaving.how: Richmond Art Center has offered tapestry and frame-loom weaving classes, though no currently scheduled session was confirmed.

whisky-society.how: The Scotch Malt Whisky Society hosts San Francisco member and guest tastings (e.g. at Elixir in the Mission), and the St. Andrew's Society runs Whisky Wednesdays tastings.
whisky-society.venue: Scotch Malt Whisky Society tastings at Elixir

sake-tasting.how: Fifth Taste Sake School runs WSET and Sake Sommelier Association courses in Berkeley and Emeryville, and two-hour Sake 101 tasting classes are listed on Cortland Avenue.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Preserved Goods in Oakland teaches two-hour kombucha classes with all supplies provided, and SF Public Library and 18 Reasons have run kombucha and SCOBY workshops.

ctf-security.how: Pacific Hackers and DevSecCon SF Bay Area run CTF events and beginner CTF sessions, but they are occasional rather than a standing weekly venue.

origami.how: Origami Palooza is an annual Japantown festival with free folding and paid master classes, and SF Public Library holds origami sessions; no standing weekly class was confirmed.

watchmaking-horology.how: Horological Society of New York's Horology 101-103 courses have been taught in San Francisco at Shreve & Co., and Worn & Wound x DIY Watch Club ran a build-your-own-watch class at Fort Mason; both are occasional.

stamp-collecting.how: San Francisco Pacific Philatelic Society meets monthly at the San Francisco Main Library, and Golden Gate Stamp Club meets twice monthly.

bharatanatyam.how: Nava Dance Theatre has run all-levels drop-in Bharatanatyam classes at Dance Mission Theatre in San Francisco and at Shawl Anderson Dance Center in Berkeley, and several academies teach on the Peninsula.

lion-dance.how: LionDanceME trains and performs lion dance from a Chinatown studio and Portsmouth Square, with lion dance clubs at five city high schools.

coffee-roasting.how: Beginner coffee roasting workshops (about 90 minutes, take home your own roast) are listed on a Marin County patio, and Sightglass runs brewing classes in SoMa.
coffee-roasting.venue: Bay Area coffee roasting class (Marin County)

gamelan.how: Gamelan Sekar Jaya runs Balinese gong kebyar music and dance classes at its banjar community centre on Shattuck Avenue in Berkeley, with beginner series and drop-ins on a sliding scale.

pet-adoption.how: Maddie's Pet Adoption Center at the SF SPCA Mission campus offers walk-in, same-day cat and dog adoptions for adults with photo ID and proof of address.

massage.how: Kabuki Springs & Spa offers Eastern, Swedish and prenatal massage alongside its Japanese-inspired bathhouse.

pedal-boating.how: Rowboats and pedal boats can be rented at the boathouse on Stow Lake (Blue Heron Lake) in Golden Gate Park.

freshwater-fishing.how: Golden Gate Angling & Casting Club is based at Anglers Lodge and its fly casting pools in Golden Gate Park, which are still in use; actual freshwater fishing is mostly in lakes and reservoirs around the Bay.
freshwater-fishing.venue: Golden Gate Angling & Casting Club (Anglers Lodge)

parkour.how: SF Parkour has listed free monthly beginner 'Urban Ninja' sessions with rotating locations including the Embarcadero and UC Berkeley, but no dedicated gym in the city was confirmed.

meditation.how: San Francisco Zen Center's City Center is an urban temple offering zazen practice, beginner resources and a calendar of classes and retreats.

sandboarding-desert.how: No desert dunes in the metro area; the nearest sandboarding is at Oceano Dunes about 4 hours' drive south, or desert dunes in Southern California.

luge.how: No luge or bobsled track in Northern California; nearest dedicated tracks are in Park City, Utah, or Lake Placid, New York.

canyoning.how: Canyoning needs slot canyons with flowing water, which the Bay Area lacks; the nearest guided canyoning is in the Sierra Nevada foothills, around 3 hours' drive.

outdoor-skydiving.how: Skydive Dubai runs tandem skydives, AFF courses and USPA licence training from the Palm Dropzone, with jumps over Palm Jumeirah.

zip-lining.how: XLine Dubai Marina is a 1 km urban zipline from a 170 m start height across the Marina, reaching about 80 km/h, with harness and safety gear provided.

parkour.how: XPark at Kite Beach is a large urban sports facility with parkour, skateboarding, wall climbing and calisthenics zones on a day pass.

snow-skiing.how: Ski Dubai in Mall of the Emirates has an 85 m indoor mountain with five runs (longest 400 m), a chairlift and a tow lift for skiers.

indoor-snow-play.how: Ski Dubai Snow Park beside the slopes is a 3,000 square metre indoor snow play area with sled and toboggan runs, an ice slide, climbing towers and an ice cave, plus penguin encounters.

safari.how: Dubai Safari Park offers bus and drive-through journeys past giraffes, lions, tigers and an Arabian desert area with oryx, a zoo-style safari rather than open-range wildlife.

sandboarding-desert.how: Evening desert safaris from Dubai by Arabian Adventures are illustrated with family sandboarding on the dunes alongside dune driving and camel riding; the dunes lie some distance out of the city.

birdwatching.how: Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary has three free public birding hides overlooking greater flamingos, stilts, egrets, avocets and migratory shorebirds at the head of Dubai Creek.

chocolate-making.how: Mirzam Chocolate Makers, a bean-to-bar factory in Al Quoz, runs chocolate factory tours with moulding, tasting and coffee-and-cocoa pairing workshops.

volunteering.how: Volunteers.ae is the UAE national government-backed platform listing field and virtual volunteering with public and private organisations, open to residents of all nationalities.

coastal-cleanup.how: Emirates Environmental Group (founded in Dubai in 1991) runs a Clean Up UAE campaign among its volunteer environmental projects; the page does not specify beach sites.

pet-adoption.how: K9 Friends is a Dubai-linked dog rescue that homes rescued dogs through an adoption process.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: K9 Friends lists a Get Involved page with several ways to help its rescue dogs.

temple-activities.how: The Hindu Temple in Jebel Ali (opened October 2022, with the Sikh gurudwara) hosts daily worship, festivals in its community hall and fire rituals; Krishna Mandir remains in Bur Dubai.

book-club.how: Bookends Dubai and several other Meetup book groups (Book Cellar, Dubai Bibliophiles, Iqraa Arabic Book Group) hold regular book club meetings in Dubai.

pub-trivia.how: Quiz & Chill runs social trivia nights in Dubai listed on Meetup.

netball.how: NISAA Fitness hosts ladies-only netball sessions listed on Meetup.

running-club.how: Founders Running Club Dubai and JBR Run & Pilates Club hold regular group runs listed on Meetup, and Kite Beach run clubs such as F45 Run Club meet weekly.

pilates.how: JBR Run & Pilates Club runs group Pilates sessions in Jumeirah Beach Residence, listed on Meetup.

meditation.how: Dubai Mindful Circle and other Meetup groups run mindfulness and guided meditation sessions in Dubai.

yoga.how: Dubai Outdoor Yoga & Meditation Community and Sunrise Soul Club run outdoor yoga sessions, and beach yoga events such as Dubai Yoga for Longevity meet at Jumeirah 2 Beach.

philosophy-cafe.how: Practical Philosophy Club - Dubai and PhiloLifers Dubai host philosophy discussion events listed on Meetup.

poetry-slam.how: Dubai Bibliophiles Book Club hosts poetry sessions listed on Meetup; no dedicated slam series was confirmed.

public-lectures.how: Curious Pickle runs a lecture series on psychology topics in Dubai, listed on Meetup.

meetups.how: Meetup.com lists dozens of active Dubai hobby groups, from badminton, hiking and improv to language exchange, philosophy and book clubs.

dog-sledding.how: No snow or sled-dog culture exists in the UAE; the nearest option is in cold-climate Europe or Asia, many hours away by air.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers exist in the UAE or nearby Gulf region; the nearest glacier trekking is in the Alps or Central Asia, many hours away by air.

volcano-boarding.how: No volcanoes exist in the UAE; volcano boarding is done at sites such as Cerro Negro in Nicaragua, a long-haul flight away.

white-water-rafting.how: The UAE has no perennial rivers or rapids; white water rafting requires travel abroad.

hot-spring-bathing.how: Dubai has no natural hot springs; the nearest are at Ain Al Faidha near Al Ain, roughly 1.5 hours by road.

bullfighting.how: Spanish-style bullfighting does not exist in the UAE; the only bull sport nearby is traditional bull-butting in Fujairah, about 1.5 hours by road, which is a different sport.

ski-simulator.how: Indoor real-snow slope (not a simulator) with lifts and terrain parks, skis and jackets included in the ticket.

surf-simulator.how: Wild Wadi water park has FlowRider-style standing-wave surf simulators (Wipeout and Riptide).

hot-air-ballooning.how: Sunrise hot air balloon flights over the Dubai desert run daily from October to May.

mountaineering.how: Dubai metro area is flat desert and coast with no mountains; the nearest range is the Hajar Mountains around Hatta, about 134 km east (roughly 1.5 hours by road).

canyoning.how: Flat desert and coast with no gorges; the nearest wadis and canyons are in the Hajar Mountains near Hatta or Ras Al Khaimah, roughly 1.5-2 hours away.

cave-exploring.how: Flat alluvial desert with no natural caves in the metro area; the nearest caves are in the Hajar Mountains (Hatta/Fujairah/Oman), roughly 1.5-2 hours away.

luge.how: No mountain terrain or ice track in the metro area; the nearest mountain toboggan ride is at Jebel Jais in Ras Al Khaimah, roughly 1.5-2 hours away.

cricket.how: ICC Academy in Dubai Sports City has two floodlit ovals, 38 turf pitches, indoor nets and a cricket cage, hosting league cricket and coaching, and the wider city has a large expat cricket scene.

snowboarding.how: Ski Dubai inside Mall of the Emirates has a 85 m high indoor mountain with five runs, a chairlift and a tow lift for skiers and snowboarders, with lessons and rental on site.

sailing.how: Dubai Offshore Sailing Club (est. 1974) is an RYA Training Centre on Jumeirah Beach Road with keelboat and dinghy racing fleets, cruising rallies and sailing courses.

dinghy-sailing.how: Dubai Offshore Sailing Club runs RYA dinghy courses and has Optimist, Laser, Pico and open dinghy fleets off Umm Suqeim beach.

keelboat-yachting.how: Dubai Offshore Sailing Club has IRC-rated keelboat racing fleets, RYA cruising and yacht courses and monthly cruising rallies in UAE waters from October to April.

bouldering.how: Rock Republic in Dubai Investment Park is a Walltopia-built bouldering centre with 150+ routes up to 4.5 m with mats, and Mountain Extreme lists 129 bouldering problems with beginner courses.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Mountain Extreme lists about 125 top-rope routes and 14 auto-belays with beginner courses for juniors and adults, and other Dubai gyms offer auto-belay walls.

archery.how: Mushrif Range Shooting runs one-hour archery lessons with equipment included in Mushrif Park, and Dubai Archers Club (D'Archers) is a volunteer-run club active for 20+ years.

horse-riding.how: Dubai Polo & Equestrian Club and Emirates Equestrian Centre give riding lessons from beginner to advanced, with lessons listed from about Dhs240.

pottery-wheel.how: Several Al Quoz studios (Maison Terrae, The Mud House Studio, OKA Ceramics, Yadawei) teach wheel throwing from single intro sessions of roughly AED 210-280.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Maison Terrae, OKA Ceramics and Yadawei Ceramic Studio in Al Quoz teach hand-building alongside wheel work, with beginner sessions from about AED 210.

piano.how: Melodica Music Academy (JLT, Town Square), Prime Symphony Music Centre (Academic City), SOPM (Dubai Investment Park) and others give private piano lessons for all ages.

guitar.how: Prime Symphony Music Centre, Melodica Music Academy, SOPM and Dubai Music School (about AED 250 per hour) offer guitar lessons.

salsa-bachata.how: VR DanceWorld (Business Bay), MOOVnation (JLT), James & Alex Dance Studio (Media City) and Tempo Dance Academy run beginner salsa and bachata classes with social dancing.

tango.how: Tempo Dance Academy's JLT Latin programme lists tango among its courses; no dedicated Argentine tango milonga was confirmed.

stand-up-comedy.how: Dubomedy's arts school and the 5-week Comedy Kix beginner workshop (ending in a live set) teach stand-up, and Dubai has regular English-language comedy nights; content is subject to UAE media-content rules.

improv-comedy.how: Courtyard Playhouse in Al Quoz is a dedicated improv theatre running workshops for adults, teens and kids with free trial classes.

ballet.how: The Ballet Centre Dubai (Motor City, Jumeirah), The National Ballet Studio (Jumeirah Islands) and Melodica Music Academy teach ballet to adults and children, many with trial classes.

pole-dance.how: Studio Republik and Pole Fit Dubai Aerial Arts Academy (Dubai Marina) run pole fitness classes for adults.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Studio Republik, Pole Fit Dubai and TRIX DXB (International City) teach aerial silks, hoop and hammock classes.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Guided Dubai kayak tours (e.g. Hydro Water Sports at Royal Central The Palm) pass small mangrove stands; dedicated mangrove kayaking is mainly in Abu Dhabi.

kayaking.how: Guided and rental kayak tours run along the Dubai coast and Marina, for example from Hydro Water Sports at Royal Central The Palm.

camel-racing.how: Camel racing is a spectator sport at Nad Al Sheba / Al Marmoom tracks on the Dubai outskirts (season roughly October to April); racing itself is for owners with robot jockeys.

hiking.how: Meetup groups (Alpine Trekkers, AFT Mountain Adventures) run weekly hikes in the Hajar Mountains, with Hatta about 1.5 hours from the centre; Dubai itself is flat desert and coast.

bobsled.how: No bobsleigh or skeleton track exists in the UAE; the climate is hot desert.

buzkashi.how: Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback sport tied to Afghanistan; no UAE equivalent club exists in Dubai.

cheese-rolling.how: Cheese rolling is a single annual event at Cooper's Hill, Gloucestershire; it is not practised in the UAE.

elephant-polo.how: Elephant polo needs working elephants (Nepal, Thailand, India); there are none in Dubai.

ski-jumping.how: Ski jumping needs a large outdoor hill with natural snow; Ski Dubai is too small and has no jump; nearest hills are in Europe.

snow-sculpture.how: Dubai's climate makes outdoor snow sculpture impossible; nearest snow festivals are in East Asia and Europe.

scuba-diving.how: PADI centres such as Bermuda Diving Center (Jumeirah 3), Scuba Shade and ScubaDive.ae run try-dives from about AED 250-580 and Open Water courses (around AED 2,500) in the Gulf, plus a pool at Deep Dive Dubai.

skateboarding.how: XDubai Skatepark at Kite Beach is a 3,100 sq m park with a day pass of about AED 75, and free public parks exist at Al Mamzar, The Block (d3), Business Bay and elsewhere.

bmx.how: Adventure Zone indoor skate parks in Dubai malls (Galleria, Times Square Centre) have a BMX area on timed passes; no outdoor BMX track was confirmed.

ice-skating.how: The Dubai Mall has an Olympic-sized ice rink used for public skating sessions and Emirates Ice Hockey League games.
ice-skating.venue: Dubai Ice Rink, The Dubai Mall

ice-hockey.how: The Dubai Mall's Olympic-sized rink hosts Emirates Ice Hockey League games, and the UAE Ice Hockey Association runs the national league and teams.
ice-hockey.venue: Dubai Ice Rink, The Dubai Mall

dragon-boat.how: Dubai Paddle Club is a dragon boat crew based at Dubai Offshore Sailing Club, and Dubai Dolphins, Barracuda and Move One Dubai Sea Dragons also paddle, under the UAE Dragon Boat Association.

fencing.how: Dubai Fencing Club, founded in 2002 by coach Mihail Kouzev, trains foil, epee and sabre fencers; it met at the Quay Health Club, Mina A'Salam, in older reports.

padel.how: Padel is widely played in Dubai, with Meetup groups such as Padel Nation running weekly social nights with rackets and balls included.

photography.how: Gulf Photo Plus at Alserkal Avenue runs workshops and photo walks, and Moutasem Academy, The Photography Institute and SAE Dubai teach digital photography courses.

oil-painting.how: The Palette Art in Al Barsha and Dubai International Art Centre run painting classes including oil.

watercolour-painting.how: Dubai International Art Centre (founded 1976, Jumeirah 1) and The Palette Art offer watercolour courses.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: The Jamjar at Alserkal Avenue runs figure drawing workshops and Meraki Art and Design Studio lists a charcoal course; nude-model sessions are limited by UAE public-decency rules.

candle-making.how: Studio Kinza (Al Quoz), Resin Art Hub (Al Garhoud) and La Plume Candles run candle-making workshops of 1.5-2.5 hours, listed from AED 180.

perfumery.how: Oo La Lab in Dubai Design District runs one-hour introductory scent-blending sessions from AED 320 with no experience needed, and Grasse Institute of Perfumery offers technical courses.

rugby.how: Dubai Exiles RFC (founded 1966) at The Sevens on Al Ain Road runs mini, youth, senior men's and women's rugby plus social touch rugby for adults, and welcomes newcomers.

taekwondo.how: WTTU Moo Duk Taekwondo (DIFC, Sports City, Al Barari), The Warrior Academy and The Ballet Centre Dubai teach taekwondo from toddlers to adults.

judo.how: The Warrior Academy (Al Quoz) lists judo alongside taekwondo, karate and jiu-jitsu, but is described as child-focused, so adult judo is unconfirmed.

stargazing.how: Dubai Astronomy Group runs public stargazing nights at Al Qudra desert (about an hour from the centre, entry free to independent visitors) and the Al Thuraya Astronomy Centre in Mushrif Park offers telescopes.
stargazing.venue: Al Thuraya Astronomy Centre, Mushrif Park

camping.how: Overnight camping in Dubai emirate is restricted to Dubai Municipality-permitted areas (e.g. Wadi Al Amerdi, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej), and Al Qudra camping has been officially banned in places.

fishing.how: Deep-sea fishing charters depart Dubai Marina twice daily on 4-hour trips with tackle and bait included (about AED 312 each on Platinum List).

bharatanatyam.how: Laasya Performing Arts in Jebel Ali Village teaches Bharatanatyam and Kathak to children and adults and performs at Global Village.

kathak.how: Laasya Performing Arts in Jebel Ali Village teaches Kathak and Bharatanatyam with trained instructors.

tabla.how: Tharangini Music Centre in Al Nahda is listed for tabla and other Indian music and dance classes; no operator page was opened.

dj-turntablism.how: Dancemania DJ & Music Production studio in Al Safa runs one-to-one and group DJ courses for beginners and advanced students.

music-production.how: Dancemania Music Studio in Al Safa runs DJ and music production courses, and SAWT Music Academy offers production courses in English and Arabic.

rug-tufting.how: Tufting Time runs guided rug-tufting sessions (from about AED 315) at Dubai Festival City Mall, Jumeirah and Town Square, where participants design and make their own rug.

knitting-crochet.how: Solandis Crochet in Al Qusais teaches private beginner crochet classes (about AED 345).

leatherwork.how: Fuse DXB runs a private DIY leather jewellery workshop in Arabian Ranches listed through Skilldeer; no dedicated leatherwork studio was confirmed.

filmmaking.how: SAE Institute Dubai (Knowledge Park) offers a film diploma, BazAct blends acting with short-film making, and Skilldeer lists filmmaking classes.

big-wall-climbing.how: Dubai is flat desert and coast with no big walls; the nearest big rock is in the Hajar Mountains of Ras Al Khaimah and Oman's Musandam, about 1.5-2 hours away.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: The Dubai metro area is flat desert and coast with no crags; the nearest outdoor climbing is in the Hajar Mountains near Hatta and Ras Al Khaimah, about 1.5 hours away.

surfing-ocean.how: Surf House Dubai offers surf and paddleboard lessons on the small Gulf swell, while Dubai's main wave sports are kitesurfing at Kite Beach; real ocean surf waves are rare.

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: IGNITE Sport Services rents stand-up paddleboards on Palm Jumeirah by the hour (about AED 95) with a short beginner lesson, paddle and life vest included.

australian-rules-football.how: Dubai Dingoes and other clubs played in the AFL Middle East nines league (since 2008/09) at Dubai Sports City, but current club activity was not confirmed.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Dubai Celts GAA (formed 1995) fields men's, ladies' and juvenile Gaelic football, hurling and camogie and runs the annual Dubai Duty Free Gulf Gaelic Games.

choir.how: One Day Choir Dubai runs no-audition single-day choir sessions, and Dubai Camerata Singers is a multicultural community choir founded in 2017.

nature-guided-walks.how: Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary at the head of Dubai Creek has free public bird hides with flamingos; organised guided walks were not confirmed.

pickleball.how: Picklers in Al Quoz is an indoor club with six enclosed climate-controlled pickleball courts, and other venues such as PickleTurf at Port Rashid also take court bookings.

printmaking-screenprint.how: The Workshop DXB, a screenprinting studio opposite Alserkal Avenue, ran a Dubai Culture screenprinting training programme, and Tashkeel has run multi-session screenprinting workshops.

chinese-calligraphy.how: Chinese calligraphy in Dubai appears mainly as event performances and children's writing sessions via tutor directories, with no dedicated adult class confirmed.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Tashkeel runs multi-session Jewellery Manufacturing Basics workshops (wax carving, sawing, filing, soldering), and The Jewel Teller at Alserkal Avenue has offered goldsmith-led metal pendant courses.

urban-sketching.how: Urban Sketchers Dubai, an official chapter of the international organisation, holds free on-location sketching meetups at pre-arranged spots, open to all skill levels.

capoeira.how: Afro-Ritmo Capoeira runs adult and children's classes in Jumeirah Lake Towers, and Nacao Capoeira Dubai has also run classes in the city.

ultimate-frisbee.how: Dubai has a long-running ultimate community (Dubai Ultimate Players Association, United Arabian Ultimate) that hosted the 2015 World Championships of Beach Ultimate and plays recreational sessions.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Lindy Hop Dubai ran free beginner swing sessions at a JBR hotel bar according to a 2015 listing; current activity is unconfirmed.
swing-lindy-hop.venue: Lindy Hop Dubai (Speakeasy Bar, Ramada Plaza)

bookbinding.how: Tashkeel has run introductory bookbinding workshops (accordion, single signature, Japanese stab binding) at Dubai Design District and Emirates Towers, and operates a makerspace at Alserkal Avenue; sessions are occasional.

embroidery.how: Craft Land in Jumeirah teaches hand embroidery alongside sewing and quilting, and beginner courses (intro class in Jebel Ali, Town Centre Jumeirah) are listed.

tap-dance.how: The Ballet Centre in Motor City and Dance For You in Garhoud list tap dance classes among their dance programmes.

breakdancing.how: Tempo Dance Center in Jumeirah Lake Towers lists break dance lessons, and Red Bull BC One regional events have run in Dubai.

irish-dance.how: The Ballet Centre in Motor City, a children's dance school, lists Irish dance among its classes; no adult or dedicated Irish dance school was found.

taiko.how: Shoten Taiko Drummers, founded in Dubai in 2014 as the Middle East's first taiko group, perform at events; open classes are not confirmed.

film-photography-darkroom.how: Tashkeel has a fully equipped darkroom and has run courses developing and printing black-and-white film, and Analog The Room is a Dubai analog photography lab offering film development workshops.

ikebana.how: The Ohara School of Ikebana UAE branch has taught in Dubai since 2014, with regular workshops open to outsiders including an annual cherry-blossom class, and Ikebana International has a Dubai chapter.
