chess.how: Dubai Chess and Culture Club in Al Mamzar has a 250-seat tournament hall, a chess school with training rooms and runs the annual Dubai Open and junior championships; Dubai Social Chess Club also meets.

mahjong.how: Mahjong Dubai, a Riichi (Japanese-style) mahjong group, hosts regular meetups in the city.

board-games.how: Several board game groups, including Dubai Board Gamers, House Rules and Game Knights, host regular social game nights at cafes and venues across the city.

escape-rooms.how: Dubai has dozens of escape rooms, including Game Over, NoWayOut in JLT, Escape Hunt at Galleria Mall and horror-themed Escape House, typically 60-minute games for 2-10 players.

paintball.how: Singo Paintball is an air-conditioned indoor paintball arena in Dubai, and Battle Park and Action Park run outdoor fields with gear supplied.

woodworking.how: The Makers Society in Ras Al Khor runs woodworking trial classes (hand-saw and hand-plane basics, tools provided) plus wood-turning and kids' courses.

3d-printing.how: Origin Base in Al Quoz offers memberships and day passes with 3D printing and laser cutting training, and FabLab UAE and the Hamdan Award Fab Lab offer public access to 3D printers.

laser-cutting.how: Origin Base in Al Quoz has a 100 W CO2 laser cutter with safety training for members, and FabLab UAE also lists laser cutting.

cnc-machining.how: FabLab UAE lists CNC milling alongside 3D printing and laser cutting with staff training, and Origin Base has wood and metal shops for members.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Origin Base, a makerspace in Al Quoz, includes an electronics lab alongside other shops for members; the 2017-verified listing may be dated.

amateur-radio.how: The Emirates Amateur Radio Society runs licensing training, exams and repeaters for the UAE from Sharjah, roughly 25-30 km from central Dubai.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: Le Gourmet at Galeries Lafayette and Culinary Boutique run hands-on cooking workshops across cuisines including pasta, sushi and dumplings.

sushi-making.how: SUSHISAMBA Dubai has run an Edomae sushi masterclass with lunch, and the Meydan Hotel's Shiba restaurant ran a dim sum and sushi class.

dim-sum-making.how: Hotel restaurants such as Shiba at Meydan Hotel and Zhen Wei at Caesars Palace Bluewaters have run occasional two-hour dim sum classes.

wine-tasting-wset.how: The Tasting Class has offered WSET Level 1 and 2 wine courses to the public in Dubai since 2017, alongside tasting events in hotels and restaurants.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: The Gulf Roleplaying Community runs tabletop RPG games in the UAE, and tabletop.me, a Dubai tabletop convention held at the Concourse Convention Center in Dubai Outlet Mall, included Dungeons & Dragons sessions.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Battlezone on Jumeirah Road was listed as hosting card and war gamers with Warhammer 40K among the most popular games; the listing is old.

latte-art.how: ICCA Dubai's Artisanal Coffee programme includes a full day of hands-on latte art, and City & Guilds barista skills courses run at Dubai Knowledge Park.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Dubai International Bowling Centre in Al Mamzar has 36 lanes, and Black Bunny in Al Quoz and Glitch at Al Ghurair Centre have eight-lane alleys.

vr-gaming.how: VR Park Dubai on the second floor of Dubai Mall is a dedicated virtual reality venue, and Black Bunny and Glitch also offer VR games.

arcade-games.how: Sega Republic in Dubai Mall and family venues such as Black Bunny and Glitch have large arcade game floors.

art-gallery.how: Alserkal Avenue in Al Quoz hosts about 25 contemporary art galleries and spaces such as Ayyam Gallery, Carbon 12 and Green Art Gallery, with exhibitions, talks and community events.

museums.how: Museum of the Future on Sheikh Zayed Road is an immersive exhibition venue across five themed floors on science, technology and innovation.

science-museum.how: Museum of the Future presents exhibits on space, ecology, technology and near-future solutions, with a children's interactive floor.

toastmasters.how: Many Toastmasters clubs meet in Dubai, including Dubai Internet City Toastmasters, JLT Dubai Toastmasters and Emirates Toastmasters Club.

language-exchange.how: Dubai hosts several language exchange meetup groups such as The Language Society, Dubai Language & Communication Circle and Dubai Expats Social & Language Exchange.

japanese-language.how: Berlitz runs in-person private and group Japanese classes at its Dubai language centres in JLT and Jumeirah, and other schools such as Eton Institute also list Japanese courses.

spanish-language.how: UCAM Espanol Institute in JLT is an Instituto Cervantes-accredited centre and DELE exam venue offering 20 to 60-hour Spanish courses in person or online.

german-language.how: Goethe-Institut Gulf Region runs German courses from A1 to C2 (standard and intensive, on-site and online) at its Dubai centre in Bur Dubai.

mixology.how: ICCA Dubai teaches bartending and alcohol-free mixology courses, PATH Bar School offers cocktail and spirits certification, and venues such as Time Out Market run paid cocktail masterclasses.

whisky-tasting.how: Hotel and venue whisky tastings and masterclasses (a Le Clos Taste of Whisky evening at Bulgari Hotel Yacht Club, Macallan pairing tastings at The St. Regis) run as ticketed events in licensed venues rather than as a standing class.

horse-polo.how: Dubai Polo & Equestrian Club in Arabian Ranches has a polo academy and riding school with beginner polo lessons.

esports-gaming.how: Dubai has gaming cafes such as Esport Arena that host PC cafe tournaments, and the Dubai Esports and Games Festival runs competitions in titles like Valorant and League of Legends.

tai-chi.how: A community group practises tai chi and martial arts in South Ridge Park in Downtown Dubai every weekend, and several studios list tai chi classes.

stamp-collecting.how: The Emirates Philatelic Association (founded 1996, 700+ members) is based in Dubai and organises stamp exhibitions including the Dubai 2026 World Stamp Exhibition.

vinyl-records.how: The Flip Side at Alserkal Avenue is an independent vinyl store, and Raw Music Store, Metal East Records and Cavo also sell new and used records.

sourdough-baking.how: One-off sourdough workshops are run by home bakers and bakeries, such as a sourdough experience at The Bread Basket in Jumeirah 1.

tea-ceremony.how: Urasenke-style tea ceremonies and matcha workshops are held in Dubai by a study group and by organisers such as IKIGAI-SHU, mostly as occasional events.

trading-card-games.how: Magic: The Gathering events including regional qualifiers are held at Dubai game stores such as Back to Games and tabletop.me.

trading-cards.how: PokeMENA in Dubai Silicon Oasis sells Pokemon and graded trading cards, and BattleZone stocks Yu-Gi-Oh, Magic and Pokemon cards.

cosplay.how: Cosplayers gather mainly at the annual Middle East Film and Comic Con at Dubai World Trade Centre, which includes cosplay competitions and workshops.
cosplay.venue: Middle East Film and Comic Con

hackathons.how: AI Tinkerers Dubai runs in-person hackathons and demo days (a Global Hackathon in September 2026), and events such as AngelHack Dubai and Falak.me CodeFest have also been held.

coding-meetups.how: AI Tinkerers Dubai holds screened in-person builder meetups, and CodersHQ is a Dubai hub for developer meetups, talks and hackathons.

go-weiqi.how: Shanghai Weiqi (Go) Club meets weekly on Sundays at The Press near Hankou Lu; beginners are welcome and the organiser brings a board and teaches the rules.

chess.how: Shanghai Social Chess Club holds relaxed chess meetups on Tuesday evenings in cafes around Jing'an Temple, open to all levels including beginners.

tai-chi.how: Shanghai Tai Chi Group runs 60-minute beginner-level taichi classes on Sundays at a hotel in Changning, with a trial fee.
tai-chi.venue: Shanghai Tai Chi Group (Shanghai Anadi Hotel)

coding-meetups.how: codebar Shanghai runs free coding workshops open to anyone, hosted at rotating venues such as a bookstore in Huangpu.

language-exchange.how: Language Exchangers Shanghai (about 3,500 members) hosts Friday evening and Sunday afternoon language exchange socials in Xuhui and Changning bars and cafes; a ticket includes a drink.
language-exchange.venue: Language Exchangers Shanghai (Tims Coffee Greenland Wonderful City / Koala Bar)

creative-writing.how: The Inkwell, a writing group founded in 2015, runs free fiction, nonfiction and poetry workshops and open writing sessions at cafes and bars in central Shanghai; no experience required.

book-club.how: The Inkwell holds a free Reading Group every other Monday at Garden Books on Changle Lu.

mahjong.how: Shanghai Mahjong Workshop teaches internationals Chinese mahjong in simple English on Sunday afternoons at Happy Mahjong Club on Fumin Lu; described as beginner-friendly.

big-wall-climbing.how: KL Climbing Park in Libo 1987 has indoor walls of 16 m, 20 m and up to 34 m with auto-belay routes; no natural big walls nearby.

museums.how: The Shanghai Museum at People's Square holds over 120,000 pieces across eleven permanent galleries of bronzes, ceramics, calligraphy and painting.

science-museum.how: Shanghai Science and Technology Museum in Pudong has hands-on exhibits and a robotics lab, with adult tickets around CNY 45.

wartime-history.how: The Shanghai Jewish Refugees Museum in the former Ohel Moshe Synagogue covers the WWII-era Hongkou refugee sector with documents, photographs and a memorial wall.

art-gallery.how: Power Station of Art, China's state-run contemporary art museum in a former power plant on the Huangpu riverside, hosts the Shanghai Biennale and free-to-enter exhibitions.

temple-activities.how: Longhua Temple, the city's largest Buddhist temple, is open to visitors for a small fee and holds an annual temple fair and a New Year's Eve bell-striking ceremony.

parkour.how: LINK Parkour runs parkour training at SOHOGYM on Yongtai Lu in Xuhui and a second site on Pingji Lu.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Party King Bowling Sports Bar in the Dimei Shopping Center off Renmin Avenue near People's Square hosts group game nights with bowling, archery, foosball and billiards for about RMB 150 including a drink.
ten-pin-bowling.venue: Party King Bowling Sports Bar (Dimei Shopping Center)

archery.how: Party King Bowling Sports Bar offers archery as part of its unlimited-play game nights, and the ASAS Archery Battle community runs weekend archery-tag games organised through WeChat.
archery.venue: Party King Bowling Sports Bar (Dimei Shopping Center)

running-club.how: RunnersHai holds free social runs and coached training on the West Bund on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and weekend mornings, and the Shanghai Hash House Harriers run a new route every Sunday afternoon.

history-walks.how: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel) runs a Sunday afternoon heritage walk, 'Secrets, Spies & Art Deco', through the former French Concession from Jiangsu Road to Huashan Road, and Weekend Riverfront City Walk leads bilingual walks along the Bund, Suzhou Creek and the former French Concession.
history-walks.venue: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel)

meetups.how: Shanghai FUN is a bilingual social community with over 8,000 members and a 1,000-event history, running regular social nights, networking and classes at venues around Jing'an and the Bund.

meditation.how: Shanghai Sahaja Yoga Meditation offers free guided meditation sessions with no prior experience needed, listed as online Zoom sessions; in person, the Learn Qigong in Shanghai group teaches gentle qigong in English at Fuxing Park.
meditation.venue: Learn Qigong in Shanghai (Fuxing Park) / Shanghai Sahaja Yoga Meditation

board-games.how: The Second Languages & Cross Culture's Communication meetup group hosts a Saturday evening board games night in the roadshow hall of Fudan Science Park.
board-games.venue: Fudan Science Park (Saturday Shanghai Board Games)

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: OKDeal Travel / Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai host 'Authentic China Tastes' cooking classes, including one with a Michelin chef in the Jing'an Temple area.
pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.venue: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel)

wine-tasting-wset.how: Dramamoves.com Projects, a bespoke wine service behind Plaza 66, runs drop-in tastings of French and Italian wines from independent producers; no WSET course was confirmed.

hackerspace-electronics.how: XinCheJian, China's first hackerspace (2010), is a volunteer-run nonprofit in Huangpu with monthly memberships, Wednesday open nights and electronics workshops.

robotics-arduino.how: XinCheJian runs workshops on Arduino, PCB design and robot building (e.g. Otto robot, DIY drone).

3d-printing.how: XinCheJian hackerspace provides 3D printing among its member facilities.

laser-cutting.how: XinCheJian hackerspace provides laser cutting among its member facilities.

cnc-machining.how: XinCheJian hackerspace lists machine work and digital fabrication among its member facilities; CNC specifically was not confirmed.

public-lectures.how: Shanghai Library runs a regular public lecture series (Shanghai Library Lectures) alongside exhibitions and training courses at its Huaihai Road and East branches.

archival-research.how: Shanghai Library holds historical literature collections and a Genealogy Library open to readers at its Huaihai Road branch.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: Shanghai is flat delta land with no natural crags; local gyms such as Roaring Climbing Gym in Hongkou organise outdoor climbing trips out of the city.

snow-sculpture.how: Shanghai's mild climate gives little reliable snow; large snow sculpture exhibitions are held in Harbin each winter, roughly a 3-hour flight away.

toastmasters.how: Shanghai has several Toastmasters clubs listed in the club directory, including Shanghai People's Square Toastmasters Club, Shanghai Xujiahui Toastmasters Club and Shanghai No.1 Toastmasters Club.

massage.how: Dragonfly (悠庭) is a chain of massage and beauty spas with branches in Shanghai offering classic massage for men and women with online booking.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The Shanghai Jewish Refugees Museum in the former Ohel Moshe Synagogue preserves the heritage of the Jewish community that sheltered in Hongkou in the 1930s and 1940s.

heritage-trails.how: A self-guided half-day walk through the former French Concession starting at Wukang Road and Huaihai Road is recommended by the city tourism guide, and Hongkou's 1933 Old Millfun is free to enter.

dim-sum-making.how: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel) lists xiaolongbao and dumpling-making cooking classes among its hands-on cultural activities.
dim-sum-making.venue: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel)

mountaineering.how: Flat Yangtze delta (average about 4 m above sea level, highest hill Sheshan 118 m) has no mountains; nearest real mountaineering is Huangshan or Mount Tianmu in Anhui/Zhejiang, roughly 3-5 hours away by high-speed rail and road.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers in the flat Yangtze delta; the nearest glaciers are in western China (Yulong Snow Mountain, Yunnan, or Tibet), a 3-4 hour flight away.

canyoning.how: Flat delta terrain has no gorges or canyons; the nearest canyoning is in the Zhejiang and Anhui mountains, roughly 3-4 hours away.

white-water-rafting.how: Flat delta with slow tidal rivers has no whitewater; nearest river rafting is in Zhejiang (for example Fuchunjiang or Anji area) around 2-3 hours away.

base-jumping.how: No cliffs or tall natural exposures in the flat delta and BASE jumping from buildings is illegal; nearest sites are Zhangjiajie or Tianmen Mountain in Hunan, a 2-hour flight away.

dog-sledding.how: Climate with only about 5 snowy days a year rules out snow dog sledding; the nearest is in Heilongjiang or Jilin, a 2.5-3 hour flight north.

snow-skiing.how: Natural snow is rare (about 5 days a year) and there are no mountains; nearest natural-snow skiing is in Zhejiang/Anhui winter resorts or Jilin, about 3 hours by flight.

volcano-boarding.how: No volcanoes anywhere near the delta; nearest is Changbai Mountain in Jilin or Tianchi areas, a 3 hour flight north.

sandboarding-desert.how: No desert in the metro area; nearest desert dunes are in Inner Mongolia or Gansu, a 3-4 hour flight west.

whale-watching.how: Silty estuary and shallow East China Sea off Shanghai have no regular whale-watching industry; the nearest established whale watching is in Taiwan or Japan, around 2-3 hours by flight.

meteorite-hunting.how: No strewn fields or desert/dry-lake terrain near the delta, where alluvial soil covers the ground; meteorite hunting is done in Xinjiang or Inner Mongolia deserts, a 3-4 hour flight away.

cave-diving.how: Delta alluvial plain has no limestone caves or flooded cave systems; the nearest cave systems are in the Zhejiang and Anhui karst areas, 3-4 hours away, and recreational cave diving is rare in China.

bullfighting.how: No bullfighting tradition and not practised legally in China; the nearest are in Spain or Portugal, a 12 hour flight.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: The Yangtze estuary coast is too far north and cold for mangroves (natural range stops in southern Zhejiang); the nearest mangrove paddling is around Wenzhou in Zhejiang or Fujian, roughly 2-3 hours by train.

hunting.how: Recreational hunting of wildlife is restricted and effectively unavailable in Shanghai's urban metro; nearest licensed hunting grounds are in remote provinces such as Inner Mongolia, a 3 hour flight.

cricket.how: Shanghai Cricket Club runs a two-division league and welcomes casual players, playing at the Shanghai Community Sports Club in Pudong.
cricket.venue: Shanghai Cricket Club (Shanghai Community Sports Club ground)

rugby.how: Shanghai Rugby Football Club trains weekly at Wellington College (Tue) and Harrow International School (Sat) and welcomes complete newcomers; Dolphins Rugby also runs touch and contact sessions at Luwan Stadium.

ultimate-frisbee.how: Shanghai Ultimate Players Association plays pick-up games on Monday nights at Jing'an Workers' Stadium and Saturday mornings at Shanghai Community Sports Club for about RMB 50 per session.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Shanghai GAA (founded 2002) trains Tuesday evenings at Luwan Stadium; training is free to try and absolute beginners are welcome.

fencing.how: Dragon Fencing Center teaches adult beginners with an annual membership that includes a weekly group lesson (2015 SmartShanghai profile; current status unconfirmed).

ice-hockey.how: Shanghai Hockey Club runs adult ice hockey with a skate assessment used for team placement.

ice-skating.how: All Star Skating Club under the Mercedes-Benz Arena is among Shanghai's better rinks, and SmartShanghai lists a dozen-plus rinks citywide including Hongqiao Ice Sports Center.

curling.how: Shanghai has a few curling sites (Putuo Ice Sports Center converted rinks into five sheets for the 2026 national championships; Dream World Qingpu has a rink for hockey and curling), but public drop-in curling was not confirmed.

bouldering.how: BANANA+ in The Lightbox is a large Jing'an bouldering gym with beginner-friendly problems; Pongo and Beta Boulders are other dedicated bouldering gyms.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Acme Climbing at 189 Plaza and Magirock offer top-rope and lead walls with harness and shoe rental and basic instruction.

horse-riding.how: Shanghai Westend Equestrian Club on Changxing Island offers English-style group and private lessons with a trial class; roughly an hour's drive from downtown.

dragon-boat.how: Shanghaied Dragons is an amateur expat dragon boat team that accepts paddlers of any ability and trains beginners with weeknight practices.

salsa-bachata.how: Latin Soul Dance Studio teaches salsa (On1, On2, rueda) and bachata classes Monday to Friday evenings for all levels; ByC! and Phoenix studios also teach bachata.

improv-comedy.how: Zmack Improv has performed in English since 2009 and runs Zmack Comedy School improv classes for adults.

stand-up-comedy.how: SpicyComedy in Xintiandi runs English stand-up showcases most nights, sometimes with open-mic formats.

pottery-wheel.how: The Pottery Workshop teaches wheel throwing to adults in English or Chinese, seven days a week.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Meet Pottery and Taoni Xuanxiao offer drop-in DIY hand-building and wheel sessions for RMB 120-158 including firing.

printmaking-screenprint.how: IdleBeats Print Club in Xuhui runs two-hour beginner screen-printing workshops in English and Chinese plus open-studio blocks.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Lao Feng Xiang hosted a one-off expat silver pendant design-and-polish workshop at its Yuyuan Garden flagship in 2026; regular classes were not confirmed.
jewellery-silversmithing.venue: Lao Feng Xiang flagship, Yuyuan Garden Malls

capoeira.how: Capoeira Mandinga Shanghai lists classes (kids confirmed); an older expat thread describes adult beginner sessions near Zhongshan Park.

taekwondo.how: Mingwu martial arts school lists taekwondo alongside taiji, sanda and Thai boxing in a SmartShanghai martial arts listing.

skateboarding.how: ICONX operates one of Shanghai's first indoor skateparks at Jing'an Sports Center, and SMP Skatepark in Yangpu is billed as China's biggest; Linkong Skateboard Park in Changning is an outdoor park.

snowboarding.how: Smile Snow in Changning and SHEERCOOL have ski simulators; L+SNOW in Lin-gang (Pudong) is a very large year-round indoor snow resort, roughly 55 km from the centre.

bobsled.how: No bobsleigh or skeleton track exists in the Shanghai region; the nearest is the Yanqing track near Beijing, about 1,100 km away.

ski-jumping.how: No ski jumping hill exists near Shanghai; hills are in northern China such as Zhangjiakou (Chongli) near Beijing, about 1,100 km away.

buzkashi.how: Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback game and is not played in the Shanghai area; the nearest traditions are in Xinjiang, thousands of km away.

camel-racing.how: Camel racing needs camels and desert terrain; nothing comparable exists near Shanghai (nearest in Inner Mongolia/Xinjiang, thousands of km away).

cheese-rolling.how: Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling is an annual event in Gloucestershire, England, with no equivalent in the Shanghai region.

elephant-polo.how: Elephant polo requires working elephants, which are not kept in the Shanghai region; it is played in Thailand, Nepal and India (about 5-hour flights).

surfing-ocean.how: The Yangtze estuary coast near Shanghai is muddy and shallow with no reliable surf; the nearest surf spots are in Hainan (for example Riyue Bay), around a 3-hour flight.

trail-running.how: Shanghai Hash House Harriers hold weekly Sunday trail walk/run events at rotating locations, and RunnersHai runs free social runs at West Bund; true trail terrain is limited by the flat delta.

hiking.how: Sheshan National Forest Park offers hill trails within the city, while longer hikes require trips to hills in neighbouring Zhejiang or Jiangsu, such as the guided Changzhou trips sold to Shanghai expats.

camping.how: Shanghai has a handful of designated park camping areas and a guided camping trip trade for expats, though most multi-night camping happens in neighbouring provinces.
camping.venue: Guided camping and hiking trips (Hello China Trip)

kayaking.how: New Jiangwan City Culture and Sports Park in Yangpu has a professionally managed water sports centre for paddleboarding and kayaking, with Direction Kayak ASSN training at Nianfeng Park.
kayaking.venue: New Jiangwan City Culture and Sports Park water sports centre

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: Danba Art Dock in Putuo offers sunset paddleboard yoga and paddle polo, and Tingdong Kayaking Club teaches beginner paddleboarding.

scuba-diving.how: Big Blue Scuba Diving International runs 400 RMB discovery dives in a pool in Qibao and PADI courses with open-water dives at Qiandao Lake.

guitar.how: Studio Insight offers one-on-one and group guitar lessons with local and expat teachers, with a trial class listed at RMB 58.

piano.how: Studio Insight offers one-on-one and group piano lessons with local and expat teachers.

music-production.how: Gate Music in Changning is an Ableton-certified training centre teaching music production with bilingual materials and international instructors.

dj-turntablism.how: Gate Music and Studio Insight teach DJing with international instructors; C-Space in Jing'an is another DJ school.

chinese-calligraphy.how: InkMoon Workshop on Fumin Lu runs small-group (max six) one-off and long-term calligraphy classes for RMB 280 per person.

oil-painting.how: Salon de Verve on Huashan Lu runs three-hour oil painting classes by appointment with canvas, paints and instructor included.

embroidery.how: Make in China on Jiashan Lu runs three-hour weaving, macrame, block printing, embroidery and crochet workshops; Shanghai Mass Art Museum also has a 12-session embroidery course for foreigners.

weaving.how: Make in China runs three-hour weaving and macrame workshops at about RMB 400 per person.

knitting-crochet.how: Make in China lists crochet among its three-hour craft workshops; dedicated knitting groups were not confirmed.

glassblowing.how: Shanghai Museum of Glass runs hands-on glassmaking workshops priced RMB 98-380; whether full hot glassblowing is included was not confirmed.

pickleball.how: InLove Sports Club in Huangpu has two indoor pickleball courts, and Rocker Park at Bailian Xijiao in Changning converts to four courts.

padel.how: PadelX operates two padel courts at Bailian Xijiao Shopping Center in Changning, open 7am to midnight.

choir.how: Shanghai Voices International Choir has drawn members from over 20 countries since 2000, and the Shanghai Citizen Art Night School runs singing classes for expats.

ballet.how: Dance Flow Studio near iAPM and Dance Box offer adult ballet and contemporary classes.

pole-dance.how: La Luna in Minhang is a studio specialising in pole dancing, with yoga and contemporary classes.

fishing.how: Luyuan Fishing Leisure Center in Pudong has man-made ponds for day-ticket carp fishing, and Fishing Bay Ecological Garden in Xinchang has fishing ponds.

freshwater-fishing.how: Luyuan Fishing Leisure Center in Pudong has man-made ponds for bamboo-rod day-ticket carp fishing (2017 SmartShanghai article).

stargazing.how: Sheshan Observatory's historic 40-cm telescope has been partially opened to booked public visits since 2023, and the Shanghai Astronomy Museum in Lin-gang offers night views through a one-metre telescope; no amateur club was found.

escape-rooms.how: Shanghai has hundreds of escape-room venues such as MC Puzzle Room and Mofang Secret Room, most run in Mandarin, with some English-friendly or translator-on-request options.

pilates.how: JM Pilates in Yangpu offers private and small-group reformer pilates classes taught in Chinese, Korean and English.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Occasional D&D 5e events are listed on Meetup for Shanghai and a board-game guild meets weekly near Jing'an Temple, but no confirmed current regular D&D group was found.
dungeons-and-dragons.venue: Shanghai board game guild (Cactus, Jing'an Temple)

whisky-tasting.how: The Scotch Malt Whisky Society holds ticketed whisky tastings at BritCham Shanghai and Johnnie Walker House in the former French Concession offers a permanent tasting experience.
whisky-tasting.venue: Scotch Malt Whisky Society at BritCham Shanghai

whisky-society.how: The Scotch Malt Whisky Society runs member-priced tasting events with BritCham Shanghai, though a standing local chapter was not confirmed.
whisky-society.venue: Scotch Malt Whisky Society at BritCham Shanghai

mixology.how: A small-group mixology workshop with tastings in English or Mandarin is offered by Eatwith at a bistro on Yongjia Road.
mixology.venue: Eatwith mixology workshop, Yongjia Road bistro

esports-gaming.how: Shanghai has esports-themed venues such as the ESP eSports Experience Center and IMBA eSports Center at Global Harbor Mall in Putuo, plus many internet-bar gaming halls.
esports-gaming.venue: IMBA eSports Center, Global Harbor Mall

artisan-bread-baking.how: Shanghai Young Bakers Baking Center runs public bread classes such as a baguette and milky-bread course at its centre near Qilianshan Road on Line 11.

pub-trivia.how: Pub quiz nights run in Shanghai, including weekly quizzes at bars such as The Camel and chamber-of-commerce quiz nights at BritCham Shanghai After Hours.

hackathons.how: Hackathons in Shanghai are occasional, such as the French Tech Shanghai team hackathon and NYU Shanghai's HackShanghai, alongside an Indie Hackers builders meetup.

birdwatching.how: Shanghai Birding runs a WeChat group and led trips to Cape Nanhui, while the Shanghai Wild Bird Society and studios run beginner outings at Century Park and Gongqing Forest Park.

german-language.how: Language Exchangers Shanghai holds weekly Friday and Sunday meetups where German is among the practised languages, though no dedicated German course was confirmed.

spanish-language.how: Language Exchangers Shanghai holds weekly Friday and Sunday meetups where Spanish is among the practised languages, though no dedicated Spanish course was confirmed.

japanese-language.how: Language Exchangers Shanghai holds weekly Friday and Sunday meetups where Japanese is among the practised languages, though no dedicated Japanese course was confirmed.

yoga.how: Many studios such as Body & Soul Yoga Club, Pure Yoga (IAPM Mall) and Hatha Yoga Boutique run beginner-to-advanced classes in English and Chinese.

paintball.how: A SmartShanghai listing describes PK6, a foam-pellet shooting arena in Yangpu, and an older listing mentions a paintball park in Gucun Park, Baoshan; no current proper paintball field was confirmed.

volunteering.how: Charities such as Stepping Stones China, Shanghai Sunrise, Heart to Heart Shanghai and Shanghai Young Bakers take expat volunteers for teaching, fundraising and events.
volunteering.venue: Stepping Stones China / Shanghai Sunrise (SmartShanghai list)

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Volunteer-run Shanghai Furry Friends Rescue and Second Chance Animal Aid rescue and rehome strays and need fosters, drivers and helpers; small dog shelters also take weekday volunteers.

pet-adoption.how: Shanghai Furry Friends Rescue and Second Chance Animal Aid rehome rescued stray cats and dogs locally and overseas.

homebrewing-beer.how: A byFood-listed beer brewing workshop in Shanghai lets participants brew a batch to collect after a month; no homebrew club was found.

clay-sculpture.how: The Pottery Workshop on Fuxing Zhong Lu runs hand-building and wheel classes for adults in English or Chinese, and other studios offer one-off clay sessions.

chocolate-making.how: Zotter Chocolate Theatre in Yangpu lets visitors craft their own chocolate bars, and the Callebaut Chocolate Academy in Huangpu runs classes mainly for professionals.

sauna.how: Finnish sauna evenings with a cold plunge are held by FinnCham at the FinChi Innovation Center in Zhangjiang, and Japanese-style onsen spas with Finnish saunas operate in the city.
sauna.venue: FinnCham sauna evenings, FinChi Innovation Center

cold-plunge.how: FinnCham's Finnish sauna evenings in Zhangjiang include a cold plunge, but no dedicated cold-plunge venue was found.
cold-plunge.venue: FinnCham sauna evenings, FinChi Innovation Center

lion-dance.how: Lion dance troupes such as Sanlin Dragon and Lion Dance Troupe perform at Shanghai festivals and theatres, but no public classes were found.
lion-dance.venue: Sanlin Dragon and Lion Dance Troupe

orchestra.how: Shanghai City Symphony Orchestra is a non-profit amateur orchestra founded in 2005 that includes foreign and Chinese musicians living in Shanghai.

geocaching.how: Geocaching.com lists past caches in Shanghai parks and a 2024 event on the Bund, but those listings are archived and the current number of active caches was not confirmed.

disc-golf.how: UDisc and PDGA list several Shanghai-area courses, including 18-hole layouts at 8090 DG Base, Pudong Red Kiln and Guangfulin Country Park in Songjiang.
disc-golf.venue: Guangfulin Country Park disc golf course

drone-flying.how: Shanghai's rules from February 2026 open free-fly zones covering about 46 percent of the urban area, plus bookable public drone experience areas at Century Park, Expo Culture Park and Botanical Garden.
drone-flying.venue: Shanghai Century Park drone experience area

rc-aircraft.how: The Shanghai International Aviation Competition Court in Jiading hosts model-aircraft contests and gives hobbyists space to fly, with paid admission and training courses.

kite-flying.how: Shanghai lists around 18 parks that allow kite flying, and Century Park, Zhongshan Park and Fuxing Park are popular spots with kite sellers nearby.

fermentation-kombucha.how: One-off kombucha workshops are held in Shanghai, such as a free brewing workshop at NYU Shanghai's ICA and a paid session by BASAO Kombucha in Changning in 2024.

vr-gaming.how: Shanghai has dozens of VR arcades, with a 2016 TechNode count of at least 25 and sessions priced around 70 yuan for 15 minutes at venues like Machouse.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Forum posts describe Zark, a Games Workshop-stocking shop in Daning Shopping Plaza with gaming tables, and a local group of foreign 40K players, but the sources are years old.

woodworking.how: Culturally runs a traditional Chinese woodworking workshop near Tianzifang where participants make wooden kitchen utensils with hand tools, and Zowoo at Joy City offers beginner classes.

poetry-slam.how: Occasional poetry open mics are held at venues such as Cotton's on Xinhua Lu and Kartel, often tied to A Shanghai Poetry Zine launches, but no weekly slam was confirmed.
poetry-slam.venue: A Shanghai Poetry Zine launch open mics

cosplay.how: Shanghai hosts large annual cosplay-centred events such as Bilibili World and ChinaJoy, plus smaller comic conventions and the Wujiaochang ACGN Festival.
cosplay.venue: Bilibili World / ChinaJoy (Shanghai New International Expo Centre)

stamp-collecting.how: Shanghai has long-standing philatelic societies including the Shanghai Philatelic Society and the Shanghai Shengxiao Philatelic Society, and hosted a large philately exhibition in early 2025.

vinyl-records.how: Dedicated record shops such as Jodo Space, The Melting Pot, Vinyl Villa and Deer Music sell new and second-hand vinyl across the city.

contract-bridge.how: The Hu Ronghua Bridge Club runs bridge tournaments and youth bridge education under the Shanghai Bridge Association.

lampworking.how: Shanghai Museum of Glass in Baoshan offers hands-on glassblowing and flameworking workshops priced roughly 98-380 RMB.

science-museum.how: The China Science and Technology Museum is a national-level science museum with exhibition halls, labs and special-effect theatres beside the Olympic Green.

wartime-history.how: The Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance Against Japanese Aggression at Wanping Fortress covers the Second Sino-Japanese War in four halls.
wartime-history.venue: Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance Against Japanese Aggression

go-weiqi.how: The Beijing Go Club teaches and plays go (weiqi) weekly on Wednesdays, open to all levels and especially beginners.

board-games.how: Board game cafes sell hourly or per-person tables with libraries of games, such as Big Devil King overlooking the CBD.
board-games.venue: Big Devil King Board Game Cafe

ten-pin-bowling.how: Cosmic Bowling is a 20-lane ten-pin alley inside the Lido Hotel, open evenings daily.

pub-trivia.how: Lush in Wudaokou runs a quiz night every Wednesday at 8pm; Paddy O'Shea's also lists a free Wednesday quiz night (listing may be dated).

paintball.how: The Olympic Sports Centre Paintball Strike Range near subway line 4 offers paintball and laser tag.
paintball.venue: Olympic Sports Centre Paintball Strike Range

wargaming-warhammer.how: The Beijing Qiwan Miniature Wargame Club is listed as a miniature wargaming club; whether it plays Warhammer specifically is not stated.

arcade-games.how: Da Yin Jia Arcade is a small arcade covering the main video game genres; other arcades are listed in the Beijinger gaming-club directory.

bmx.how: The Beijing International Fashion Sports Park (formerly Woodward Beijing) is the city's largest skate park and runs classes from BMX freestyle to dry-land snowboarding.
bmx.venue: Beijing International Fashion Sports Park (Woodward Beijing)

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: Black Sesame Kitchen runs scheduled and private hands-on cooking classes in a hutong courtyard, with a minimum of four guests for private bookings.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Haollee Professional Baking Classes teaches professional baking, patisserie and cake design in Chaoyang.

coding-meetups.how: The Beijing Linux User Group (BLUG) is a community tech group listed in the Beijinger directory.

language-exchange.how: The Beijing Language Exchange Meetup Group holds weekly Talkspace sessions (Friday evening and Sunday English Corner).

toastmasters.how: Toastmasters-format meetings run weekly on Sundays via PET International Friends and Beijing Chinese Language Group on Meetup.

book-club.how: The PET Reading Club meets every Sunday afternoon to share a book, organised through Meetup.

meetups.how: Meetup hosts frequent social events in Beijing such as game nights, frisbee, salsa and world-traveller parties (PET International Friends, Beijing Chinese Language Group).

mixology.how: PET International Friends advertises a recurring cocktail tasting-and-making workshop through Meetup.

flamenco.how: Casa Flamenco in the CBD teaches flamenco dance and guitar for all levels, taught by teachers trained in Spain and the USA.

spanish-language.how: Casa Flamenco (CBD) offers Spanish language classes, and Berlitz lists Spanish among its courses.

german-language.how: Berlitz Language Training Center lists German among its courses, with private tutorials available.

japanese-language.how: Berlitz Language Training Center lists Japanese among its courses, with private tutorials available.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Shou Designers' Jewelry Academy is a jewelry-making school with classes from beginner to professional level.

embroidery.how: A small hutong workshop (Shuiguiqi Traditional Cultural Workshop) offers drop-in sessions in embroidery, tie-dye and clay figurines for about RMB 30 per session.

wine-tasting-wset.how: Beijing Wine Club holds monthly tasting events (blind tastings, wine quizzes) with some wine education; no WSET course was confirmed.

vinyl-records.how: Li-Pi Records in the 798 Art District is a large, well-stocked vinyl record store operating since 2008.

snowboarding.how: The urban area has no natural snow terrain; the nearest snowboard park is at Nanshan Ski Village in Miyun, about 108 km from the centre (roughly 1.5-2 hours by shuttle bus).

homebrewing-beer.how: Jing-A Brewery runs craft taprooms across Beijing (CBD, 798, Wangjing and others); no public brewing classes were confirmed.

filmmaking.how: The Beijing Film Actors and Producers Group meets weekly to perform and film scenes, with a director teaching film acting and production.
filmmaking.venue: Beijing Film Actors and Producers Group

history-walks.how: The China Culture Center offers guided English-language tours, day trips and weekend excursions around Beijing.

mahjong.how: Our Beijing runs mahjong workshops for visitors, and mahjong game rooms are common in the city.

escape-rooms.how: Mr. X is a well-known Beijing escape-room operator with English-language rooms such as The House of Suicide and Alcatraz, bookable via Dianping.

dim-sum-making.how: The Hutong cooking school teaches hands-on dumpling and xiaolongbao classes at its Beixinqiao courtyard.

art-gallery.how: UCCA Center for Contemporary Art in the 798 Art Zone is open daily 10:00-19:00 with major contemporary exhibitions (Carsten Holler: Two through January 2027).

museums.how: The Capital Museum in Xicheng is open 9:00-20:00 (closed Tuesdays) with permanent history and art exhibitions plus visiting shows.

chess.how: The Camera Stylo chess club (founded by David Burgess) meets for casual games and tournaments at a Gulou cafe-bar, open to all ages and levels (2021 article; venue may have changed).

birdwatching.how: Beijing hosts 480+ bird species with sites such as Olympic Forest Park, Yuyuantan Park and Beijing Botanical Garden, and the Beijing Birdwatching Society (400+ members) is the local club (2017 article).

comic-collecting.how: Steamed Bun Comics sells 2,000-3,000 Marvel, DC and Dark Horse comics from inside The Factory bar and music venue in Gulou.

cosplay.how: The Weibo IN Interdimensional Gravitational Zone, an anime/comic/game complex in the former Olympic Volleyball Stadium at Chaoyang Park, draws visitors in cosplay and hosts fandom events.

esports-gaming.how: The Weibo IN Interdimensional Gravitational Zone at Chaoyang Park includes an esports venue and a VR game among its attractions.

vr-gaming.how: The Weibo IN Interdimensional Gravitational Zone at Chaoyang Park includes a VR game attraction.

latte-art.how: Yinpobian, a small Gulou cafe, ran a Monday-night barista class covering espresso machine use and latte art for about RMB 99 (2015 listing).

whisky-tasting.how: Charles' Whisky Bar in Sanyuanqiao offers whisky by the glass with an aroma-sampling corner; Atlas Whisky Bar in Sanlitun stocks about 240 whiskies (2016-2018 articles).

tap-dance.how: On Pointe Dance Studio teaches ballet, jazz and tap, mainly for expat children.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Khan Kon, an annual bilingual gaming convention in Beijing, features Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder and other tabletop RPG sessions (2014 listing).

trading-cards.how: Khan Kon, an annual Beijing gaming convention, hosts a Magic: The Gathering tournament (2014 listing).

poetry-slam.how: Lush in Wudaokou hosts a Sunday-night open mic described as the most eclectic in town.

cold-plunge.how: Winter ice swimming takes place at Houhai lake, where hundreds of swimmers dived in on National Ice Swimming Day (2009 report).

whale-watching.how: Beijing is inland, about 150 km from the Bohai Sea coast near Tianjin, so no whale or dolphin watching exists in the metro area.

coastal-cleanup.how: Beijing is inland with no beaches; the nearest coast is the Bohai Sea near Tianjin, about 150 km away.

beekeeping-honey.how: The China Honey Bee Museum at the Botanical Garden in Fragrant Hills offers honey sampling and beekeeping exhibits, but no hands-on beekeeping course was found.

luge.how: The only luge track is the Yanqing National Sliding Centre about 74 km northwest of central Beijing (roughly 1 hour by the Jingzhang rail line plus transfer), beyond the 30 km metro radius and not open for casual use.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers exist in the Beijing region; the nearest trekkable glaciers are in the Tian Shan near Urumqi, roughly 2400 km away (about 4 hours by air plus transfer).

volcano-boarding.how: No ash-slope volcano suitable for boarding lies near Beijing; the nearest volcanic cones are around Datong (about 300 km, roughly 2 hours by high-speed rail).

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is not part of Chinese culture and has no venues in the Beijing area; the nearest tradition is in Spain or Mexico, a 10+ hour flight away.

hunting.how: Recreational deer hunting is effectively prohibited under Chinese wildlife protection and firearm control law; the nearest game-hunting grounds are in Inner Mongolia, several hours away.

bobsled.how: No bobsleigh or skeleton track exists in the Beijing urban area; the Yanqing National Sliding Centre (2022 Olympic track) is about 75 km northwest of the centre.

ski-jumping.how: No ski jumping hill exists within the Beijing urban area; the nearest are in Zhangjiakou (Chongli), roughly 200 km northwest.

camel-racing.how: Camel racing needs camels and desert terrain; nothing comparable exists in the Beijing area (nearest in Inner Mongolia, several hundred km away).

elephant-polo.how: Elephant polo requires working elephants, which are not kept in the Beijing area; it is played in Thailand, Nepal and India (5+ hour flights).

cheese-rolling.how: Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling is an annual event in Gloucestershire, England, with no equivalent in the Beijing area.

buzkashi.how: Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback game not played in the Beijing area; the nearest comparable traditions are in Xinjiang, thousands of km away.

surfing-ocean.how: Beijing is inland with no ocean surf; the nearest coast (Bohai Sea at Tianjin or Qinhuangdao, 150-300 km) has little rideable surf.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Beijing is inland and has no mangroves or sea coast; the nearest sea kayaking is on the Bohai coast, 150+ km away.

intertidal-walking.how: Beijing is inland with no tidal flats; the nearest intertidal areas are on the Bohai coast near Tianjin, about 150 km away.

cricket.how: Beijing Cricket Club (expat-founded) fields teams in a local league and the BCC International Cricket Sixes; matches have been played at Dulwich College in Shunyi.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Beijing GAA, a multinational Gaelic games club, trains weekly at a school sports ground in the diplomatic area (2008-era report; current status unconfirmed).

ice-skating.how: The National Speed Skating Oval (Ice Ribbon) on the Olympic Green is open to the public on 'the fastest ice' in China, and Tsinghua and Beijing Sport University rinks also admit the public.

curling.how: Beijing Sport University's ice centre has two curling lanes and the Ice Cube (National Aquatics Centre) hosted Olympic curling; public rinks such as Mencheng Lake in Mentougou have offered free curling and hockey tasters by reservation.
curling.venue: Beijing Sport University Ice Sports Center

ice-hockey.how: Beijing has multiple Olympic-standard hockey rinks, e.g. the CUPE Skating Rink, and university rinks open to the public.

bouldering.how: Let's Climb is a dedicated bouldering gym of about 400 sq m with a two-storey mezzanine bouldering area.

skateboarding.how: Beijing Fashion Sports Park in Daxing houses park skateboarding and U-pool areas, and Burning Ice Skate Park in Xicheng has about 2,000 sq m of indoor skating.

horse-riding.how: Demeanor Equestrian runs English-style riding lessons (often one-on-one, foreign coaches invited) for riders including embassy families.

kayaking.how: Kayak and paddleboard hire is available on the North Moat (Deshengmen to Andingmen) and Zhuanhe River, open 10:00-21:00 with life jackets required.

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: Stand-up paddleboards can be rented at the North Moat and Zhuanhe River starting piers (about 2 km routes each) from 10:00 to 21:00.

pickleball.how: TBX Pickleball has five outdoor courts with floodlights and trainers near Sun Park, bookable through a WeChat mini-program at roughly RMB 88-138 per court-hour.

salsa-bachata.how: Sazon Cuban Dance School Beijing runs salsa and Cuban dance classes Monday to Saturday evenings.

stand-up-comedy.how: Beijing Comedy Club hosts a free fortnightly Wednesday open mic at Hot Cat Club (five-minute sets), Giggle Bar has had a Thursday open mic, and Taps in Sanlitun hosts monthly comedy shows.
stand-up-comedy.venue: Hot Cat Club (Beijing Comedy Club open mic)

improv-comedy.how: Beijing Improv Group performs as house act at Hot Cat Club comedy nights (older listing; current schedule unconfirmed).

scuba-diving.how: Beijing Chenyuen Scuba School (PADI) has an on-site training pool and offers an Open Water course with full equipment rental; no prior experience needed.

archery.how: Jian Club in Sanlitun SOHO has 16 indoor lanes with 8-24 lb bows and free coaching for newcomers; Arrow Strike (Guomei First City) has 10 m and 18 m lanes with beginner bows.

pole-dance.how: Skyline Dance Lab in Sanlitun SOHO has eight poles and ran pole classes for all levels at RMB 150 (2015 review; current status unconfirmed).

aerial-silks-circus.how: Skyline Dance Lab in Sanlitun SOHO taught aerial silk and hoop classes at RMB 175 (2015 review; current status unconfirmed).

charcoal-life-drawing.how: UCCA Beijing (798) ran adult drawing series for all levels including a figure-drawing session (2017 members' class; current programme unconfirmed).

capoeira.how: CapoeiraBeijing ran kids' classes at East Gate Plaza with adult sessions following (2013 post; current schedule unconfirmed).

chinese-calligraphy.how: Hutong Calligraphy offers short English-language beginner calligraphy classes near Wangfujing, bookable through travel platforms.

hiking.how: Fragrant Hills Park (Xiangshan) in the Western Hills has a north route and a harder south route over Incense Burner Peak; Beijing Hikers also runs graded weekend group hikes, mostly on Great Wall sections farther out.

dragon-boat.how: Beijing International Dragon Boat Club, founded in 2001 starting with foreign expats, fields teams for domestic and international races (training venue and current schedule unconfirmed).

rugby.how: Beijing Aardvarks (founded 1999) train at a grass pitch in Chaoyang, and Beijing Devils, Beijing Ducks and Beijing Brothers are other clubs in the local rugby scene.

stargazing.how: Beijing Planetarium has two courtyard observatories with telescopes, and Tsinghua University's student astronomy society has held public observing open nights (2016 report).

tango.how: Beijing Bilingual Tango School (BJBTango) teaches Argentine tango in Chinese and English, and the Westin Beijing Chaoyang listed tango classes with an Argentine teacher (older listing).

swing-lindy-hop.how: Beijing has a Lindy Hop scene and an annual Swingtime Ball, and Beijing Ballroom Dance Club has run drop-in swing classes before Saturday parties (older listing).

taekwondo.how: Olympic-style (WTF) taekwondo clubs are described as easy to find in Beijing, and the Beijing Sport University has hosted taekwondo classes taught by a former Korean national-team member (2006 forum thread).

choir.how: The Friends of Latin America choir in Dongcheng sings in Chinese, Spanish and Portuguese for a membership fee of RMB 100 a year, and the French-linked Choral de Pekin meets weekly.

breakdancing.how: Sunshine Dance offers street dance classes and a team in Beijing (older listing); the Forbidden City Rockers are a long-running Beijing bboy crew.

fishing.how: Shangzhuang Reservoir northwest of downtown is the closest reservoir to the city and is popular for informal free angling from April to October.

freshwater-fishing.how: Shangzhuang Reservoir northwest of downtown is the closest reservoir to the city and is popular for informal free angling from April to October.

yoga.how: Drop-in and course yoga classes run at studios such as Yogi Yoga in Ritan Park, Chaoyang, with several other studios listed in the expat directory.

pilates.how: Pilates and Gyrokinesis sessions are offered at studios such as Iso Fit in Chaoyang, and Alona Pilates Studio has run mat classes since 2005.

snow-skiing.how: No outdoor ski slope lies within about 30 km of the centre; the nearest resorts are Nanshan (Miyun, roughly 62 km), Yunfoshan and Yuyang (about 60 km), with the Chongli resorts around 250 km away.

hot-spring-bathing.how: Geothermal hot spring bathing in indoor and outdoor pools is available at Longmai Hot Spring Resort in Xiaotangshan, Changping, a half-day trip from the city.

running-club.how: HeyRunning and other groups hold weekly group runs, including a free monthly 5k and regular sessions at Chaoyang Park, and a Hash House Harriers chapter runs on Sundays.

safari.how: No drive-through safari lies within about 30 km; Beijing Wildlife Park in Daxing has a self-drive safari section but is roughly 42 km from the centre, about an hour's drive.

poker.how: Beijing Poker Club organises sanctioned Texas Hold'em tournaments, but cash games are restricted and expat home games are informal; sources are dated.

mountain-biking.how: Trail riding exists in the western hills (for example Beishan trails, Changping) and group rides such as Serk's depart from the city; trail listings are on MTB Project.

hot-air-ballooning.how: A tethered hot air balloon ride (about 50 m up for ten minutes) has operated at Beijing Expo Garden in Fengtai; free-flight balloon rides are only in Yanqing, far outside the metro area.

woodworking.how: Mu Ben Mu Gong Fang is a woodworking studio in eastern Beijing where visitors build wooden objects and simple instruments.
woodworking.venue: Mu Ben Mu Gong Fang (木本木工坊)

orchestra.how: The Beijing Union Symphony Orchestra recruits musicians and the Starry Sky Orchestra is an open amateur ensemble.

acting.how: Beijing Improv runs weekly improvisational theatre workshops in English, with no full acting school confirmed.

tai-chi.how: BLCU Continuing Education College runs evening and weekend tai chi courses (24-form, Chen and Wu styles, sword) and private schools such as Black Tiger Club and Jinghua Wushu teach in Chaoyang.
tai-chi.venue: BLCU Continuing Education College Taichi training

french-language.how: The Alliance Francaise de Beijing, a non-profit French school founded in 1998 with Beijing Language and Culture University, teaches French language courses.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Private dog and cat shelters in Shunyi and Tongzhou, such as Hui's Sanctuary, run volunteer days that welcome expats; most coordination is by WeChat.

volunteering.how: Expat volunteers can join animal rescue volunteer days in Shunyi and Tongzhou and other community groups, organised mostly through WeChat.

3d-printing.how: Beijing Fablab in Zhongguancun offers 3D printing alongside CNC milling, laser processing and circuit making.

laser-cutting.how: Beijing Fablab lists laser processing and vinyl cutting among its lab capabilities.

cnc-machining.how: Beijing Fablab lists CNC milling and precision milling among its lab capabilities.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Beijing Fablab (circuit making, open to makers) and the Beijing Makerspace community (MAXPACE) support electronics tinkering; listings are dated.

parkour.how: Beijing Parkour Community and the Snow Fox Parkour Club have run indoor and outdoor training, and parks such as Ritan and Tiantan have calisthenics areas; sources date from 2009-2015.

pedal-boating.how: Pedal boats can be hired by the hour at Beihai Park and around Houhai and Qianhai lakes from mid-March, with a deposit.

massage.how: Foot and full-body massage parlours are in nearly every neighbourhood, with spa brands such as Liangzi Spa, Gin Spa and Bodhi Spa in Sanlitun.

stamp-collecting.how: The China National Post and Postage Stamp Museum in Dongcheng covers philatelic heritage, and philatelic companies and themed post offices sell commemorative stamps.
stamp-collecting.venue: China National Post and Postage Stamp Museum

public-lectures.how: Open English-language talks and book events are held at venues such as Yale Center Beijing in the IFC Building, Chaoyang.

dog-parks.how: Beijing's 2019 rules bar dog walking in city parks and require leashes, so no off-leash dog parks were found; the nearest pet activity areas are in Yanqing, about 75 km away.

amateur-radio.how: University and school clubs such as the BUPT amateur radio club (BY1BY) operate club stations, and licensed hams in the BA1/BD1/BG1 prefix area are listed under the Chinese Radio Sports Association.
